chapters.title: Chapter 101 | Grade 5 Genesis Bloodline Diamond Rice
paragraphs: The next morning, Dexter woke up before his 5:00 AM alarm.
He stared at the ceiling, debating whether to sleep for another ten minutes until the alarm rang, but he shook his head and chuckled.
’If I sleep again, even the alarm won’t be able to wake me.’
He knew himself too well; if he closed his eyes again, he wouldn’t be getting up until noon.
He stretched and yawned. ’Alright. Today is an exciting day. Lots of things to do.’
He dragged himself out of bed to start his morning routine. However, when he stepped into the bathroom to bath, he found the shower drain completely clogged.
Dexter sighed, pulling on a pair of cleaning gloves. He reached into the drain and pulled out a massive clump of hair with three different colors.
Silver, amber, and dark strands all tangled together.

His expression went completely deadpan. He obviously couldn’t tell the girls not to wash their hair, but the sheer volume of it was ridiculous. He shook his head, packed the hair into a plastic bag, tied it shut, and tossed it into the waste bin.
After cleaning up the bathroom and arranging the rooms, his mind drifted back to the three Bloodline Evolution Stones resting in his storage ring.
He had forgotten about them long enough. It was time to figure out how to give them to the girls.
His eyes lit up.
He could mix the bloodline stones into the food.
As a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, he had the accumulated knowledge and culinary techniques of masters far beyond his years.
If he could extract the raw essence from the stones and infuse them into a meal, the girls would absorb the bloodlines naturally without ever knowing they had consumed a priceless treasure.
Dexter closed his eyes, sifting rapidly through the vast library of Foodsmith memories embedded in his mind.
He searched for methods of extracting essence from solid spiritual objects, cross-referencing techniques for dissolving mana-dense materials into edible form.
One method surfaced above all others.
His Emperor Void Flame.
The 9th Heavenly Flame possessed unique properties that could gently melt and strip the pure essence from a Bloodline Evolution Stone without destroying or degrading its core properties.
The extracted essence could then be seamlessly blended into a spiritual meal, binding with the ingredients on a molecular level.
’Now, that’s a solid plan.’
Dexter’s grin widened as the full plan crystallized in his mind.
He would use the Diamond Rice, combined with the Heavenly Treasures he still had in storage, and the fresh ingredients he had purchased from the market.

Together, he would formulate a perfect Grade-Five meal. A rice-based dish so refined that the bloodline essence would be completely undetectable, absorbed effortlessly by the girls’ bodies as they ate.

He had considered using the stones on himself. But a Bloodline Evolution Stone could only be used once per person. If he took one, his Ancient Flame Demon Bloodline would advance a single grade, but not game-changing.
More importantly, he only had three stones for three girls. If he took one for himself, one girl would be left out, he didn’t think it would be fair.
Dexter retrieved the three shimmering crystals from his storage ring.
Then summoned a thin, controlled thread of his Emperor Void Flame—a warm white fire flickered gently above his fingertips unlike the violent crimson of his combat flames.
With precision control of a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, he wrapped the white flames around the first stone.
The crystal began to glow.
Slowly, the outer shell of the stone liquefied, releasing a shimmering, vapor that rose into the air like distilled starlight.
Dexter guided the vapor with his mana, channeling it directly into the pot of cooking Diamond Rice.
The rice grains absorbed the essence instantly, their crystalline structures glowing faintly before returning to normal.
To the naked eye, nothing had changed. But Dexter’s Gastronomy body could sense the transformation as the bloodline essence blended perfectly with the grain.
He repeated the process with the second and third stones, infusing each one into a separate portion of the meal.
Then he added the Heavenly Treasures: thin slices of Origin Sun Fruit, crushed Star Essence threads of Millennium Blood Ginseng and various others.
The Diamond Rice absorbed everything, the grains swelling with concentrated energy.
The kitchen filled with an aroma so rich, that Dexter himself had to suppress the urge to grab a spoon and dig in.
The fragrance wassweet, savory, earthy, and faintly celestial, with a warmth that seemed to seep into the walls themselves.
By 7 o’clock, the meal was complete.
[Name: Celestial Bloodline Genesis Rice]
[Grade: 5 Arcane Meal]
[Description:

A legendary rice dish crafted from Diamond Rice and a collection of rare Heavenly Treasures, refined through the Emperor Void Flame. Every crystal-like grain contains perfectly balanced life essence, nourishing the body from the cellular level while awakening its hidden potential.]
[Effects]
• Permanently increases Physical Strength by 20%.
• Greatly enhances the body’s natural healing ability, increasing recovery speed by 300%.
• Removes accumulated toxins and impurities from the body.
• Greatly restores stamina, vitality, and mana.
[Hidden Effect]
• Randomly awakens one compatible bloodline from the sealed Bloodline Essence contained within the meal.
• If the user already possesses a bloodline, there is a chance for it to evolve instead of awakening a new one.
Over the past few days, Dexter and the girls had fallen into an unspoken morning routine.
He would cook from 5 until 7am. During that time, Lyra and Selene would wake up, go to the bathroom, brush their teeth, bathe, and freshen up on their own.
Once they were done, Dexter would go to their room to help Mira with her morning routine.
Afterward, all four of them would eat breakfast together.
This morning, Dexter had made one small adjustment. He had opened the kitchen window to ventilate the cooking smoke, but he had also closed the door connecting the kitchen to the hallway.

He knew from experience that if Lyra caught even a faint whiff of the Diamond Rice cooking, she would materialize in the kitchen like a hungry ghost, and he wouldn’t be able to finish plating the food.
So the door stayed closed. The window stayed open. And the aroma drifted outside into the morning air instead.
Dexter washed his hands at the kitchen sink, preparing to go to the girls’ room to help Mira.
He dried his hands on a towel and was about to step into the hallway when—
"BANG!"
A loud, violent crash echoed through the house.
Dexter froze.
"CRACK!"
Another one? It was followed by shattering of soemthing.
’What just happened right now?’
His body tensed and he surged forward, rushing toward the girls’ bedroom, but as he reached the hallway, he realized the sound wasn’t coming from the bedroom.
It was coming from the bathroom.
Dexter sprinted to the bathroom door and threw it open.
He was stunned by what he saw.
Mira was sitting in her wheelchair, half-naked.
Her shirt had been removed, leaving her upper body exposed but her spectral arma hovering behind her covered her exposed skin. But that wasn’t what made Dexter stunned.
It was the massive crack on the bathroom wall with chunks of plaster and tile scattered across the wet floor.
Not to mention the toilet had also been shattered, as if someone had gripped it with inhuman force and squeezed.
The shower head had been ripped clean off its mount, the metal pipe bent at an ugly angle.
Dexter stood in the doorway, stunned.

chapters.title: Chapter 102 | Please Feed Me
paragraphs: "What did you do?"
Mira’s head hung low, her hair hanging forward to cover her face as she stared at the ground ad though it was the most interesting thing in the world.
She looked like a child who had broken something expensive and was waiting for the scolding. Her spectral arms had retracted slightly, curling behind her shoulders as if trying to hide.
Dexter exhaled slowly through his nose.
He understood immediately what had happened. Mira had tried to take care of herself. She had wanted to be independent, to handle her own morning routine without needing his help.

But her control over the spectral arms was still crude. She had probably gripped the shower head too hard, yanked it off the wall, panicked, and lashed out, destroying the toilet and punching a hole through the wall in the process.
Dexter rolled his eyes then stepped into the bathroom carefully, avoiding the broken ceramic.

"Since you’re not really proficient with your mana arms yet," he said, his voice calm and even, "let me be the one to take care of you until you are. For now, don’t enter the bathroom without my permission."
He didn’t scold her but what he said seemed to have more effect.
Mira blinked her eyes.
’He didn’t complain?’
She expected more but it turned out Dexter wasn’t really mad.
However, she didn’t look up or argue. She simply sat there with her ears burning red.

Dexter turned to assess the damage. He walked to the kitchen, grabbed a wooden stool, and carried it back to the bathroom. He climbed up, retrieved the mangled shower head from the floor, and examined the broken metal pipe.
"Whoosh!"
He immediately summoned a thin thread of Emperor Void Flame, wrapping it carefully around the severed joint, fusing the pipe and shower head back together as if they had never been broken.
Satisfied, he stepped down from the stool and turned to Mira.
She was still unusually quiet.

Dexter washed her hair carefully, lathering shampoo into her scalp and rinsing it with warm water from the repaired shower. He scrubbed her shoulders, her arms, her back and her legs with a soft sponge without a single change in expression.
But one could only imagine the insane struggle coursing through his veins.
Especially since his bloodline advanced to Ancient grade, he was becoming more and more active.
Thankfully, the pain managed to keep the dragon from rising. Otherwise, Mira wouldn’t be the only embarrassed one.
He supporting her weight against his chest as he washed the rest of her body.
Throughout the entire process, Mira said nothing.
Not a single mocking word or observations. Nor even clever jabs about him being gay or something.
Dexter found it both amusing and oddly cute.
Mira always had something to say. Always. The fact that she was completely quiet meant she was genuinely embarrassed.
He dried her off with a fresh towel, patted her skin dry, and dressed her with a purple sundress covered in small white flowers.
Mira’s eyes immediately snapped open when she saw it.
She gritted her teeth and glared at him.
Dexter shrugged innocently. "What?"
Mira continued to glare, her crimson eyes narrowing to slits. Then she let out a sharp snort.
"Hmph!"
Dexter smirked and dressed her in the flower sundress, adjusting the straps over her shoulders. He brushed her damp hair until it fell neatly over her shoulders, then wheeled her out to the kitchen.
Lyra and Selene were already seated at the dining table. Lyra’s eyes were locked onto the covered pot on the stove with the focus of a predator tracking prey.
Selene sat beside her, eyes closed, her echolocation painting a perfect picture of the kitchen around her.
Dexter served the meal.
He ladled the glowing, star-flecked Diamond Rice into four bowls.
The rice looked and smelled exactly like the premium Arcane meals he had made last night.
He placed a bowl in front of Selene. Her hand reached out instinctively, finding the spoon without hesitation.
He placed three bowls in front of Lyra. She didn’t even wait for him to sit down before grabbing her spoon.
Finally, he placed a bowl in front of Mira. She looked at it, then at him, and then summoned her spectral arms.
One arm reached for the fork.
This time, her grip was noticeably steadier than the night before.
Dexter sat down with his own portion and began eating.
The four of them ate in silence.
Dexter glanced at each of the girls as they ate. He couldn’t wait to see what they would become.
The food was, as always, nothing short of extraordinary.
The moment the girls took their first bites, their eyes widened in unison.
Mira’s spoon, froze halfway to her mouth.

"How much Diamond Rice do you actually have?" she asked, her crimson eyes narrowing with suspicion. She had assumed the previous meal was a rare, one-time luxury. The fact that Dexter was serving it again meant he either had a secret supplier or an impossibly deep storage.
Dexter shrugged casually. "Why do you ask? Do you want to cook for us?"
Mira glared at him, recognizing the jab instantly. She turned her head away and resumed feeding herself, her spectral arm trembling as it guided the fork toward her lips.
But after two more bites, the overwhelming taste of the meal broke through her pride.
The Diamond Rice seemed to melt on her tongue, each grain releasing a burst of warm, savory energy that spread through her damaged meridians like sunlight through cracks in a wall.
Her spectral arm faltered, the fork hovering uselessly in the air as her concentration wavered.
She glanced at the arm and then at Dexter.
She hated herself for what she was about to say as she gritted her teeth but eventually said it.
"Please feed me," she murmured, her voice so small it was barely audible.
Dexter’s grin could have lit up the entire bungalow. "Of course, my lady."

Mira pursed her lips so tightly they turned white, a deep flush crawling up her neck. She almost regretted asking. But the aroma wafting from the bowl was simply too tantalizing that it overrode her stubborn pride.

chapters.title: Chapter 103 | Ewwwww!
paragraphs: Dexter’s grin could have lit up the entire bungalow. "Of course, my lady."

Dexter picked up her fork, scooped a portion of the glowing rice, and guided it to her lips. Mira opened her mouth without protesting, closing her eyes as the warmth spread through her body once more.
From that point on, the girls ate silently.
Each one was entirely consumed by the food before them, as if it were the most delicious thing they had ever tasted in their entire lives.
Lyra finished her three portions in under three minutes, breaking her personal record. Selene finished hers in five. Even Mira, being fed by Dexter, finished in ten.
Dexter stared at the empty bowls, his expression slightly stunned. "You girls were faster than usual today."
He shook his head in disbelief as the girls reached for their water glasses, drinking lots of water to wash down the rich meal.
’Thank you.’
The soft, melodic voice of Lyra drifted into Dexter’s mind like a gentle breeze. She was looking down at her empty bowl, her cheeks faintly pink, but her gratitude was genuine and warm.
Dexter smiled and projected a gentle thought back. ’You’re welcome.’
"Thank you," Selene muttered aloud. Her voice was barely louder than a mosquito’s whisper, but Dexter’s enhanced hearing caught every syllable clearly. He nodded at her with a soft smile.
Selene didn’t leave the table.
While Lyra and Mira eventually moved to the living room, Selene remained seated in her chair, her pale eyes closed.
But Dexter could feel her Echolocation talent was focused entirely on him.
He glanced at her curiously, wondering what she wanted.
’Does she want to hold my arm again?’
The memory of her clinging to him like a kitten on heat the previous afternoon made him smile goofily.
But right now, she didn’t say anything and was simply sitting there, as though listening to him move.
Dexter dried his hands and turned to face the living room before speaking.
"I need to go out this afternoon," he announced. "But I’ll make lunch for you girls first before I leave."
Mira who was in the living room frowned slightly.
But didnr say anything.
Lyra, however, spoke. Once she saw the text written by the ai glasses.
She looked up with her dark eyes.
’You’ve been going out too much lately,’ she projected into Dexter’s mind, her mental voice carrying a rare edge of displeasure.
Selene’s eyes snapped open as her head tilted toward Dexter, her expression unreadable.
Dexter held up a reassuring hand. "It’s just a spar. I made a bet with someone. If I win, I get rich."
Mira’s eyes flickered open. "And if you lose?"
Dexter shrugged. "I gain nothing, and I lose nothing."
Mira frowned, her brow creasing. "If you win, you gain something. If you lose, you lose nothing." She paused. "That doesn’t sound right."
Dexter didn’t elaborate. He simply smiled and turned back to the sink.
Mira didn’t press the issue. In truth, she didn’t particularly care where Dexter went or what he did.
Her mind was occupied by something she hadn’t told anyone.
Last night, her right index finger had moved and it wasn’t fake.
She had spent three years experiencing phantom sensations, false flickers of hope that her nerves were repairing, only to be crushed every time.
She didn’t plan to tell Dexter nor had she told Lyra or Selene. The Grand Cosmos Scripture and the Arcane meals were working.
Her nerves were slowly repairing themselves.
She couldn’t wait for the day she could move on her own again, but until then, she would keep this small, precious hope locked inside her heart.
Dexter was deep in thought as he dried the last plate.
The bloodline essence hidden in the Diamond Rice would begin taking effect soon. With any luck, the girls would awaken their new bloodlines before the day was over.
Dexter picked up the trash bin and headed for the front door. "I’m taking out the trash," he announced to no one in particular. "I’ll be right back."
He stepped outside into the cool morning air. The neighborhood was quiet, most residents already at work. A few birds chirped from the power lines above.
As he carried the trash bin toward the curb, his eyes caught movement across the street, opposite their house.
An elderly woman was kneeling in her front garden, carefully watering a row of colorful flowers with a battered watering can.
Dexter paused as he recognized her instantly.
It was the woman he had seen this yesterday morning.
And also the same old woman who Tessa said had bet against him returning.
He smiled wryly and raised his hand in a friendly wave.
The old woman glanced up, looked at him for exactly one second smiled and then turned back to her flowers.
Dexter rubbed his nose. "Tough crowd."
He was about to set the trash bin down by the curb when he felt something wet on his left foot. He looked down.

Foul, grayish water was dripping from the bottom of the trash bag, pooling directly on his bare left foot. The liquid had leaked from a torn hole in the trash bag inside and was now seeping on his leg.
"Ewwwww!"
Dexter recoiled violently, his face twisting in disgust. He shoved the trash bag into the bin, grabbed the garden hose from the side of the house, and turned it on full blast.
"Whooosh!"
He directed the cold water at his foot, scrubbing furiously with his other foot.
"Oh, that is disgusting. That is so disgusting—"
As he was hosing down his foot, a familiar voice drifted down from above.
"That must have been terrifying for you."
Dexter raised his head and he saw a young girl opposite him.

Tessa was sitting on top of the tall brick wall that divided his compound from hers. Her legs dangled casually over the edge, her red hair tied back with a strip of cloth, her green eyes watching him with amusement.
Dexter stared up at her, water still spraying against his foot.

sentences.text: Dexter’s grin could have lit up the entire bungalow.
"Of course, my lady."
Dexter picked up her fork, scooped a portion of the glowing rice, and guided it to her lips.
Mira opened her mouth without protesting, closing her eyes as the warmth spread through her body once more.
From that point on, the girls ate silently.
Each one was entirely consumed by the food before them, as if it were the most delicious thing they had ever tasted in their entire lives.
Lyra finished her three portions in under three minutes, breaking her personal record.
Selene finished hers in five.
Even Mira, being fed by Dexter, finished in ten.
Dexter stared at the empty bowls, his expression slightly stunned.
"You girls were faster than usual today."
He shook his head in disbelief as the girls reached for their water glasses, drinking lots of water to wash down the rich meal.
’Thank you.’
The soft, melodic voice of Lyra drifted into Dexter’s mind like a gentle breeze.
She was looking down at her empty bowl, her cheeks faintly pink, but her gratitude was genuine and warm.
Dexter smiled and projected a gentle thought back. ’You’re welcome.’
"Thank you," Selene muttered aloud.
Her voice was barely louder than a mosquito’s whisper, but Dexter’s enhanced hearing caught every syllable clearly.
He nodded at her with a soft smile.
Selene didn’t leave the table.
While Lyra and Mira eventually moved to the living room, Selene remained seated in her chair, her pale eyes closed.
But Dexter could feel her Echolocation talent was focused entirely on him.
He glanced at her curiously, wondering what she wanted.
’Does she want to hold my arm again?’
The memory of her clinging to him like a kitten on heat the previous afternoon made him smile goofily.
But right now, she didn’t say anything and was simply sitting there, as though listening to him move.
Dexter dried his hands and turned to face the living room before speaking.
"I need to go out this afternoon," he announced.
"But I’ll make lunch for you girls first before I leave."
Mira who was in the living room frowned slightly.
But didnr say anything.
Lyra, however, spoke.
Once she saw the text written by the ai glasses.
She looked up with her dark eyes.
’You’ve been going out too much lately,’ she projected into Dexter’s mind, her mental voice carrying a rare edge of displeasure.
Selene’s eyes snapped open as her head tilted toward Dexter, her expression unreadable.
Dexter held up a reassuring hand.
"It’s just a spar.
I made a bet with someone.
If I win, I get rich."
Mira’s eyes flickered open.
"And if you lose?"
Dexter shrugged.
"I gain nothing, and I lose nothing."
Mira frowned, her brow creasing.
"If you win, you gain something.
If you lose, you lose nothing." She paused.
"That doesn’t sound right."
Dexter didn’t elaborate.
He simply smiled and turned back to the sink.
Mira didn’t press the issue.
In truth, she didn’t particularly care where Dexter went or what he did.
Her mind was occupied by something she hadn’t told anyone.
Last night, her right index finger had moved and it wasn’t fake.
She had spent three years experiencing phantom sensations, false flickers of hope that her nerves were repairing, only to be crushed every time.
She didn’t plan to tell Dexter nor had she told Lyra or Selene.
The Grand Cosmos Scripture and the Arcane meals were working.
Her nerves were slowly repairing themselves.
She couldn’t wait for the day she could move on her own again, but until then, she would keep this small, precious hope locked inside her heart.
Dexter was deep in thought as he dried the last plate.
The bloodline essence hidden in the Diamond Rice would begin taking effect soon.
With any luck, the girls would awaken their new bloodlines before the day was over.
Dexter picked up the trash bin and headed for the front door.
"I’m taking out the trash," he announced to no one in particular.
"I’ll be right back."
He stepped outside into the cool morning air.
The neighborhood was quiet, most residents already at work.
A few birds chirped from the power lines above.
As he carried the trash bin toward the curb, his eyes caught movement across the street, opposite their house.
An elderly woman was kneeling in her front garden, carefully watering a row of colorful flowers with a battered watering can.
Dexter paused as he recognized her instantly.
It was the woman he had seen this yesterday morning.
And also the same old woman who Tessa said had bet against him returning.
He smiled wryly and raised his hand in a friendly wave.
The old woman glanced up, looked at him for exactly one second smiled and then turned back to her flowers.
Dexter rubbed his nose.
"Tough crowd."
He was about to set the trash bin down by the curb when he felt something wet on his left foot.
He looked down.
Foul, grayish water was dripping from the bottom of the trash bag, pooling directly on his bare left foot.
The liquid had leaked from a torn hole in the trash bag inside and was now seeping on his leg.
"Ewwwww!"
Dexter recoiled violently, his face twisting in disgust.
He shoved the trash bag into the bin, grabbed the garden hose from the side of the house, and turned it on full blast.
"Whooosh!"
He directed the cold water at his foot, scrubbing furiously with his other foot.
"Oh, that is disgusting.
That is so disgusting—"
As he was hosing down his foot, a familiar voice drifted down from above.
"That must have been terrifying for you."
Dexter raised his head and he saw a young girl opposite him.
Tessa was sitting on top of the tall brick wall that divided his compound from hers.
Her legs dangled casually over the edge, her red hair tied back with a strip of cloth, her green eyes watching him with amusement.
Dexter stared up at her, water still spraying against his foot.

chapters.title: Chapter 104 | Meeting Henry!
paragraphs: Tess looked down at him with amusement in her eyes as she looked at his feet.
"That must have been disgusting..."
"Yeah," Dexter muttered flatly, still hosing down his foot. "It was."
"Good morning," Tessa said cheerfully as she smiled at him.
Dexter sighed. "Good morning."
Tessa blinked her eyes and flicked her long hair to the back.
Dexter turned off the tap and grabbed a rag from the hook on the wall, drying his leg.
"So why are you once again on my wall?" he asked, raising an eyebrow. "If you wanted to greet me, you could just come to the front gate like a normal person."
Tessa shrugged, swinging her legs. "This is more comfortable. And it’s a shortcut."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
He shook his foot a few times to flick off the remaining droplets, then looked back up at the girl perched on his wall like a gargoyle.
"Shouldn’t you be in school?"
She blinked.
"School?"
For a second she looked genuinely confused before lightly smacking her forehead.
"We’re on break."
Dexter narrowed his eyes.
Something about that answer sounded suspicious.
She looked like she was making it up on the spot.
Maybe she skipped school, but it wasn’t really any of his business.
Tessa tilted her head, her nostrils flaring slightly. Her expression shifted from amused to genuinely curious.
"Were you cooking this morning?"
Dexter paused. He knew immediately she was referring to the meal he had prepared for the girls.
The kitchen window had been open to ventilate the smoke, while the door was locked for Lyra not to smell it.
The aroma of that particular dish was potent enough to travel a considerable distance.
He thought for a moment, then nodded slowly. "Yeah. Why?"
Tessa’s eyes immediately lit up like two green fireworks. "Really? I didn’t know you were such a good cook!"
Dexter shrugged. "Well. Don’t judge a book by its cover."
Tessa smiled in excitement. "Can I have some? It smells really, really nice. Please? Can I have some? Please?"
Dexter blinked at the rapid-fire begging. He shook his head. "Not a chance. It’s all finished."
Tessa’s expression collapsed into the most devastating puppy-dog eyes Dexter had ever seen.
Her green eyes widened and her lower lip pushed out in an exaggerated pout as it trembled as though she was about to cry.
"Pretty please? Please, please, please, please, please—"
Dexter lips curled. ’How can ’please’ be pretty?’
"Fine!" Dexter held up both hands in surrender.
"Fine. All right."
He had originally left a small portion in the pot for Lyra, knowing full well that she would be hungry.
But seeing Tessa begging on his wall reminded him of the pastries he had purchased from her family’s bakery for the girls.
He had forgotten it when the girls rejected his jewelries, just remembering right now.
He could give the girls the pastries as an afternoon treat instead, and give Tessa the little bit of rice left.
It wasn’t truly a full portion, just the scraped remnants clinging to the bottom of the pot that was maybe half a plate at most.
He looked up at Tessa. "It’s only a little bit. Are you sure you’d want something so small?"

Tessa nodded vigorously, her red ponytail bouncing. "Yes! It’s just smells really good this morning through your window. I tried to respect your space, I really did, but the aroma was tooooo tempting. I had no choice but to come over. My feet just brought me here on their own."
Dexter chuckled. It sounded more like a compliment than an excuse, making his ego rise a bit.
"Alright alright. I will get it for you."
He shook his head with a faint smile and walked back inside.
He entered the kitchen, scraped the bottom of the pot carefully, and managed to gather a modest portion onto a small plate.
He covered it with a clean plate to keep the warmth in, then walked back outside.
The moment Tessa saw the plate, her eyes sparkled.
She immediately leapt off the wall, landing silently on his side of the compound as she snatched the plate from his hands with the speed of a hawk.
She lifted the upper plate, brought the plate to her nose, and inhaled deeply. Her eyes fluttered shut.
"Ah..." she sighed, her voice dripping with contentment. "It truly smells heavenly."
Then her eyes snapped open. She looked at Dexter sharply and suspiciously.
"Are you an Arcane Chef?"
Dexter’s blinked his eyes.
How had she guessed so quickly?
He shrugged, his face expressionless.
"Maybe."
Tessa’s eyes narrowed slightly, studying him as a brilliant idea popped up in her head. Her eyes twinkled mischievously.
"All right. Maybe I have a business plan for you."
Dexter blinked. "Business plan?"
Before Tessa could respond, she suddenly turned her head toward her family’s compound and cupped her hands around her mouth.
"Hey! Come meet our neighbor!"
She seem to have forgotten something but she immediately corrected herself. "D-ad! Come meet Dexter."
Dexter stared at her. "You’re talking to your dad?"
From the other side of the wall, a deep voice called back. "Tessa. Don’t just climb into another person’s compound through their fence. It’s rude and disrespectful."
Tessa rolled her eyes. Then she turned back to Dexter, her expression brightening again. "Dexter, come meet my d-ad!"
Dexter thought he might have heard some hesitation in her tone. He blinked slowly then sighed as he walked through his front gate to his neighbors place.
Halfway there, the gate on the other side swung open, and a man stepped out.
He was tall, almost exactly Dexter’s height, but broader with thick shoulders and muscular arms.
His large muscle was visible beneath the rolled sleeves of a simple baker’s apron.
He looked to be in his early forties as he smiled and extended his hand toward Dexter.
"Dexter, right? I’m Henry, Tessa’s father."
Dexter shook his hand.The grip was firm and strong.
He replied with a respectful smile. "I’m Dexter."

chapters.title: Chapter 105 | Henry And Tessa
paragraphs: The moment their hands clasped, Dexter felt it as he registered the mans strength.
Peak Superhuman Realm.
Dexter maintained his composure, but he was internally surprised.
This baker was actually a Peak Superhuman expert and he was running a bakery.
"So," Henry said, his voice deep and steady. "You’re the young man who married the three girls from the Calloway, Vance, and Frost families."
Dexter rubbed the back of his head in mild embarrassment. Seemed like everyone had associated him with the three families.
"Yes, that’s correct."
Henry’s slowly nodded his head and held Dexter’s gaze for a long moment, then released his hand.
"Good grip," he remarked mildly.
"I also heard about what happened during the monster outbreak," he said quietly. "And also about the highway incident."
Dexter’s expression remained neutral. "News travels fast."

"In this neighborhood, yes." Henry studied him for another moment. Then he nodded, seemingly arriving at some private conclusion. "If you need help, you’re welcome here anytime, Dexter. Any friend of my daughter’s is a friend of ours."
He extended his hand again. Dexter shook it.
"Thatsbwyiye nice of you. Thank you. I will take my leave now."
Henry clapped him on the shoulder.
Dexter waved goodbye. "Take care."
"You too," Henry replied, watching as Dexter turned and walked back through his front gate.
Dexter disappeared into his compound, and Henry remained standing on the sidewalk for a few long seconds.
His warm smile slowly faded as his expression hardened.
He slipped his hands into his pockets, glanced once more at Dexter’s closed gate, then turned to look at the wall where Tessa was jumping over to their side.
He didn’t say anything and simply turned then walked back into his own home.
The Wren family home was deceptively ordinary from the outside, with a few potted flowers on the front porch and fresh paint on the walls.
But the moment Henry stepped through the front door, the illusion of normalcy faltered.
The interior was almost entirely empty.
There were no paintings on the walls, no family pictures, or decorations or even bookshelves or tables.
There was just two simple wooden chairs facing a small television set in the center of a empty living room, with a single center table between them.
It was as though no one was living in the house.
Henry entered the house and saw Tessa sitting on one of the two chairs.
She was staring at the plate of rice in her hand, her fork frozen mid-air.
Henry squinted at her. "Should you be eating that?"

Tessa rolled her eyes. "Relax. If they wanted to send someone, they wouldn’t send him. F-Rank affinity, no backing, no connections. I think he’d be more worried about his wives than try troubling us."
She took another bite, chewing thoughtfully.
"Moreover, why would people from Imperius Continent plant an assassin like him? It wouldn’t make sense."

Henry gazed at Tessa, then at the food in her hand, then shook his head slowly. "We have to be careful, Tessa. I, old lady Jane and the rest are here to protect you but we can’t afford to let them ever find us."
Tessa shot her ’father’ a sharp glare. "Watch your tone. I’m blending in. That’s what we’re supposed to do, isn’t it? I’m not making any trouble."
She paused, then tilted her head with an indifferent look. "If you wanted to keep a low profile, why did you open a bakery in the first place? That doesn’t exactly scream ’invisible.’"
Henry opened his mouth. Then closed it. He had no reply for that.
"Just be careful, my lady." he said quietly after a long silence. "Until you finish awakening your bloodline, there’s nothing much you can do to protect yourself if something goes wrong."
Tessa pouted, her cheeks puffing out like an angry chipmunk. "You’re annoying."
She snatched the plate off the table, stomped toward her room, and kicked the door shut behind her with a bang sound.
Henry stood alone in the empty living room, staring at the closed door. He let out a slow, heavy breath and rubbed his temples with calloused fingers.
But his eyes suddenly flashed as he checked his arms. His skin suddenly trembled as draconic scales ripped out of his skin and then retracted back.
"It’s almost time."
Back in his bungalow, Dexter prepared for the afternoon sparring session.
The training facility where the bet would take place was located deeper in the city and a considerable distance from the outer district.
He needed to leave soon if he wanted to arrive on time.
The girls were still meditating.
Lyra was on the couch, her eyes closed.
Mira was at the window, cultivating in silence. Selene was in the bedroom, equally absorbed.
Dexter moved quietly through the kitchen. He pulled the pastries he had bought from Tessa out of the microwave and considered where to put them.
He knew that if he placed them in front of Lyra, she would devour them in seconds, regardless of whether she had just eaten a full meal.
Instead, he decided to text her later in the afternoon when she got hungry. That way, the pastries would serve their intended purpose as a snack rather than an extension of breakfast.
He heated the pastries briefly with his Emperor Void Flame.
The white flames infused the dough with a subtle warmth that would never fade, even after a full day, the pastries would remain perfectly hot and fresh, as if they had just come out of the oven.
It was one of the many convenient side effects of cooking with a Heavenly Flame.
He did the same with the lunch he had prepared.
Even though he had used ordinary market ingredients rather than Heavenly Treasures, the meal had still condensed into a Grade-One Arcane dish.
His Great Grandmaster Foodsmith skills had become so refined that even basic ingredients, when combined with his mana and flame, produced meals with tangible restorative properties.
He packed the lunch into covered containers and set them on the counter where the girls could easily find them.
Cleaned himself up, took care of Mira without her permission and then spoke to the girls.
"I’m heading out for the sparring session," he announced.
Lyra opened one eye, looked at him, and simply nodded before closing it again. A moment later, her soft, melodic voice echoed in his mind.
’Good Luck!’

The worker extended the clipboard and a pen. "Sign here, please."
Dexter scribbled his signature and stepped aside, gesturing them in.
Originally, he had only ordered two beds. But at the last minute before placing the order, he had changed his mind.
Instead of two, he had purchased four, one for each of the girls.
The expense had drained nearly all his money but Dexter was expecting payment from the Hero Association so he wasn’t quite worried.
More importantly, every investment he made in his wives would return a hundredfold through the system.
So it was a win-win situation.
Dexter guided the workers through the hallway.
First, he directed them to the girls’ bedroom.
"You remove the original beds and the three new ones here side by side."
Then he led them to his own small room for the fourth.
The workers nodded and got to work, carrying the heavy mattress frames and bed components through the narrow hallway.
Mira, who had been cultivating silently by the living room window, furrowed her brows.
Across the room, both Lyra and Selene wore similarly troubled expressions, their brows knit in irritation.
Dexter saw this and immediately knew the noise might have been disturbing for them.
Dexter scratched the back of his head, feeling a pang of guilt for disrupting their cultivation.
He walked over to the girls and spoke in an apologetic tone.

"I’m sorry about the noise. I just wanted to make your sleeping arrangements more comfortable. You girls have been sharing two merged beds, and I know that can’t be good for your backs. With these new beds, everything should be properly set up, and you’ll be able to rest comfortably.
Mira’s eyes snapped open. "We never complained."
Dexter shook his head slowly. "You never needed to. I just can’t bear you three being uncomfortable when it’s within my power to change it."
The moment those words left his mouth, the room immediately went still.
[Mira + 3 Affection]
[Lyra + 7 Affection]
[Selene + 10 Affection]
Mira’s lips twitched and her crimson eyes flickered with warmth.
She immediately closed her eyes, lowered her head, and snorted softly, pretending to concentrate on her cultivation.
But the faint pink tinge creeping up her neck betrayed her.
Lyra’s eyes had snapped open as well.
The families that had married them off had treated them as burdens. The world had treated them as broken relics.
But Dexter... Dexter kept on trying his utmost to make them comfortable.
No matter his intentions, he was obviously doing this from his heart.
’Thank you,’Lyra’s soft voice echoed in Dexter’s mind.
Dexter smiled. ’You’re welcome.’
Selene hadn’t moved. Her pale eyes remained closed, and her face expressionless.
But inside, the cracks around her frosted heart continued to increase.
Dexter smiled faintly.
"They just need about thirty to forty minutes to finish setting everything up. I’m sorry for the inconvenience and the noise."
The girls nodded.
Before returning to supervise the workers,
Dexter glanced at Mira’s neck. The Type-5 Protective Amulet rested against her collarbone making him sigh in relief.
He had temporarily lowered the Type-5 House Protection Barrier so the delivery workers could enter the property. That meant, for the next forty minutes, the house was theoretically vulnerable.
But the Protective Amulet on Mira’s neck was more than capable of shielding all three girls if someone managed to slip past the lowered barrier.
And Dexter himself remained on high alert.
If anyone so much as twitched in the wrong direction, he would know.
35 minutes later, the workers were done.
Three fluffy, queen-sized beds now occupied the girls’ bedroom, each fitted with fresh sheets, thick comforters, and soft pillows.
The fourth bed, a similarly plush mattress sat in Dexter’s small room.
Dexter touched and admired his new bed. The mattress was incredibly soft, with cloud-like surface that seemed to swallow you whole the moment you lay down.
"So nice!"
He couldn’t help but smile.
Then he quickly cleared his throat and straightened his posture.
’A man shouldn’t behave like a woman, giggling over a fluffy bed.’
Hw quickly stood up and chided himself. He should have bought a harder, firmer mattress for himself. Something masculine.
But the bed was just so... fluffy.
After the workers left, he walked back to the living room.
"You can go in and check the beds now," he told the girls. "If you want to rest or close your eyes for a bit, the room is ready."
All three nodded.
But none of them moved.
They remained exactly where they were.
Dexter shrugged. Patience was part of the process.
After settling the remaining logistics around the house, he turned to the girls.
"I’m heading to the city for the spar," he announced.
’Good luck,’Lyra’s voice echoed in his mind immediately.
"Good luck," Selene murmured softly.
Dexter smiled. "Thank you."
Mira, as usual, said nothing.
Dexter opened the front door, stepped out, and pulled it shut behind him.
"I’ll be back soon," he called through the closed door.
Inside the silent living room, Mira frowned at the closed door as Dexter’s footsteps faded down the street.
Lyra caught sight of Mira’s worried expression and smiled.
’If you’re worried about him, why didn’t you tell him not to go?’ Her voice echoed gently in Mira’s mind.
Mira’s head snapped toward Lyra, her crimson eyes narrowing.
But her face quickly hardened into her usual mask of cold indifference.
"He’s a man," Mira said flatly, "Of course he’ll do whatever he wants regardless of what anyone says."
’He’s also your husband,’ Lyra’s voice teased, the mental tone laced with a playful, almost mischievous edge. ’He would listen to you if you told him to stay.’

chapters.title: Chapter 107 | Simon & The Strange Sister
paragraphs: "He's also your husband," Lyra's voice teased, the mental tone laced with a playful, mischievous edge. 'He would listen to you if you told him to stay.'
Mira's eyes narrowed sharply as she glared at the seemingly tranquil Lyra on the couch.
She opened her mouth to retort, but found she had no immediate comeback.

Lyra's lips curled into a faint, knowing smile. Her dark eyes remained closed, but beneath that calm exterior, a spark of her old self, the rumored "Shadow Saintess" with two faces, was starting to reveal itself.
There was a certain 'madness' in her quiet amusement, a subtle shift from the broken, withdrawn girl she had been just days ago.
Mira scoffed, turned her head away, and forcefully closed her eyes, plunging herself back into cultivation to escape the telepath's teasing.
Meanwhile, Dexter had booked a taxi heading deeper into the city. He settled into the back seat and gave the driver the name of the district.
A few minutes later, the taxi slowed down as two more passengers hailed it from the curb.
The car stopped, and a young man and a young woman climbed in. The woman took the front passenger seat, while the young man squeezed into the back beside Dexter.
As the taxi pulled back onto the road, Dexter frowned slightly. His enhanced senses automatically scanned the new arrivals.
'Superhuman Realm.'
The man beside him was at the Second or Third Stage of the Superhuman Realm.
The woman in the front seat was even stronge, radiating the unmistakable pressure of a Peak Superhuman.
'When did Superhuman experts become so much?'
Dexter was genuinely surprised.
Ever since he had entered the Superhuman Realm himself, he was realizing just how many powerful experts hid in plain sight in this city.
To find two of them sharing a random public taxi was quite a coincidence.
The car drove in silence for a while before the woman in the front turned her head slightly, addressing the young man in the back.
"Are you prepared for the tournament?" she asked in a cold voice.
The young man straightened his posture. "Yes, sister. I am prepared."
The woman snorted. "That's what you said last time before you lost to Colin. Just make sure not to lose this time. Don't lose our family's face again."
The young man scratched his head, looking a bit sheepish, but then his gaze hardened. "Don't worry, sister. I'll try my best."

The woman's expression darkened. "Try your best? You best isn't enough. Try your hardest. If you lose this time, it's not just about losing face. Our parents will be disappointed. And more importantly, I will be disappointed in you.
Dexter tuned out the rest of their conversation, turning his gaze to the city skyline rolling past the window.
'Tournament?'
He hadn't heard anything about a tournament happening in the city, but it wasn't really his concern.
About five minutes later, the young man suddenly turned to face Dexter.
"This weather is quite nice, isn't it?" the young man asked with a bright, friendly tone.
Dexter didn't respond immediately. He glanced to his side, realizing the young man who looked to be about his own age was trying to make small talk.
"Yeah," Dexter replied neutrally. "It is."
The young man smiled, extending his hand. "Hi, my name is Simon."
Dexter looked at the outstretched hand, then at the young man's face.
Simon was wearing a wide, somewhat foolish grin, his eyes bright with a naive, harmless energy.
Dexter blinked, then eventually took the hand and shook it.
"I'm Dexter."
"Dexter," Simon repeated, his smile widening.
"That's quite a unique name."
Dexter shrugged. "My parents were jokesters."
Simon chuckled at the rhyme. "Are you heading to the Titan Training Center too?"
Dexter nodded. "Yeah. I assume you're going there too?"
"Yeah! There's a city-wide tournament being hosted there today," Simon explained enthusiastically. "I'm trying to win the tournament and gain some reputation in the city."
Dexter blinked. "Alright. Good luck with that."
"Are you also going for the tournament?" Simon asked, leaning in slightly.
Dexter shook his head. "No, I'm just going there for a friendly spar with someone."
"Oh, alright!" Simon said cheerfully, not pressing for details. "I hope you win your spar."
Dexter offered a small nod. "I hope you win your tournament too."
Simon beamed.
Ten minutes later, the taxi pulled to a stop in front of a massive, building.
The building was enormous, with reinforced walls as a large, metallic archway loomed over the entrance.
'Titan Elite Training Facility'
The three of them stepped out of the taxi and approached the main gate.
Simon and his sister produced their Hero Identification cards, which the guards scanned.
"Go in."
The guards spoke.
The two people headed inside the gate.
The moment Dexter was out of earshot, Simon's sister grabbed her brother by the arm and yanked him to the side.
"Simon, why are you being friendly with everyone?" she hissed. "You don't know his intentions! He might be trying to get close to our family, or to me, through you."
Simon shook his head, his expression baffled. "We entered the vehicle before us. He was already sitting in the back when we hailed it. How would he have known we were going to be in the same taxi?"
"Moreover, how could he know exactly where your car would break down? How could he know we would be hailing this exact taxi? Sister, you're being way too paranoid."
The sister shook her head.

His sister's lips curled into a thin, disapproving line. "And you're being way too carefree. It's better to be paranoid than to be taken advantage of. You can greet him or talk to him, but don't get too close."
Simon sighed but eventually nodded in reluctant agreement.

As they finished their conversation and approached the gate, they caught the tail end of Dexter's interaction with the guard. Dexter casually pulled out a sleek, golden identification card and handed it over.
The guard's demeanor transformed instantly. He snapped to attention, saluting sharply.
"Good morning, Mr. Dexter! You can head inside immediately."
Simon and his sister froze in their tracks.
A gold license card. That was the highest tier of identification issued by the Hero Association.
It meant the holder was a Gold-rank registered hero, a status reserved for those whose evaluated potential placed them in the top ten of the entire city.
But Dexter didn't wait for them to react.
He simply pocketed his card, nodded to the guard, and strode through the gate, heading directly toward the location he had been given for his sparring session.
"Why would I bother getting close to you? Don't tell me you're the Storm Empress."
Dexter's lips curled into a mocking smile when his enhanced hearing overheard Simon and his sisters conversation.

chapters.title: Chapter 108 | Don’t Hold Back
paragraphs: Dexter arrived before a massive twenty-story building.
While it wasn’t the tallest structure he had ever seen, it was incredibly wide, stretching across the landscape.
There were dozens of entrances, sliding glass doors as people went in and came out of it.
He stopped at the main entrance and looked around. The violet haired girl had told him she would meet him here.
He scanned the crowds of heroes coming and going, but didn’t see her.
Then, he heard his name.
"Dexter."
The voice was soft like a whisper, yet it reached his ears with perfect clarity. He turned around.
Lexa was standing two hundred meters away across the busy place.
Before Dexter could even raise an eyebrow, she took a single step forward.
In the blink of an eye, the two-hundred-meter distance vanished. She blurred through the crowd without disturbing a single person, reappearing just five meters away from him.
She then slowed her pace, walking the remaining distance at a casual, unhurried stroll.
"Let’s go in," she said simply, stepping past him.
Dexter blinked. He had almost forgotten he was dealing with an Ultra-rank expert.
To someone at that level, crossing two hundred meters was no different from taking a single step. They could appear anywhere their eyes could see in an instant.
As she walked past him, Dexter noticed something else. She wasn’t wearing her dark cloak today.
Instead, she was dressed in a fashionable crop top and fitted jeans, her violet hair pulled back into a neat, stylish ponytail.
She looked like she was heading out for a casual afternoon of shopping or attending a fashion show, not preparing for a soaring session at all.
Dexter stared at her back for a second, then blinked.
It was painfully obvious she didn’t take their upcoming spar seriously.
The violet-eyed girl smiled faintly as they entered the building together.
Inside, the main hall was enormous. There were tens of receptionists stationed behind a massive, curved counter, efficiently handling a constant stream of heroes booking training facilities.
Lexa walked up to a receptionist whose station had just opened up.
"We want to book a sparring arena," she said.
The receptionist, a polite young woman, smiled and nodded. "Yes, we have several available. Which tier would you like to book? We have Ordinary, Standard, Deluxe, Premium, or the Presidential suite."
"Deluxe will be okay," Lexa responded casually.
The clerk nodded and typed on her terminal. "Alright, that will be $5,000 per hour. Please scan your card to pay here."
Lexa pulled out her phone and scanned the QR code on the counter. The payment of $5,000 went through in an instant.
The clerk produced a sleek, black access pass and handed it over. "Here is the pass to Arena 512. You can find it in the Deluxe section down the east corridor. Good luck."
Lexa took the pass and started walking. Dexter followed closely behind.
They moved past the Ordinary and Standard sections. The building’s interior was designed like a massive indoor sports complex.
Through reinforced glass walls, Dexter could see various open arenas, much like indoor boxing rings where heroes were already sparring with each other.
The sounds of clashing weapons, explosive impacts, and cheering spectators echoed through the vast halls.
They continued walking until they crossed the threshold into the Deluxe section, where the atmosphere grew noticeably quieter.
They reached the door markedArena 512.
She tapped the key card against the scanner, and the heavy steel doors slid open with a soft hiss revealing the room to them.
’Damn!’
Dexter was stunned as he entered the room.
The room beyond was enormous. The entire chamber was an arena in itself, built for serious combat.

The walls were forged from graded reinforced pure steel, designed to absorb and dissipate the shockwaves of high-level battles so that combatants could go all out without damaging the surroundings or alerting the outside world.
Along one wall, a row of advanced measuring equipment was mounted.
It could record and track impact force, reaction speed, mana output, and a dozen other combat metrics.
Adjacent to those, a collection of gymming and running equipment lined the far corner.
Dexter’s eyes lingered on a set of dumbbells resting on a reinforced rack.
The smallest one was labeled 5,000 kg. The next was 10,000 kg. The largest read 200,000 kg.
He wasn’t particularly surprised. Superhuman-level heroes reached these levels of physical strength as a baseline.
Dexter himself wasn’t certain of his exact lifting limit, but he knew with certainty that it exceeded 15,000 kilograms by a comfortable margin.
Beyond the combat area was a private bathroom occupied one side, complete with a shower and changing area.
In the opposite corner, a relaxation zone with leather sofa, wall-mounted television, a mini fridge, and a fully stocked minibar.
"This is actually nice," he murmured, rolling his shoulders.
This was a place where he could go all out.
Every technique, every ability, every ounce of his strength could be unleashed here without restraint.
He could polish his combat skills, refine his patterns, and push himself to his absolute limits without holding back.
No wonder heroes flocked to these facilities.
As Dexter was still taking in the room, the violet-eyed girl dropped her bag near the wall and walked to the center of the arena, then turned to face him.
She tilted her head slightly, her ponytail swaying with the motion as she asked.
"Are you ready?"
Dexter turned toward her.
He glanced at her crop top, her jeans and the nice boots she was wearing.
"Aren’t you going to change or something?"
The girl smirked. "There’s no need for that, It will be over in less than 3 moves."
Dexter stared at her.
’Actually calling me weak?’
He shook his head slowly, then walked to the center of the arena to face her.
The girl closed her eyes as the mana radiating from her body began to shift and compress.
Layer by layer, her energy diminished, compressing inward like a collapsing star until it stabilized at a far more manageable level.
Superhuman Realm, Third Stage.
She opened her violet eyes. "Done. Are you ready?"

sentences.text: Dexter arrived before a massive twenty-story building.
While it wasn’t the tallest structure he had ever seen, it was incredibly wide, stretching across the landscape.
There were dozens of entrances, sliding glass doors as people went in and came out of it.
He stopped at the main entrance and looked around.
The violet haired girl had told him she would meet him here.
He scanned the crowds of heroes coming and going, but didn’t see her.
Then, he heard his name.
"Dexter."
The voice was soft like a whisper, yet it reached his ears with perfect clarity.
He turned around.
Lexa was standing two hundred meters away across the busy place.
Before Dexter could even raise an eyebrow, she took a single step forward.
In the blink of an eye, the two-hundred-meter distance vanished.
She blurred through the crowd without disturbing a single person, reappearing just five meters away from him.
She then slowed her pace, walking the remaining distance at a casual, unhurried stroll.
"Let’s go in," she said simply, stepping past him.
Dexter blinked.
He had almost forgotten he was dealing with an Ultra-rank expert.
To someone at that level, crossing two hundred meters was no different from taking a single step.
They could appear anywhere their eyes could see in an instant.
As she walked past him, Dexter noticed something else.
She wasn’t wearing her dark cloak today.
Instead, she was dressed in a fashionable crop top and fitted jeans, her violet hair pulled back into a neat, stylish ponytail.
She looked like she was heading out for a casual afternoon of shopping or attending a fashion show, not preparing for a soaring session at all.
Dexter stared at her back for a second, then blinked.
It was painfully obvious she didn’t take their upcoming spar seriously.
The violet-eyed girl smiled faintly as they entered the building together.
Inside, the main hall was enormous.
There were tens of receptionists stationed behind a massive, curved counter, efficiently handling a constant stream of heroes booking training facilities.
Lexa walked up to a receptionist whose station had just opened up.
"We want to book a sparring arena," she said.
The receptionist, a polite young woman, smiled and nodded.
"Yes, we have several available.
Which tier would you like to book?
We have Ordinary, Standard, Deluxe, Premium, or the Presidential suite."
"Deluxe will be okay," Lexa responded casually.
The clerk nodded and typed on her terminal.
"Alright, that will be $5,000 per hour.
Please scan your card to pay here."
Lexa pulled out her phone and scanned the QR code on the counter.
The payment of $5,000 went through in an instant.
The clerk produced a sleek, black access pass and handed it over.
"Here is the pass to Arena 512.
You can find it in the Deluxe section down the east corridor.
Good luck."
Lexa took the pass and started walking.
Dexter followed closely behind.
They moved past the Ordinary and Standard sections.
The building’s interior was designed like a massive indoor sports complex.
Through reinforced glass walls, Dexter could see various open arenas, much like indoor boxing rings where heroes were already sparring with each other.
The sounds of clashing weapons, explosive impacts, and cheering spectators echoed through the vast halls.
They continued walking until they crossed the threshold into the Deluxe section, where the atmosphere grew noticeably quieter.
They reached the door markedArena 512.
She tapped the key card against the scanner, and the heavy steel doors slid open with a soft hiss revealing the room to them.
’Damn!’
Dexter was stunned as he entered the room.
The room beyond was enormous.
The entire chamber was an arena in itself, built for serious combat.

The walls were forged from graded reinforced pure steel, designed to absorb and dissipate the shockwaves of high-level battles so that combatants could go all out without damaging the surroundings or alerting the outside world.
Along one wall, a row of advanced measuring equipment was mounted.
It could record and track impact force, reaction speed, mana output, and a dozen other combat metrics.
Adjacent to those, a collection of gymming and running equipment lined the far corner.
Dexter’s eyes lingered on a set of dumbbells resting on a reinforced rack.
The smallest one was labeled 5,000 kg.
The next was 10,000 kg.
The largest read 200,000 kg.
He wasn’t particularly surprised.
Superhuman-level heroes reached these levels of physical strength as a baseline.
Dexter himself wasn’t certain of his exact lifting limit, but he knew with certainty that it exceeded 15,000 kilograms by a comfortable margin.
Beyond the combat area was a private bathroom occupied one side, complete with a shower and changing area.
In the opposite corner, a relaxation zone with leather sofa, wall-mounted television, a mini fridge, and a fully stocked minibar.
"This is actually nice," he murmured, rolling his shoulders.
This was a place where he could go all out.
Every technique, every ability, every ounce of his strength could be unleashed here without restraint.
He could polish his combat skills, refine his patterns, and push himself to his absolute limits without holding back.
No wonder heroes flocked to these facilities.
As Dexter was still taking in the room, the violet-eyed girl dropped her bag near the wall and walked to the center of the arena, then turned to face him.
She tilted her head slightly, her ponytail swaying with the motion as she asked.
"Are you ready?"
Dexter turned toward her.
He glanced at her crop top, her jeans and the nice boots she was wearing.
"Aren’t you going to change or something?"
The girl smirked.
"There’s no need for that, It will be over in less than 3 moves."
Dexter stared at her.
’Actually calling me weak?’
He shook his head slowly, then walked to the center of the arena to face her.
The girl closed her eyes as the mana radiating from her body began to shift and compress.
Layer by layer, her energy diminished, compressing inward like a collapsing star until it stabilized at a far more manageable level.
Superhuman Realm, Third Stage.
She opened her violet eyes.
"Done.
Are you ready?"

chapters.title: Chapter 109 | Draconic Might!
paragraphs: Dexter blinked in surprise.
She was actually able to precisely control her energy, suppressing her cultivation from Ultra-rank all the way down to a third level of the Superhuman Realm.
Dexter nodded. "All right. I’m ready."
The girl’s expression turned serious as she said with indifference.
"I would advise you to take this seriously, because I will. This will determine whether you have the strength to keep the key."
Dexter frowned. "I thought we talked about this. I’m not giving you the key."
The girl smiled coldy.
"When did the weak have the rights to give orders?"
A chuckle rang out from her mouth. "If you were the same strength as I am, I would have left it with you willingly. But you’re simply too weak for your opinion to matter."
She paused, letting the words sink in.
"Taking the key from you is as easy as snatching lollipop from a baby. Instead, I decided to amuse my self with this duel. Let’s see whether you have the strength to keep it."
Dexter’s expression hardened.
He had been treating this spar as a friendly exchange, a chance to test his abilities against a stronger opponent.
But she was actually threatening to snatch the key by force if he couldn’t stop her.
His gaze turned cold.
"Since you’ve reduced your strength," he said, his voice turned flat and dangerous, "I hope you don’t hold back. Because I won’t either."
The girl’s lips curled upward. "Good."
"Can I know the name of the person I’m going to defeat?" Dexter asked.
The girl’s smile widened.
"My name is Violette."
The instant the last syllable left her lips, she blurred.
"BOOM!"
The air around the place she had been staying previously suddenly exploded by the sheer amount of speed.

One moment she was standing twenty meters away. The next, she was directly in front of Dexter as her fist shrieked through the air, punching directly at Dexter’s chest with all the strength of a level 3 Superhuman expert!
Her fist moved with the speed of a bullet train as it slammed into him Like a sledge hammer.
"BOOM!"
A massive explosion erupted from the point of impact as shockwaves blasted outward in every direction, the force of her movement catching up with her in a devastating secondary detonation.
The steel walls trembled slightly as the shockwave from the punch slammed into it.
However, despite all of these impressive feat, Dexter didn’t move a single muscle.
He stood exactly where he had been, hands in his pockets as Violett’s fist collided against with chest.
His body had absorbed the full force of the blow and transferred it straight down through his legs into the ground beneath him.
Violette’s eyes widened in shock as she stared at Dexter.
It felt as though she had punched a punched a mountain instead of a human being!
The impact had traveled back up her own arm, vibrating through her bones, making her uncomfortable.
Dexter indifferently looked down at the fist still pressed against his chest, then he raised his gaze to Violette’s face.
"Is that it?" he asked indifferently.
Violette’s face changed drastically. She flashed backward in an instant, putting five meters of distance between them in a snap.
Violett’s expression turned extremely serious as she started at Dexter as though she was seeing him for the first time.
Her brow furrowed deeply.
*What the hell was that?*
What kind of Third Stage Superhuman had a body this dense?
She couldn’t believe Dexter’s body was that ridiculous.
Dexter smirked.
The Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture, Demon Tempering Body and the Chaos Flame Demon Bloodline had forged his physique into something terrifying.
Dexter tilted his head, a faint, dismissive sound escaping his lips. "Do you want to try again?"
Violette’s eyes turned cold.
"You truly wish to die."
Her pride wouldn’t allow her to accept what had just happened.
"Bang!"
She vanished again, reappearing behind Dexter in a blur that would have been invisible to anyone without enhanced senses.
Her waist twisted as she unleashed a vicious kick directly at the back of his neck.
"Bang!"
The kick connected. Dexter’s neck tilted an inch but he remained standing and unmoved like a mountain!
Even at this point, he still hadn’t taken his hands out of his pockets!
It was truly insane!
Dexter slowly turned his head, the motion itself pushing Violette’s foot back, forcing her to retract the kick
He looked at her over his shoulder, his expression completely unbothered.
"I didn’t think Ultra-rank expert would be this weak."
"You—!"
Her face twisted anger and her violet eyes blazed with fury as she retreated backward, her fists clenching at her sides.
She had bragged two seconds ago she would defeat him in three moves.
Right now, she had struck twice and yet her opponent had barely moved!
As an ultra rank expert, her body should naturally be stronger than a Superhuman rank brat. Even if she surpressed her strength, there’s no way to surpress durability.
But yet, her body was actually weaker than a Third Stage Superhuman.
Someone she had told that he was too weak.
The humiliation burned through her veins like magma.
"Draconic Body!"
She growled as she activated her talent.
"ROOOOOOOOAAAR!"
Instantly, a phantom image of a golden dragon erupted from her body as it roared like a true ancient beast.
"Down!"
Violette stomped her feet as she burst forward with speed. The golden dragon behind her surged ahead of her, its massive maw opening wide as it descended upon Dexter along with Violett’s fist.
Dexter raised an eyebrow. The pressure emanating from the dragon was intense.
He couldn’t tell if it was a bloodline technique or an innate talent, because the energy waves it radiated blended seamlessly with Violette’s own mana signature.
But even after seeing this, he simply let out an indifferent snort.
"Reckless struggle."
He only took out one of his hands out of his pockets and punched out with the second fist.
"KA-BOOM!"
The explosion was deafening as a massive shockwave erupted like a thunderclap detonating inside a sealed chamber.
The steel walls groaned as they absorbed the brunt of the force as the wind trembled viciously.
Violette’s eyes widened when she saw she didn’t even manage to push Dexter an inch backward!
"Die!"
She roared in fury and punched again.
"Bang!"
Dexter matched it.
She immediately released a barrage of punches.
"Bang!" "Bang!" "Bang!"
Their fists became blurs.
Each collision sent another thunderous shockwave rippling through the arena.
The steel walls rang with each impact as the ground beneath their feet groaned and trembled.
Every punch Violette threw was equally matched by Dexter.
She struck faster even faster, her fist looking like a machine gun shooting out rapid bullets of fists.
But Dexter was no different, he matched her punches and also matched her speed!
His expression didn’t change a single bit and he didn’t move a single inch.
What does it meant to be invincible in the same realm!?
Violette suddenly flipped backwards as ash roared.
"Divine Dragon Might!"
Violette’s left eyes shone as it transformed into a pure golden eye of a dragon.
Her fingernails elongated into curved claws as her canine teeth extended into fangs.
She had activated her bloodline.
Her energy surged, her strength exploded upward, and the golden dragon coiling around her body doubled in size.
"ROOOOOOAR!"

chapters.title: Chapter 110 | Take Me Out For Lunch
paragraphs: Violette flashed suddenly vanished, reappearing behind Dexter and launched a devastating downward kick.
Dexter sidestepped effortlessly. The kick slammed into the ground.
"BOOM!"
The floor trembled violently but didn’t explode down the steel been made of special material.
Violette spun and released another kick, this time a horizontal sweep aimed at Dexter’s midsection.
"Bang!"
Dexter raised his arm and received the kick on his forearm.
"Bang!"
Dexter was actually forced to take a step backward. But it was actually just a single step!
But Dexter simply smiled.
"It’s quite impressive you manage to push me backward," he said calmly, "But in the same realm, I am invincible."
The instant the words left his mouth, his body flashed as he picked out with intense speed.
"Boom!"
The wind shrieked as his fist tore through the air as he punched directly at Violette’s chest.
In that instant, Violett’s face changed drastically and she quickly brought up her hand in x shape manner to block.
The phantom image of a dragon around her suddenly wrapped its wings around Violette to protect her.
"BOOM!" "CRACK—"
The golden barrier made of wings immediately shattered like it was made of glass as it slammed directly against Violett’s crossed arms.
"KA-BOOM!"
Her arms was forcefully pressed against her chest as her shirt exploded from the force revealing sport bra holding two massive breasts.
"Whoosh!"
Like a leaf in an hurricane, she was blasted backwards with an extreme force.
She slammed into the far steel wall with a deafening ’bang’ as she bounced back and landed on the ground.
Dexter slowly pulled his fist back, a small smile on his face. He looked across the arena at her crumpled form.
"Are you convinced?"
Violette looked up at him, panting heavily.
Her golden dragon eye still blazed. Her claws were still extended. Her chest rose up and down rapidly, and a thin line of blood traced from the corner of her lip.
Fury!
A deep surge of anger ripped through her like a hurricane.
Suddenly, a pressure wave of pressure spread out of her like head.
Her suppressed energy shattered its restraints, climbing from Third Stage Superhuman to Fourth... Fifth... Sixth... Ninth... Twelfth...
The barrier between realms cracked.
"Ultra Realm."
The moment her energy touched the Ultra Realm threshold, Dexter’s face changed.
’She’s really angry over a spar and willing to go all out?’
Dexter’s gaze hardened. He began channeling mana into his bloodline, preparing to activate Scorching Fury—
Then, just as suddenly as it had erupted, the pressure stopped.

Violette closed her eyes and ghe golden dragon pupil in her left eye retreated, the color fading back to violet. Her claws retracted, shrinking back into normal fingernails. Her fangs withdrew. The golden dragon coiling around her body dissolved into sparkling motes of light that scattered and faded.
She stood there, expressionless, staring at Dexter for a long, silent moment.
Then, without a single word, she turned, walked to the side of the arena, picked up her bag, and headed toward the restroom.
Dexter blinked.
He stared at the closed restroom door, stunned.
Then he shook his head and let out a quiet laugh.
"Like granddaughter, like grandfather," he muttered to himself.
It was exactly the same thing her grandfather had done.
When Dexter had won their bet, learning the Grand Cosmos Scripture in a single day, the old man had simply walked away without saying a word.
Now the granddaughter was doing the exact same thing. Beaten in a spar, her pride stinging, she had retreated to the washroom without uttering a single word.
Dexter shrugged. He would let her compose herself. Pride was a fragile thing, and he had just shattered hers rather thoroughly.
He looked down.
His right boot had exploded during the fight, most likely from the accumulated shockwaves of their fist exchanges.
The leather had torn apart, the sole had separated, and his sock was poking through a hole at the front of the boot.
Dexter face-palmed with his free hand.
"Seriously?"
He shook his head, kicked off the remnants of the destroyed boot, and limped slightly as he walked to the sideline to wait for Violette.

Luckily, a pair of disposable sandals sat neatly arranged on a shelf near the relaxation zone—courtesy of the training center, presumably for combatants whose footwear hadn’t survived their sparring sessions.
Dexter slipped them on. They were slightly tighter than his size, the thin rubber pressing uncomfortably against his toes, but they were infinitely better than walking barefoot through the city.
He limped back to the arena and waited.
Five minutes passed, ten. No sign of Violette.
’What’s she doing in there?’
Dexter frowned and crossed his arms, staring at the closed restroom door with impatience. He had won the spar and he wanted the money she owned him.
He had no intention of standing around all afternoon waiting for a sore loser to finish sulking in the bathroom.
He frowned and was prepared to go knock.
The restroom door clicked open.
Violette stepped out.
She had changed into a fresh outfit, a simple white blouse and dark slacks, her violet hair now loose and falling past her shoulders.
Her expression was carefully composed, the mask of cold indifference firmly back in place.
She looked at Dexter. She seemed to want to speak, but hesitated, her tongue darting out to wet her lips. Then, finally, she spoke.
"How about lunch?"
Dexter shook his head immediately. "No. I just want to get home."
Violette hissed softly through her teeth. "If you want your money, I’d suggest you come with me."
Dexter frowned, his eyes narrowing. "You’re holding the bet hostage over dinner?"
Violette shrugged, a hint of smugness returning. "You won already. The money is yours. The least you could do is fulfill one of my wishes before I hand it over."
