She had changed into a fresh outfit, a simple white blouse and dark slacks, her violet hair now loose and falling past her shoulders.
Her expression was carefully composed, the mask of cold indifference firmly back in place.
She looked at Dexter.
She seemed to want to speak, but hesitated, her tongue darting out to wet her lips.
Then, finally, she spoke.
"How about lunch?"
Dexter shook his head immediately.
"No.
I just want to get home."
Violette hissed softly through her teeth.
"If you want your money, I’d suggest you come with me."
Dexter frowned, his eyes narrowing.
"You’re holding the bet hostage over dinner?"
Violette shrugged, a hint of smugness returning.
"You won already.
The money is yours.
The least you could do is fulfill one of my wishes before I hand it over."

chapters.title: Chapter 111 | Country Bumpkin
paragraphs: Violette shrugged, a hint of her earlier smugness returning. "You won already. The money is yours. The least you could do is fulfill one of my wishes before I hand it over."
Dexter stared at her for a long while as he frowned. He thought for a bit then eventually agreed. It wouldn’t hurt to just take her to lunch and leave after.
"Alright. What restaurant?"
"I know a place close to here," Violette said, already walking toward the exit. "Let’s go."
Dexter followed her out of the Titan Training Facility entirely.
The afternoon air was warm against his skin as it reached its highest intensity.
Violette confidently led the way. Her earlier fury seemingly dissolved, or at least deeply slightly reduced.
"There’s an Arcane restaurant nearby," she said over her shoulder. "Best one in the district."
The restaurant was called House Of Daily Gourmets.
The building was incredible. They mixed traditional along with modern architecture, making it look really nice.
The entrance was framed by two enormous stone lions, their eyes set with tiny mana gems that flickered with ambient light.
Despite the restaurant’s size, it was packed.
The main dining hall was filled to the brim with heroes, businessmen, wealthy civilians, and what appeared to be several minor nobles.
Waiters moved between tables with practiced grace, carrying steaming dishes that filled the air with a complex, mouthwatering aroma.
Yet despite the crowd, the restaurant was so spacious that there were still plenty of empty tables available.
Violette walked in as if she owned the place. She selected a table near the window and Dexter sat down opposite her.
A waiter appeared almost instantly. He was a young man in a black uniform with a cloth napkin draped over his forearm.
"Good evening. Welcome to House Of Daily Gourmets. Are you ready to order, or would you like a moment to review the menu?"
Violette didn’t even glance at the menu. "I’ll have the Grade Two Stamina Recovery Set. Dragon-Tail Steak with Moon-Herb Sauce."
The waiter nodded and turned to Dexter, presenting a leather-bound menu with a subtle bow.
Dexter opened it.
His eyes nearly popped out of his skull.
The menu was organized by grade.
Grade One meals occupied the first page, with prices ranging from 3,000 to 8,000 dollars per plate.

Grade Two meals started on the second page, with prices between 12,000 and 50,000 dollars. Grade Three meals which was the highest the restaurant offered actually began at 80,000 dollars and climbed to a staggering 150,000.
Dexter stared at the numbers.

A Grade Two meal, similar in quality to the simple rice dishes he casually cooked for his wives every morning, cost 12,000 dollars per plate here. And that was the cheap end. The higher-end Grade Two dishes ran up to 50,000.
’What the hell!’
The simple meals he cooked at home were Grade One at minimum, even with ordinary ingredients.
With Diamond Rice and Heavenly Treasures, he was producing Grade Four meals that didn’t even exist on this restaurant’s menu.
If a Grade Two meal here cost 50,000 dollars per plate, what would a Grade Four meal be worth?
’What would a Grade Five meal be worth?’
The numbers went through his mind like he was a number calculator.
One could even see dollars sigh in his eyes!

If he opened a restaurant, serving even Grade Two or Grade Three meals to the public, he could generate astronomical income. Tens of thousands of dollars per plate. Hundreds of thousands per day. Millions per month.
And that was just the beginning. As a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, his capabilities far exceeded anything this restaurant could produce.

He was in a class of his own. There were only three Grandmaster Foodsmiths registered in the entire city, and none of them could reliably produce Grade Four meals. He could do it with his eyes closed.
A restaurant, his own establishment. A place where his Foodsmith skills could generate consistent, massive revenue, revenue that could be reinvested into his wives to gain 10,000 times returns!
The more he thought about it, the more excited he became. His eyes practically glowing with fire.
Across the table, Violette noticed the brightness in Dexter’s eyes.
Her lips curled upward in a small smile.
She mistook his excitement for the naive wonder of a young man experiencing fine Arcane Meal for the first time.
In her mind, she was looking at a country bumpkin who had never set foot in a restaurant this expensive.
The resentment she felt from losing to him eased slightly.
’So he’s strong,’she thought to herself, taking a sip of water.
’Strong but poor. Interesting combination.’
"You’ve never been to an Arcane restaurant before, have you?" she asked, a trace of condescension in her voice.
Dexter pondered and realized he truly hadn’t seen an arcane restaurant before. He shook his head. "No."
Violette’s internal diagnosis of "country bumpkin" was confirmed. She smiled warmly—the first genuinely warm expression she had shown him all day.
"You should try their food. It’s really quite good."
Dexter nodded absently, still mentally calculating potential restaurant revenue streams.
He selected a Grade One meal from the menu.

*Grade One Iron-boar Steak: Premium monster beef steak served with mana-infused wild rice and fire-roasted vegetables. Restores physical stamina, slightly strengthens muscle fibers, and accelerates recovery from physical exertion. Ideal for post-training consumption.*
Price: 5,000 dollars.
Dexter ordered because he wanted to taste it.
He wanted to compare a professional restaurant’s Grade One meal against his own cooking to see where he stood. To understand the gap between his Foodsmith skills and the commercial market.
The waiter collected the menus and disappeared into the kitchen.
Dexter leaned back in his chair, his eyes drifting across the restaurant.
The atmosphere was refined but not stuffy. Soft instrumental music played from hidden speakers.
The clinking of fine china and the murmur of polite conversation created a comfortable, ambient noise.
Violette sat across from him, her posture elegant, her violet eyes watching him with quiet, assessing interest.
"You handled yourself well in the arena," she said after a moment, her tone carefully neutral.
Dexter looked at her. "You don’t sound happy about it."
"I’m not," she admitted without hesitation. "I reduced my strength to Third Stage Superhuman and still lost. That shouldn’t have been possible."
"You told me not to hold back, I didn’t."
Violette’s jaw tightened slightly. "Your body... it’s not normal. No Third Stage Superhuman should be that durable. What cultivation technique are you practicing?"
Dexter smiled enigmatically. "A man should have his secrets."
Violette studied him for a long moment, then let out a soft, reluctant huff. "Fine. Keep your secrets."
The waiter returned, carrying two large, covered plates balanced expertly on one arm.

He placed the first plate in front of Violette—her Grade Two Dragon-Tail Steak, the meat glistening with a shimmering moon-herb sauce that radiated faint, silvery mana. The aroma was rich and complex, carrying hints of wild game and aromatic herbs.
Then he placed Dexter’s plate in front of him. The Grade One Iron-boat Steak Set.
The steak was thick and perfectly seared, resting on a bed of mana-infused wild rice alongside fire-roasted vegetables.
The meat had a faint, reddish glow the telltale sign of monster beast beef, which contained trace amounts of ambient mana.
The presentation was clean and professional.
Dexter blinked his eyes. ’Looks nice but I want to eat, not soak my eyes in designs.’
Dexter muttered as he saw the design on his food and the small portions given to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 112 | Mysterious Faction
paragraphs: In just ten seconds, Dexter had completely deconstructed the meal.
With the refined palate of a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, he analyzed everything about the dish.
The precise blend of herbs in the seasoning, and the method of mana infusion. He could taste every ingredient, trace every step of the cooking process, and identify every single flaw.
In just a few seconds, he recognized so many flaws.
The mana infusion method wasn't done right.
The seasoning was slightly too heavy on one side, masking the natural umami of the meat.
The fire-roasted vegetables were slightly over-charred, introducing a bitter taste that clashed with the steak's savory nature.
For an ordinary person, the meal was decent and even enjoyable. But for someone like Dexter, it was far from perfect.
'Disappointing.'
Although he was extremely disappointed by the food he was never one to waste food.
His Chaos Flame Demon bloodline and his metabolism, burned through the calories and mana with quickly. He finished the entire plate in under two minutes.
Violette stared at him, stunned by his speed of eating.
She had barely finished a quarter of her own steak and this guy had eaten all of it.
Her lips tugged slightly. 'Truly a country bumpkin.'
Dexter set down his fork and leaned back. "So," he said, meeting her violet eyes. "Are you going to tell me anything about the necklace?"
Violette's expression flickered as she pondered.
Then, instead of answering his question, she asked one of her own.
"What do you know about the powers controlling this place?"
Dexter frowned. "The powers controlling this place?"
"Do you mean the Nine main families of Stargate City?"
Violets sneered with disdain and arrogance in her tone. "What Nine main families? They are merely frogs playing house in a well. I'm talking about the three main associations?"
'Did she just compare the seven main families as frogs in the well?' Dexter's pupils constricted violently and he knew Violette status might be even more astonishing than he thought.
Dexter considered her question for a moment. "There's the Hero Association, the Geneticists Association that manufactures genetic serums, and the Federation."
Violette raised an eyebrow. "Any other powers?
Dexter shook his head slowly. "I know there are likely other powers operating behind the scenes, but I've never heard of them."

Violette nodded again. "There's a reason you've never heard of them. The Hero Association is the strongest, having the support of the federation, and they make sure the news about other associations is suppressed."
Dexter's frown deepened. "So what does that have to do with the necklace?"
Violette grinned darkly.
"The necklace is a sort of key," she said quietly.
"The key is only given to the successor of one of those hidden factions you're taking about. If you wear the necklace, you automatically become the next generation leader of a hidden faction."
Dexter's face changed.
'Leader?'
Becoming the next-generation leader of a hidden faction? How was that possible?
Had that old man actually given him the key to leading a mysterious organization just because he had won a bet about learning a cultivation technique?
Not to mention that it was a mysterious faction, if he was caught, the Hero Association would definitely not let him off.
Violette smirked, watching the realization dawn on his face. "So now, do you know how much trouble you're in?"
"If word gets out, not only would you be hunted by opposite factions, but by the Hero Association also."
She suddenly leaned forward slightly. "Why don't you give me the necklace? And just like that—"
"Snap!"
"Your trouble disappears. Simple."
Dexter blinked and for a brief moment, he truly considered giving her the necklace right there.
Afterall he still had to take care of three wives. And now, he somehow became the next generation leader of some mysterious organization?
He could bare take care of his girls and himself. If his identity was revealed, he would place the girls in danger. They were his investments afterall.
But then, another thought came to his head.
What if she was lying?
He had only ever heard of the Hero Association, the Geneticists Association, and the government.

Those were the acknowledged powers of the continent. The idea that there were other, hidden factions was plausible, but the notion that he would casually meet an old man, win a bet, and receive a token of leadership for one of these secret organizations?
It was simply too absurd.
And if there was one thing Dexter had learned from living with Mira, it was how to recognize when someone was trying to be manipulative.
His gaze focused as he sneered at Violette. "I know your tricks. And I won't fall for them."
Violette stared at him, genuinely stunned.
Then, slowly, she smirked. She didn't try to correct him not did she argue. She simply let his dismissal stand as a knowing amusement danced in her violet eyes.
"Alright. I won't say much regarding this matter any longer."
"What academy are you attending?" she asked suddenly, shifting topics entirely. "What university?"
Dexter frowned. "University? Why would I need to go to a university?"
Violette's brow creased. "Are you not planning anything for your future?"
Dexter shrugged. "I'm not planning to attend any university."
Violette appeared even more stunned than before. She opened her mouth, then closed it.
Her frown deepened into something approaching genuine concern.
"If you're not planning to attend an Ultra University," she said slowly, "then the key would be useless to you anyway. You should really hand it over to me."
Dexter's ears pricked up. "Ultra University? What's that?"
Violette hesitated as she studied his face, searching for any sign that he was joking.
When she found none, her expression shifted changed into something between disbelief and pity.
She opened her mouth to speak, but then closed it. A faint, cryptic smile replaced her frown.
"The key would eventually..." She paused, shaking her head. "I have no idea why Grandfather gave you the key instead of giving me. But I'm pretty sure you will regret his choice very soon."
Her face lightened up as she smiled making her face look even prettier. She had a smile that could actually dim the surroding noise as she smiled at him.
But Dexter's brows were scrunched up into a frown instead.
Violette let out a quite giggle and offhandedly raised her hand and called the waiter.

chapters.title: Chapter 113 | Mister Wayne, Young Leader Michael
paragraphs: Dexter remained frowning as Violette called the waiter and started the process of payment.
’Ultra University.’
He had never heard of such a thing. He had heard of Hero University, of course.
He had finished secondary school but never attended one. Hero Universities were for the wealthy.
Dexter didn’t need a certificate as his path became clear when he got the system.
Become a licensed hunter, raid dungeons, use the Slaughter Extraction System to grow stronger with every kill, earn money, and spoil his wives, making them grow even stronger.
As for the Hero university, it was unnecessary for that route.
But an Ultra University? That classification of academy was entirely new to him.
He was intensely curious, but Violette didn’t seem to want to explain as she paid the waiter, stood up, and wanted to leave.
Before she could take a single step, a voice suddenly spoke out from behind her.
"Violette?"
The voice was masculine, wounded, confident, and was quite gruff.
A young man stepped out from between the tables.
The young man was tall and had a chiseled jaw that looked as though it had been carved from marble.
His tailored suit perfectly complemented his broad shoulders and fit body.
Every detail of his appearance was neat, from the crisp knot of his tie to the mirror-like shine of his shoes.
He looked like a model who’d just walked out of a magazine.
A charming smile spread across his face as he approached.
"Violette," he repeated, his smile widening. "I thought I recognized you from across the room. I figured my eyes were playing tricks on me, but... it’s actually you."
Dexter blinked his eyes and observed the exchange.
The moment the man appeared, Violette’s face turned indifferent.
"Wayne," she said flatly. "I’m leaving."
She moved to walk past him, but Wayne shifted effortlessly into her path. It didn’t look aggressive but natural instead.
"No, no," he said, his smile never wavering. "You can’t leave just like that. I’ve been trying to get in touch with you for the past month. Please... don’t leave on my account."
Violette’s gaze turned cold as she stared at the young man.
The young man’s attention drifted to Dexter.
A subtle frown came across his face as his eyes landed on Dexter.
Dexter was dressed plainly and ordinary, like those construction workers. His eyes drifted to his feet, and the arrogance in Wayne’s face increased.
Dexter looked ordinary. Perhaps a little handsome, but nothing that explained why someone of Violette’s standing would be dining with him in a restaurant like this.
The frown disappeared like it had never appeared in the first place as he revealed a fake smile and stretched his hand out.
"I’m Wayne," he said pleasantly. "And who are you?"
Dexter glanced at the offered hand before shifting his gaze to Violette.
She hadn’t said a word, but he caught the faint flicker in her violet eyes.
Dexter looked back at Wayne’s outstretched hand, stood up, and replied curtly.
"Hey, I’m leaving."
He gave Violette a brief nod then without a second thought, walked past Wayne without another word.

Dexter didn’t want to get tangled into whatever was happening between the two. They might be exes and might have had a relationship with each other; everything would simply be messy if he gets involved. So he decided to walk away instead.
His sandals made muffled flip-flop sounds as he exited the restaurant, and moments later, he was gone.
Wayne remained motionless, his hand still suspended awkwardly in the air.
For the briefest instant, his smile cracked, and his brown eyes turned pure red.
Wayne was an Ultra-Rank Hero.
Every superhuman hero who met him would immediately show respect without being needed to be told.
Power was respect in this world, it was simply the natural order of things.
Yet this ordinary-looking man hadn’t merely failed to show him respect.
He had dismissed him entirely.
A faint killing intent leaked out as his gaze hardened.
Then Wayne inhaled slowly.
His composure returned until his polished smile settled back into place.
Violette, seeing the exchange, chuckled lightly as she reached for her handbag.
"If there’s nothing else," she said coolly, "I’ll be leaving."
She slung the bag over her shoulder and headed for the exit.
This time Wayne didn’t block her.
Instead, he fell into step beside her, matching her pace.
"You should really get in touch with Young Leader Michael," he said casually, but there was a hidden force in his tone.
"He’s been trying to reach you. Just as I have, he has something he wants to tell you. Something he believes you might actually be willing to hear."
Violette suddenly stopped.
Around them, the restaurant carried on as normally and yet, the space between Violette and Wayne had gone deathly cold.
Then she turned.
Her violet eyes met his.
The cold within them could have frozen an ocean.

"It seems Michael has been lenient towards you. Speak to me that way and you will not just lose your tongue. And as for Young Leader Michael, tell him that if we ever choose to ally with another faction, it certainly won’t be with Blood Crown."
She stared at Wayne, whose face had drained a bit of color, then smiled.
Without waiting for a response, she turned and walked away.
Wayne stood where he was, watching her disappear through the restaurant doors.
He was still smiling but his face was slightly pale from fear. However, the fear and the fake smile vanished.
A streak of crimson veins bulged along the side of his neck, up to the edge of his eyes, before it slowly receded as pure killing intent flashed within his eyes.
His gaze instantly became savage and bloodthirsty. It was terrifying.
It lasted only a heartbeat before he managed to compose himself.
Throughout the entire exchange, another young man had stood quietly behind Wayne.
He hadn’t spoken nor had he moved a muscle to draw attention to himself.
Only after Violette disappeared completely did he finally break the silence.
"Mister Wayne..."
He hesitated.
"I don’t understand why Young Leader Michael is so determined to form an alliance with them."
Wayne slowly turned.
His gaze settled on the young man with the crushing weight of a collapsing mountain.
The temperature around them seemed to drop as if the killing intent he had suppressed moments earlier still lingered in the air.
The young man’s face instantly lost all color.
Sweat formed across his forehead as he lowered his head, his earlier curiosity evaporating without a trace.
Wayne opened his mouth and spoke in a calm but terrifying tone.
"You presume to question Young Leader Michael’s decisions?"
The young man hurriedly shook his head.
"I... I wouldn’t dare."
Wayne’s expression remained impassive.
"Then learn to keep your mouth shut."
His face slowly calmed as he continued.
"The thoughts of Young Leader Michael are beyond people like us. Simply do your job and nothing more.
"...Yes, Mister Wayne."
The young man’s head faced the ground even more, and his entire body trembled with fear and respect.
Only after the restaurant gradually returned to normal did Wayne glance once more toward the exit Violette had taken.
A faint smile that didn’t reach his eyes slowly curved across his lips.
he murmured to himself,
"You’ve really chosen your side."

chapters.title: Chapter 114 | $1,000,000
paragraphs: As he exited onto the street, he overheard several patrons talking excitedly about a tournament happening at the Titan Training Center.
He the suddenly remembered about Simon and his strange sister.
’That must be the tournament Simon had mentioned. Maybe he would win?’
To him, Simon was too kind-hearted but he also knew kindheartedness doesn’t mean he isn’t a demon in combat.

He decided against going back to watch. Instead, he hailed a taxi. The green taxi stopped and after giving his home district, the driver with accent nodded his head and then took off... just like his mom.
The taxi had been driving for about 2 minutes when Dexter’s phone buzzed.
He pulled it out and glanced at the screen.
[Credit Alert: $200,000 deposited into your account]
He stared at the notification. Violette had actually kept her promise and sent part of the money.
Before he could fully process the number, a second notification appeared.
[Credit Alert: $870,000 deposited into your account.]
Dexter’s eyes widened.
One million and seventy thousand dollars.
’I’m a freaking millionaire!’
Dexter’s mind trembled as he felt extremely giddy. He was an actual millionaire in less than a day!
A massive grin split across his face, almost reaching his ears.
It was so wide that even the taxi driver who offhandedly glanced at him through the rear mirror almost had a heart heart!
Fortunately, he had holy water in his car.
’Should be easy to tie the kid up and exorcise him.’
Dexter didn’t car what the driver thought. This was his first time having so much money. He had never in his life come into contact with such massive digits.
Except when using a calculator.
His mind immediately shifted into overdrive as he pulled up his phone’s browser and started searching.
What should he buy first? How should he spend the money? Buying a few things shouldn’t take all his money right?
He started to look on the internet what he could buy for the girls, big mistake. There was lots and lots of items on the internet.
So he settled on fashion clothing, shoes, boots, newer version wheel chair for Mira, newer phone model for Lyra and newer AI Contact Lens for Selene.
Then a thought struck him. He was in a taxi, why couldn’t he just purchase a vehicle instead of simply using a taxi. Then transporting the girls and items woukd be even easier. bulletproof SUV.
As he thought about this, he couldn’t keep the thought lying down. It’s a million dollar right? Buying a car shouldn’t take much from his money!
After pondering he decided to get a bulletproof SUV.
He was not going to repeat the highway incident where the taxi driver got sniped in the skull.
The driver who was at the front suddenly got goosebumps and he immediately made the cross sign over his chest. ’This boy might be really possessed!’
Dexter suddenly leaned forward and spoke.
"Change of plans, take me to Valerium car dealership at Raestrum District."
The driver nodded and adjusted his route.

Five minutes later, the taxi pulled up in front of a massive car dealership. The showroom floor stretched across an enormous, brightly lit space, filled with rows of gleaming vehicles of types and luxury.
Dexter stepped out of the taxi and walked inside. The moment he crossed into the building, a salesman in a tailored suit materialized at his side like he had just teleported.
"Good evening, sir! Welcome to Valerium Motors. How can I assist you today?"
Dexter smiled like therich millionairethat he was.
"I need an SUV," he said. "Preferably bulletproof. Bulletproof glass, reinforced chassis, the works."
The salesman’s eyes brightened. "Of course, sir. We have an excellent selection of armored SUVs. Right this way."
He led Dexter through the showroom to a section where several rugged, imposing vehicles were parked.
Each one was black or dark grey, with thick, reinforced doors and windows.
"This is our latest model," the salesman said, gesturing proudly at a sleek, modern SUV.

"This year’s edition. Reinforced vibranium-alloy frame, mana-infused bulletproof glass rated to withstand Superhuman-level impacts, self-sealing tires, and a built-in mana shield generator. Retail price: $350,000."
Dexter’s heart jumped. 350k just for a car? His entire fortune would be gone just by purchasing three!
Dexter pretended to observe the vehicle truly in fact, he was looking for ways to reject this vehicle and maybe can el his whole plan of buying anything at all.
But as he examined the vehicle, he noticed that it was quite beautiful. But was Modern, aggressive and really looked like a manly vehicle.
But It was too flashy.
If he drove this thing through his neighborhood, every pair of eyes on the street would track it and people would know he got into some money.
If he saw the vehicle the next morning, then that simply mean pigs could fly.
Dexter looked at the salesman and shook his head.
"This," he said. "It’s too flashy. Don’t you have old models, preferably one that is perfect to assist with someone with wheelchair?"
The salesman’s smile faltered slightly. "I’m sorry, sir? You want a reinforced car that is perfect for transporting someone in a wheelchair and make things easier?"
Dexter nodded and added. "Don’t forget not flashy either. I need something that looks ordinary on the outside but is reinforced underneath."
The salesman blinked, he recovered as he smiled professional. "I understand completely, sir. Follow me."
Dexter thought the salesman might tell him they don’t have, giving him a perfect excuse to withdraw from this purchase.
But seeing the confident expression on the young man’s face, Dexter decided to go with him.

The young man led Dexter across the showroom floor, to a quieter section at the back. Here, the vehicles were older body styles, muted colors, and ordinary in every way. Outside, they wouldn’t earn a second glance on any street.

"This is our Reliability Line," the salesman explained. "Older exterior designs, but we retrofit the internals with the same military-grade reinforcement packages as our newest models. Same protection but less attention.
Dexter’s eyes scanned the row and settled on a dark grey SUV. It looked perfectly ordinary!
The kind of vehicle you’d see in a grocery store parking lot and immediately forget.
Dexter when forward to open the door and he was surprised.
The door was easily three times heavier than a standard car door. The windows was also bulletproof and the interior was minimalist and wide too.
"What’s the spec on this one?" Dexter asked, sliding into the driver’s seat.

"Excellent choice, sir," the salesman said, brightening. "This is the Vanguard V4. Reinforced vibranium-steel alloy chassis, hidden beneath standard exterior paneling. Ballistic resistant bulletproof glass rated to withstand Peak Superhuman-level impacts. Self-sealing run-flat tires."
"Built-in mana shield generator with a six-hour sustained output. EMP-resistant electronics. And a 600-horsepower mana-hybrid engine that runs on both standard fuel and Nexus Cores."
He walked to the rear of the vehicle and pressed a button on the key fob.
The tailgate rose automatically.
Then, with a soft mechanical hum, the floor folded outward as a compact hydraulic ramp extended smoothly to the ground.

"The rear cabin has been completely reconfigured," the salesman continued. "The third-row seats have been removed to create a dedicated wheelchair bay. It features an automatic restraint system that locks the chair securely to the floor, during sudden maneuvers."
He stepped aside, allowing Dexter to look inside.
The interior was surprisingly spacious.
A wheelchair could roll straight up the ramp without needing to be lifted. Once inside, it would lock into place automatically, leaving enough room for another passenger to sit comfortably beside it.
The roof had been raised slightly to provide extra headroom, and the side doors opened nearly ninety degrees, making transfers effortless if they were ever necessary.
"Despite the modifications," the salesman added with a smile, "from the outside, it still looks like an ordinary family SUV."
It was perfect to transport Mira with the vehicle!
"So how much is it?"
The salesman smiled.
"Including the reinforcement package and accessibility conversion, the total comes to $280,000 sir."
Dexter almost went mad right there it was simply too expensive.
However, the mind was willing, but the flesh was unruly.
He ran his hand over the steering wheel. It was really really comfortable.
He looked at the salesman. "I’ll take it."
The salesman’s face lit up like a sunrise. "Fantastic, sir! If you can provide your Hero license, I’ll start the paperwork immediately."
The moment the young man saw the gold card, his face changed and what supposed to take thirty minutes was finished in ten.
Within ten minutes, Dexter had transferred the funds, signed the registration documents, and was handed a pair of keys.
He slid into the driver’s seat, adjusted the mirrors, and twisted the key.
"Vroooom!"
The way the engine purred made Dexter feel like it was totally worth it.
He pulled out of the dealership onto the city street.

chapters.title: Chapter 115 | Neuro-link Wheelchair
paragraphs: The Vanguard V4 drove really smoothly and purred when you wanted it to.
The steering was responsive, the suspension smooth, and the cabin was soundproofed too.
Dexter entered onto the highway, his mind already shifting to his next destination.

Mira’s wheelchair and then a boutique with decent clothing and maybe flowery dress for Mira. He loved them on her, owning perfectly well she doesn’t like it. Her puffed up checks when she’s angry always reminds him of a angry chipmunk with red hair.
The standard hospital-issue wheelchair she had been using since their wedding was getting olds so he needed to change them.
Now that Mira had awakened her Spectral Arms, she was already attempting to move herself, but the old wheelchair’s wheels were stiff, requiring extra strength and precision.
He alredy found he was looking for earlier.
It was a tech boutique store (Arctech) next called Hexatech Innovations.
They specializing in arcane technology that mix modern engineering with arcane craftsmanship and he had found a product called the Neural-Linked Wheelchair.
According to the online description, the wheelchair came with a neural choker that, when worn, released a pulse that read the user’s motor intentions.
The wheelchair would move exactly where the user wanted to go, responding to subconscious directional impulses with zero lag.
Dexter set the GPS and drove.

Hextech Innovations boutique was a large building located in the city’s mid-district. It was all glass and polished steel, with billboard display showcasing rotating models of various Arctech. (Arcane technology)
Dexter parked the Vanguard V4 in the lot and walked inside.
A young lady who was a receptionist approached him with a professional smile.
"Welcome to Hexatech Innovations. How can I help you today?"
"I’m looking for the Neural-Link Wheelchair," Dexter said.
The receptionist’s smile widened. "Of course. Please follow me."
She led him to a dedicated section of the store where a sleek, futuristic wheelchair sat on a raised platform.
A slim, silver choker rested on a velvet display stand beside it.
Dexter examined the chair. It looked really elegant, light weight and not stuffy as Dexter would have expected.
Even the seat was padded with adaptive memory foam that adjusted to the user’s body shape.
"This is one of our flagship products," the receptionist said enthusiastically.
"The neural choker reads the user’s motor cortex impulses. The user simply thinks about where they want to go, and the wheelchair responds instantly.
She gestured to the wheels. "It can navigate stairs, both up and down, using retractable treads. It automatically detects changes in elevation and adjusts its center of gravity accordingly."
Dexter sighed and knew he was going to be drained once more as he asked. "How much?"
"One hundred and twenty thousand dollars."
Dexter blinked. Then blinked again.
$120,000. For a wheelchair.
He stared at the chair, then at the choker, then back at the chair.
One hundred and twenty thousand dollars just so a necklace could read someone’s mind and move them around.
He nearly laughed. For that price, he could push Mira himself for the next ten years.
*I’d rather be the one to push her,* he thought, shaking his head.
The receptionist, sensing his hesitation, quickly continued her pitch.
"Sir, if I may—the wheelchair’s functions go far beyond simple mobility. Allow me to demonstrate."
She activated a holographic display above the chair, showing a detailed simulation of its capabilities.

"The neural-link system also includes an automated toileting function," she explained, swiping through the display. "When the user needs to use the restroom, the wheelchair’s seat module reconfigures, safely transferring the user to a toilet fixture and then returning them to a seated position afterward. This process is fully automated and requires no external assistance."
Dexter’s expression shifted slightly.

"The wheelchair also contains a built-in emergency toilet system within the base," she continued. "For situations where a restroom is not accessible, the chair can process waste internally through a sanitization cycle, maintaining complete hygiene and dignity for the user."
Dexter hesitated. The price was still staggering. But the functions... were functionable. Mira might be slightly less embarrassed by this.
If Mira had this wheelchair, she could move herself anywhere in the house. Outside, bathroom, toilet.
Most importantly, she wouldn’t need him to carry her to the toilet or transfer her from the chair to the bed.
She would have her independence back.
Dexter sighed and pulled out his phone. "I’ll take it."
The receptionist beamed. "Wonderful choice, sir."
As she began processing the order, a middle aged salesman approached Dexter cautiously.
"Excuse me, sir," he said. "I hope you don’t mind me asking, but I’m guessing the person you’re buying this for is a friend or family member who is paralyzed?"
Dexter frowned at the man and his gaze turned cold.

The salesman quickly raised both hands. "No, no, sir—please don’t misunderstand. I’m not making light of the situation. I simply wanted to introduce you to some companion products that I believe would significantly improve the user’s quality of life."
Dexter’s frown eased slightly. "Go ahead."
The salesman gestured toward a large, rectangular box nearby. The box was sleek and white, with a glass front panel revealing what looked like a compact, vertical pod.

"This is our Self-Operating Human Shower System," the salesman explained. "It’s a Grade-One Arctech device designed to pair directly with the Neural-Linked Wheelchair. When the two systems are connected, the wheelchair can automatically transfer the user into the shower pod, where the system bathes them entirely—hair, body, everything—in under five minutes. Once the cycle is complete, the user is dried up dressed and then transferred back into the wheelchair."
He tapped the glass panel, and the pod hummed, demonstrating a series of internal spray nozzles and drying vents.
"It’s fully customizable—water temperature, pressure, soap type, hair treatment. And because it’s mana-powered, it uses less than two liters of water per cycle."

Dexter stared at the shower pod. His mind went back to every morning he had spent carefully lifting Mira into the bathtub, washing her hair, scrubbing her skin, drying her with towels—all while she sat there with her ears burning.
Dexter assumed she was humiliated by it.
If he had this machine, Mira could bathe herself. Privately. Without him seeing her naked or touching her.
The salesman, reading Dexter’s expression, pressed his advantage. He pointed to a smaller device beside the shower pod—a compact, self-contained unit about the size of a mini fridge.

"And this is our companion Portable Toilet System. It pairs with both the wheelchair and the shower unit, creating a complete personal care ecosystem. The wheelchair can transfer the user to any of these three systems—shower, toilet, or back to the chair—entirely through neural-link commands."
Dexter stood there, surrounded by three pieces of technology that could give Mira back her privacy, her dignity, and her independence.
"How much for all three?"
The salesman’s eyes widened slightly. "The wheelchair is $120,000. The shower system is $180,000. The portable toilet system is $100,000. As a bundled package, that’s $400,000 total."
Dexter exhaled slowly. Three Grade-One Arch-tech devices for $400,000.
It was an astronomical sum for Grade-One items. But these weren’t weapons or cultivation tools—they were Arctechs. Very expensive.
But the value of Mira’s dignity? That was priceless.
"I’ll take all three."
The salesman nearly vibrated with excitement. "Excellent, sir! I’ll process the full bundle immediately."
While the paperwork was being prepared, Dexter wandered through the store.
His eyes landed on a display of newer smartphones with enhanced durability, and expanded battery life.
He purchased four.

Dexter inputted his home address for delivery of the wheelchair system, shower pod, and portable toilet. The store confirmed that a specialized installation team would follow him back to his home to install the items.

chapters.title: Chapter 116 | What Do Women Want?
paragraphs: Dexter parked the Vanguard V4 in front of the bungalow just as the sun fully set.
He killed the engine and proceeded to revive his finances.
Starting balance: $1,070,000.
Vanguard V4 SUV: -$280,000.
Neural-Linked Wheelchair bundle: -$400,000.
Four mana-infused smartphones: -$8,000.
Fashion Items:- $ 70,000
Remaining balance: $312,000.
The delivery truck from Hextech Innovations was already parked outside the gate, and the installation team was unloading the boxes.
Dexter entered the house, carrying with him the Neural-Linked Wheelchair. He wanted to surprise Mira himself.
Mira was the only one in the living room. She sat in her old, hospital-issue wheelchair by the window, her eyes closed in deep cultivation.
She didn’t open her eyes even when he entered, but her brows twitched, letting Dexter know she knew he was here.
"How are you?" Dexter asked, walking over to her. "I hope you’re doing well."
Mira opened her eyes, breaking her meditation as she glanced at him from the corner of her eye.
Her lips curled into a mocking smile. "You’re back from playing with your other women?"
Dexter was speechless. "You know jealousy isn’t good for the body, right?"
Mira sneered and was about to deliver one of her usual sharp retorts, when her gaze landed on the object beside Dexter.
It was a wheelchair, but it looked entirely different from hers. It was futuristic, sleek, and quite pretty.
Her crimson eyes narrowed. "What is this?"
Dexter smiled, beaming with pride. "A gift. I got you an advanced wheelchair. I thought this might be more comfortable than the one you’re currently using."

He gestured to the silver choker resting on the seat. "This one can read your mind. It carries your brain waves and determines where you wish to go or what you wish to do. It can even take you to the toilet and bathe you with just a thought."
He smiled proudly, fully expecting Mira to be thankful.
After all, he had spent $400,000 on this ecosystem. It was the ultimate solution to her lack of independence.
Suddenly, Mira’s eyes slowly started to glow until they turned blazingly fiery.
The temperature of the room rose to a drastic degree it was as though a sun was sitting in the center of the room!
Ever since they got the Grand Cosmos Scripture, they could use the star nodes to power their talents without the need to use mana.
A dangerous, burning anger flared in her crimson irises.
Dexter’s smile faltered. He frowned, taking a step back. "You’re... angry?" he asked, though it was more of a statement than a question.
Mira glanced at him, then at the high-tech wheelchair, and then simply closed her eyes, turning her face away.
’What the hell?’
Dexter stood there, completely confused. He blinked his eyes and looked down at the wheelchair, and then at Mira who was radiating so much heat it was almost unbearable.
’What did I do wrong? I’m obviously trying my best here; how did she manage to turn it around and get angry?’
He scratched the back of his head, wondering what on earth he had done wrong.
He sighed and then proceeded to check the girls in the bedroom.
Lyra was the only one inside. She sat cross-legged on her new fluffy bed, cultivating but Selene wasn’t there. So he assumed she was in the backyard.
Feeling his presence, Lyra opened her eyes.
Suddenly, a melodic voice sounded directly inside Dexter’s mind.
’Don’t you want to take care of Mira anymore?’
Dexter blinked, greatly startled by the question.
’Have you finally grown tired of her?’Lyra continued as her voice took an accusatory tone.
’Do you consider her and us a burden to you now?’
"What?" Dexter frowned, projecting his thoughts back to her. ’What do you mean, don’t I want to take care of Mira any longer? Of course I want to take care of her.’
’So why did you get her that particular wheelchair that can read her mind and take care of her?’ Lyra asked.

Dexter almost yanked his hair out in frustration. ’I thought she wanted to be independent! After the bathroom incident, I wanted to make her life a little bit easier. That was why I got the advanced wheelchair for her. I didn’t think she wouldn’t like it. Why didn’t she like it?’

Lyra blinked her eyes, gazing at Dexter’s face but seeing he was truly serious. She shook her head slowly, a faint, knowing smile touching her lips. ’She’s really angry. Which allows me access to her thoughts right now. Moreover, it’s loud.’
"So what should I do?" Dexter asked, rubbing the back of his neck. "Explain to her that I just want to make her life easier. That was the exact reason why I bought the wheelchair in the first place."

Lyra shook her head again. ’You should probably return it. She already likes the usual routine. She might not admit it, but she likes you taking care of her. Asking her to change that routine... she doesn’t like that.’
Suddenly Lyra hesitated but then a hidden devilish smile crossed her face.’She doesn’t want a machine to replace you. Maybe she has feelings for you? I can’t tell.’
Dexter froze.
’Replace me? Might have feelings for me?’
Dexter stared at Lyra, utterly baffled. He thought Mira disliked the sight of him and hated every second of him bathing her, carrying her, and feeding her.
He thought she was humiliated by her dependence on him, which was why he bought the three machines to surprise her.
But she actually ’liked’ the routine? She liked him doing it?
Dexter smiled bitterly, rubbing his face with both hands. "I really don’t understand women at all," he muttered. "Why are you all so confusing!?
Lyra glanced at him and let out a faint smirk as she closed her eyes and resumed her cultivation.
Just then, the installation team from Hexatech was about to come in, carrying massive boxes that contained the Self-Operating Human Shower System and the Portable Toilet.
Dexter quickly intercepted them before they could enter the living room. "Hold on, please return the items."
The man in charge of the installation looked surprised. "Sir? We’ve not even installed it yet. Is there something not up to your standard?"
Dexter shook his head. "No, the equipment is perfect. There was just a... change of heart. I want a refund. Please return the items."
The man blinked, stunned. "A refund? But you already paid for the full bundle..."
"I know," Dexter sighed. "Just pack it up and process the refund. I’ll cover any restocking fees."
The man eventually nodded, though he looked highly confused. He signaled his workers, and they began carrying the heavy boxes back out toward the truck.
Dexter stood in the doorway, watching them go.
After the workers left, Dexter went back to his room. He sat on his new fluffy bed, pondering the entire situation.
Everything was so weird. He thought she wanted nothing more than to be free of his help. But the moment he bought a machine that could do it all for her, she got really really angry.
He smiled bitterly, staring at the ceiling. ’What do women truly want?’
He figured he would never truly understand.
Still, his mind wasn’t at rest knowing Mira was angry with him.
He remembered his portion of the pastries he had bought from Tessa’s bakery, which he had heated with his Heavenly Flame.
He also had some of the spiritual tea leaves left. He went to the kitchen, brewed a small pot of the sweet, rich grade-one tea, and plated a few of the warm pastries.
’She should like this right? This should be enough to appease her right?’
He smiled as he carried the small tray into the living room. Mira was still in her wheelchair, facing the window, her eyes closed.
Dexter walked over and set the small table down right in front of her wheelchair.
Mira hearing the noise and smelling the scent of the tea and the pastries, opened her eyes.
She looked at the steaming tea and the warm pastries. Then, she looked at Dexter.
For a fraction of a second, the blazing flames in her eyes reduced slightly, but it wasn’t appeased.
Her face cold and without another word, she summoned her spectral arms, two glowing orange spectral arms materialized behind her.
They gripped the wheels of her wheelchair, and slowly, she turned until her back was turned towards Dexter.
Dexter stood there, holding the tray, staring at the back of her wheelchair.
He sighed deeply.
’Women are really confusing.’

chapters.title: Chapter 117 | Crimson Valkyrie That Loved The Rain
paragraphs: Dexter stood awkwardly in the living room after Mira turned away from him, rejecting his apology meal as she radiated anger.
Even the tea in his hand was getting superheated by her aura.
Dexter sighed as he scratched his sprouting beards.
’She’s really stubborn. Do I have to get down on my knees to say sorry for trying to help?’
He pursed his lips and turned around as he proceeded to the girl’s room. At that time, rain started to drizzle, beating down on the roof of the house.
As he got to the front of the room. He hadn’t even knocked yet when a dark-haired cutie popped her head out of the door, her eyes locked on the pastries and tea in Dexter’s hand with hunger.
Dexter chuckled. ’You’re easier to please.’
He said while giving her the tray.
Lyra glanced at him, and her lips curled up as she grabbed the tray.
She was about to leave when she suddenly paused. ’Check her name on the internet.’
Lyra’s voice sounded in his head, and she immediately went inside before Dexter could ask what she really meant.
Dexter blinked his eyes in confusion. ’Search up her name?’
He had actually never truly done that. And all the gossip he heard about them was through random channels.
Dexter brought out his new phone, making him remember he hadn’t gifted the girls the new clothes and items he got.
’I just keep getting distracted and forgetting things.’ Dexter frowned. He turned on the Intranet app and typed on the search bar: MiraCalloway.
Several videos immediately popped up of her, but there was one in particular that stood out to him.
It was an old video from four years ago, back when she was the Crimson Valkyrie.
Dexter went inside his room, sat on the edge of the sofa, and pressed play.
The video opened with Mira sitting in a studio chair, dressed in a sleek, crimson-and-black combat suit.

She looked dazzling; her red hair was vibrant, her crimson eyes were bright with life, and she wore a massive, radiant smile. She looked like the sun itself, burning with fiery confidence and an infectious energy that lit up the screen.
Dexter played the video and he was immediately enthralled by it.
After 20 minutes, he got to a particular section.
The interviewer laughed. "So, Mira, tell us. What is the one thing you really love? The one thing that can uplift you even during a bad day?"
Mira tilted her head thoughtfully, a playful glint in her eyes. "Ah, the one thing I love?"
"Yes! And you can’t say your parents, your fiancé, or your fans," the interviewer added jokingly.
Mira chuckled and it sounded so bright and melodic it seemed to belong to an entirely different person than the woman sitting behind him in the living room. "That doesn’t leave much, does it?
She paused as her expression softened.
"The one thing I love... is rain."
The interviewer’s lips parted, clearly surprised. "Rain? But your talent is fire-based. Why rain?"

Mira shrugged, her smile widening into something genuinely warm. "I know, right? Maybe in my past life, I was probably a Legend-rank water ability user. That’s probably why I love it so much." She paused again, her gaze drifting slightly.
"But honestly? Ever since I was a kid, I would go out into the rain anytime. Anytime I’m in a bad mood... if it rains, it melts my mood like ice."
The interviewer laughed loudly, and Mira laughed along with him.
"Alright. We end the segment of..."
Dexter lowered his phone. His face was clearly stunned.
’Did the feisty queen actually laugh?’
It was quite a surprise to him, as he had never even seen her smile for real.
The most he had seen was a half smile or a sneer.
Suddenly Dexter grinned as he heard the downpour of rain increasing even more.
He stood up and walked to the living room. Without a word, he walked towards Mira and unlocked the wheels of her wheelchair.
Mira’s eyes snapped open. She turned her head slightly, glaring at him coldly. "What do you think you’re doing?"
Dexter didn’t answer. He simply gripped the handles and began rolling her toward the back door.
"Dexter? What are you doing?" Mira’s frown deepened.
But Dexter still didn’t reply.
Her voice immediately rose as she growled.
"Dexter!"
Dexter smiled. "You’ll find out soon enough."
As they neared the back door, the sound of the heavy downpour grew louder, and the scent of wet earth filled the hallway.
"Pitta! Patti! Pitta!"
Mira’s eyes widened as she immediately put two and two together.
"Don’t," she said threateningly, like a cat about to strike. Only, this cat is paralyzed.
Dexter shrugged, still moving forward. "Don’t what?"
"Dexter, I’m warning you, don’t," she repeated in an even firmer tone.
But Dexter pretended like he wasn’t listening. But actually, his enhanced hearing had spread really wide.
He knew her well enough by now to tell when she was genuinely furious and when she was just trying to maintain her pride.
So, he ignored her half-hearted protest and continued moving.
Selene was already in the backyard, cultivating quietly under the shade of the roof.
She opened her white eyes, completely confused as she sensed Dexter wheeling Mira directly out into the pouring rain.
The moment the wheelchair crossed the threshold of the overhang, the rain hit them like hail of water bullets.
"Whoosh!"
The rain came down, slammed heavily against the earth, and as Mira was pushed out, the cold rain gushed on her.
Falling on Mira’s shoulders, her hair, her face, and body.

Within seconds, her red hair darkened from copper to deep burgundy, plastering itself against her skull and neck as her clothes soaked, clinging to her slim body and revealing her succulent chest and curvy waist.
However, Mira didn’t move, nor did she speak.
She just sat there in silence with her head tilted upwards and her eyes open as the rain dropped directly into her eyes and face without blinking.
It was just like he was watching a horror movie in real time.
Dexter’s heart dropped as a cold, sickening weight settled in his stomach.
’Shit! Have I misread the situation?’
He stood there for 30 seconds as the rain poured on her but she simply sat there in a terrifying silence that grabbed Dexter’s heart second after second.
’She’s changed.’
Three years of paralysis, bitterness, loss and rage and the slow, grinding erosion of everything she used to be.
Who was he to think that a video from the past could override all of that?
Who was he to think that the girl who loved the rain still existed somewhere inside this woman who couldn’t even lift her own arms?
He had actually made a grave mistake, and he knew at this moment, Mira might never forgive him for this.
’I truly messed up.’
However...

chapters.title: Chapter 118 | First Connection
paragraphs: Trauma freezes you. It locks you behind a wall of your own making, but who you are is still waiting on the other side of the ice. -Neil Gaiman
Dexter realized at this moment that he had made a mistake.
A really terrible mistake.
He had dragged her out here against her will into the rain as if three years of suffering wasn’t enough to kill whatever life she had for the rain.
Guilt surged through him like ice water. He immediately went forward, opening his mouth to apologize and quickly drag her back into the house when he saw it.
It was her lips, and they had actually curled upwards.
And it wasn’t curled upwards into a sneer as he had expected; it was a smile!
She was actually smiling!
Dexter’s breath caught in his throat, and the guilt and panic he had been feeling at that moment evaporated in an instant.
Her smile continued to widen as she tilted her head upwards, letting the rain pour on her face.
Somehow, the smile wasn’t as radiant as what he had seen in the interview and contained a hint of sadness. But it was the most genuine smile he had witnessed from Mira since he set eyes on her.
Then, slowly, two glowing orange spectral arms materialized behind her.
They unsteadily reached out into the downpour and scooped up handfuls of rainwater, bringing them back and gently pouring them over her face, neck, and arms.
She closed her eyes and scooped more as the arms continued to gather rainwater, letting it cascade over her.
Mira’s smile widened even further as a cute giggle escaped her lips.
Each handful seemed to wash and melt something within her.
Through it all, Dexter stood behind her, completely forgetting that he himself was getting soaked as his jaw hung slightly open in pure shock.
Had she actually giggled?
In all the time he had known her, he had never once seen Mira like this. Not once.
And the sight of the quiet, devastating beauty of this woman giggling in the rain made Dexter’s heart tremble with something he hadn’t felt in a long time.

No matter what happened to a person, the essence of who they were could never truly be destroyed. It could be suppressed, locked behind walls of anger and bitterness and pain, but it would always remain.
And with the right spark, it could always shine again.
Selene, who was standing beneath the overhang, had a soft, quiet smile on her face.
"So that’s what you look like. You’re perfect."
She muttered as the vibration from the rain hitting Dexter’s body perfectly outlined his face and his figure. Everything was extremely detailed as she saw him clearly for the first time.
Dexter stood behind Mira in the downpour, completely soaked to the bone, yet he couldn’t feel the cold.
He was entirely too stunned by what he was seeing.
Even after 5 straight minutes of watching Mira play in the rain, scooping water with her spectral arms like a child, he still couldn’t believe his eyes.
Slowly, Dexter reached out and gripped the handles of her old wheelchair. The feeling seemed to bring Mira back to herself.
She immediately tried to wipe the joy from her face, attempting to rebuild her icy walls. But it was too late. Her lips didn’t cooperate with her, still locked in that perfectly radiant smile.
She felt Dexter’s gaze on her, and it was hot and intense.
Mira turned around and glared at Dexter, her crimson eyes narrowing with as much menace as she could muster, which, given the smile still ghosting across her face, was not nearly enough.
"What are you looking at?" she snapped.
Dexter stared at her. His mind went completely blank.
He looked at her rain-soaked body, her flushed face and those pretty crimson eyes glaring at him, and spoke without thinking.
"You are really beautiful."
It was like a stone dropped into a still lake.
Mira froze.
For three years, no one had called her beautiful.
For three years, she had been the disabled talented heroine.
No one looked at her and saw beauty. No one looked at her like Dexter was.
And now this infuriating, reckless, stubbornly kind idiot was looking at her like she was the most breathtaking thing he had ever seen.
A deep crimson flush bloomed across her pale cheeks as her cold demeanor cracked.
She tried to retort or say something, but nothing came out.
Dexter saw the blush on her cheeks and her bashful eyes.
A sudden, reckless, playful impulse that he couldn’t resist surged through him, and he smirked playfully.

Mira’s eyes widened further. Her blush—if possible—deepened another shade. She looked away sharply, her jaw working, her spectral arms retracting against her sides as though she could somehow make herself smaller.
"What are you trying to do?" she demanded, her voice cracking slightly on the last word. She cleared her throat, trying to recover. "What are you planning?"
Dexter grinned.
"What don’t you guess?"
He tightened his grip on the wheelchair handles.
Then, without warning, he took off running as he pushed her around the backyard, spinning her in circles.
Like a father pushing a child at a park.
Mira wyws wiended.
"Don’t you dare drop me—" she growled in a commanding tone.
It was at that moment the wheelchair hit a puddle and sent a spray of water directly into her face.
Mira sputtered and blinked as the water fell down her face onto her clothes.
Dexter froze instantly and then burst out laughing as he pointed at her stained face.
Mira’s lips twitched and then, against her every will, Mira actually laughed.
From the window of the neighboring one-story building, Tessa watched them, and a small smile spread across her freckled face.
"Dexter," Tessa murmured to herself, leaning against the window wall. "You’re cute."
She felt a swell of warmth in her chest as she watched Dexter play with Mira, laughing like a kid.
For a moment, Tessa almost thought the two people actually married for love and not because of a silly contract.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 | REWARDS!!!
paragraphs: Thirty minutes later, Dexter finally wheeled a thoroughly soaked Mira back inside the house.
Her lips were still curled into a smile she couldn’t suppress, no matter how hard she tried to rebuild her cold mask.
Dexter wheeled her into the bathroom.
Without a word, he carefully stripped her naked by removing her soaked clothes, placing them in a pile by the side of the tub.
He adjusted the shower to a warm temperature carried Mira and placed her underneath the warm shower.
Mira didn’t blush this time nor did she give any sarcastic remarks.
She simply sat there, smiling quietly with her crimson eyes half-closed in contentment as Dexter took care of her.
The warm water rinsed away the rain and the cold, and she let herself simply exist in the moment.
Dexter carefullt washed her hair, arms and legs with soft sponge and soap and then turned off the shower, wrapped her in a fresh towel, and carefully dried her hair,
After which, he dressed her in a soft, warm cardigan and comfortable trousers.
Mira glanced up at him. "Your fashion sense is terrible.
Dexter rolled his eye and smiled. "Bite me."
Usually, she would have fired off a witty remark about how men shouldn’t say stuffs like that. But she simply rolled her eyes. She was still in a good mood.

Dexter carried her to her new bed the fluffy queen mattress the delivery workers had set up that morning. He gently placed her down, arranging the pillows behind her back so she could rest comfortably and covered her up with the duffel.
"Sleep well."
He was about to turn and leave when something suddenly wrapped around his wrist.
He looked down and saw a glowing orange spectral arm had extended from behind Mira, its translucent fingers curled gently around his forearm.
Dexter turned toward her. Mira was lying with her back flat on the bed but she had turned her face from him, making her red hair fan out across the white pillow.
Then she mumbled in a small voice.
"Thank you. It was nice."
Dexter smiled gently as warmth bloomed in his chest. he whispered back.
"Any time."
The spectral arm slowly faded into nothing, realizing his wrist.
Mira closed her eyes and within minutes, her breathing slowed as she fell into the deepest, most peaceful sleep she had experienced in three years.
Dexter quietly left the bedroom, closing the door behind him. He was pondering what to make for dinner for the other two girls who would definitely eat when—

After which, he dressed her in a soft, warm cardigan and comfortable trousers.
Mira glanced up at him.
"Your fashion sense is terrible.
Dexter rolled his eye and smiled.
"Bite me."
Usually, she would have fired off a witty remark about how men shouldn’t say stuffs like that.
But she simply rolled her eyes.
She was still in a good mood.
Dexter carried her to her new bed the fluffy queen mattress the delivery workers had set up that morning.
He gently placed her down, arranging the pillows behind her back so she could rest comfortably and covered her up with the duffel.
"Sleep well."
He was about to turn and leave when something suddenly wrapped around his wrist.
He looked down and saw a glowing orange spectral arm had extended from behind Mira, its translucent fingers curled gently around his forearm.
Dexter turned toward her.
Mira was lying with her back flat on the bed but she had turned her face from him, making her red hair fan out across the white pillow.
Then she mumbled in a small voice.
"Thank you.
It was nice."
Dexter smiled gently as warmth bloomed in his chest. he whispered back.
"Any time."
The spectral arm slowly faded into nothing, realizing his wrist.
Mira closed her eyes and within minutes, her breathing slowed as she fell into the deepest, most peaceful sleep she had experienced in three years.
Dexter quietly left the bedroom, closing the door behind him.
He was pondering what to make for dinner for the other two girls who would definitely eat when—
[Ding!]
Golden text erupted across his vision as notifications popped up all over his line of sight.
[10,000x Investment Multiplier System]
[Investment Return Activated]

Three Premium Beds Invested.

Each bed is forged from Dreamwood and Void Silk.
While sleeping on them:
• Cultivation speed increases by 200%.
• Mental fatigue disappears after only one hour of sleep.
• Nightmares cannot affect the sleeper.
• Mana recovery increases by 200%.
• The body continuously absorbs surrounding mana even while asleep.
• Minor injuries slowly heal throughout the night.

Temporarily increases fire affinity, strength, regeneration, and cultivation speed.
Duration: Seven days per serving.
Nine-Star Moonfish Essence Soup
Greatly increases mana recovery, strengthens the soul, improves concentration, and permanently increases spiritual perception after repeated consumption.
Celestial Kirin Spirit Rice
Improves physical constitution, removes cultivation impurities, greatly enhances mana absorption, and increases breakthrough success rate.

Type-4 Virgo’s Might Necklace
A life-saving treasure containing the full-powered attack of a Transcendent Realm expert.
Once activated, it unleashes a devastating beam capable of heavily injuring—or even killing—an early Transcendent Realm cultivator.
Uses Remaining: 1/1
Type-4 Aurora’s Guardian Necklace
A defensive treasure capable of sensing fatal danger.
The instant the wearer encounters a life-threatening attack, the necklace automatically teleports them anywhere within a 100-mile radius.
Can only be activated once before needing to be recharged with mana.

2) Second Move: Roaring Thunder Fang
3) Third Move: Eightfold Lightning Severance
3) Fourth Move: Thunder Dragon’s Descent

8) Eighth Move: Myriad Lightning Cataclysm
9) Ninth Move: Godkill Judgment

Time spent to Prepare Meals for Wives → Reward Granted

Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture evolves to Indestructible Buddha Endurance Body (Tier 7)

Talent Upgraded: Enhanced Hearing — C-Rank → B-Rank

Obtained: Type-6 Arcane SUV — Ultima Skybreaker
A masterpiece forged by master Arcane Engineers and Arcane Blacksmiths.
Abilities:
• Transcendent Armor: Chassis forged from Type-6 Arcane Alloy, capable of withstanding several full-powered attacks from a Transcendent Realm expert.
• Flight Mode: By consuming Mana Cores, deploys hidden jet thrusters and can fly at tremendous speed.
• Ultra-Speed Engine: Top speed rivals a Peak Ultra Realm expert.
• Mana Cannon: Mounted beneath the chassis; capable of severely injuring an Ultra Realm expert and threatening an early Transcendent Realm cultivator.
• Arcane Machine Guns: Twin mana-powered machine guns with automatic hostile target lock-on.
• Adaptive Shield: Energy barrier automatically activates when danger is sensed.
• Amphibious Mode: Can travel across water and underwater for extended periods.
• Self-Repair System: Minor damage repaired automatically using stored mana.
• Spatial Storage Trunk: Contains a storage space several times larger than its exterior dimensions.
And that wasn’t all!

chapters.title: Chapter 120 | REWARDS 2!!!
paragraphs: [Reward 12]
Investment Detected: Purchased Mobile Phones → 100× Return Activated!
Obtained: Three Type-3 Arcane Smart Devices
• Self-charging through mana and body heat.
• Unlimited internet access through automatic satellite synchronization.
• Can perform minor hacks to other devices
• Built-in emergency distress beacon.
• High-grade encrypted communications.
[Reward 13]
Investment Detected: Purchased Ice Suppressant Medicine → 100× Return Activated!
Obtained: Thirty Grade-3 Eternal Frost Suppressant Serums
Each serum suppresses unstable ice energy for one full week. While active:
• Ice outbreaks are completely halted.
• Pain caused by frost energy is greatly reduced.
• The user’s body slowly adapts to the ice energy instead of rejecting it.
[Reward 14]
Investment Detected: Giving Possible Companion: Ancient Beast Egg → 100× Return Activated!
Reward: Incubation Accelerated
The incubation time has been reduced by 90%.
[Reward 15]
Investment Detected: Cooked for wives → 100× Return Activated!
Obtained: 100 Kilograms of Premium Diamond Spirit Rice
[Reward 16]
Investment Detected: Protected Selene from Cold Energy → Reward Option Unlocked
Fusion Opportunity Available
Would you like to fuse the following flames?
• Heavenly Flame (Emperor Void Flame)
• Demonic Flame (Chaos Flame Demon Bloodline)
Fusion Result: Abyssal Heart Flame (6th Heavenly Flame)
[Reward 17]
Target: Mira — Happiness Level Increased → 100× Return Activated!
Obtained: Grade-5 Divine Nerve Restoration Pill ×1
A legendary medicinal pill capable of restoring damaged nerves.
Effects:
• Instantly heals 20% of all damaged nerves.
• Greatly accelerates the regeneration of remaining damaged nerves.
• Permanently increases nerve vitality.
• Can only be consumed once every six months.
[Reward 18]
Special Family Reward — Three girls’ trust has increased simultaneously.
Obtained: Family Guardian Barrier Formation (Grade-6)
A defensive formation that can be installed in the house. Once activated:
• Prevents enemies below the Transcendent Realm from entering by force.
• Conceals the house from ordinary perception.
• Detects hostile intent.
• Automatically alerts Dexter whenever an intruder approaches.
• Can operate continuously using Nexus Cores.
The stream of golden notifications finally ended.
Dexter who was on his way to the kitchen was entirely stunned.
His face was flushed and he was panting heavily without him knowing!
Not to mention, his hands were trembling from the sheer magnitude of the rewards!
Three Type-6 relic weapons, a flying, armored, weaponized SUV. Grade-6 recipes and heavenly ingredients. A Grade-6 defensive barrier for the house and dozens of other priceless treasures.
Even a Transcendent Realm expert would go mad with envy if they learned what he had obtained in a single day!

If these items were suddenly found in the city, every family would wage war on each other for these items with him and yet, he had earned it all by buying, cooking meals, and pushing a wheelchair into the rain.
Dexter slowly exhaled as a wide smile spread across his face. The excitement that had calmed down after coming back from the rain increased drastically.
"Worth it."
He looked toward the bedroom door, behind which Mira was were sleeping on the new bed he purchased for them and he couldn’t help but grin.
"What a wonderful day!"
Dexter sat cross-legged on his bed with widened eyes like a restless child on Christmas morning.
He pulled up the system interface again, and began sorting through his rewards one by one.
’Thankfully the Type 3 beds looks just the same as the one I bought. The girls shouldn’t suspect a thing.’
But he knew the girls would definitely notice something was off once the effect of the items started to show.
The three Type-6 weapons also retained the appearances of the Type-3 relics he had bought from the Ultra realm person at the black market.
’Seems like the system likes being discreet also.’ Dexter muttered in thought.
He decided to swap them when they were sleeping.

Of course the girls would notice the difference the moment they actually channeled mana into them, but he wasn’t worried. He wasn’t going to let them fight anytime soon anyway. He would protect them from everything.
His mind shifted to the three Grade-6 Arcane Recipes.l and his mouth practically watered.
The system had generously provided ten full portions of ingredients for each recipe.
Even if he failed a few times, with his Great Grandmaster Foodsmith proficiency, he was confident he could produce at least six or seven successful Grade-6 meals.

Also there was the Grade-4 Celestial Moon Pastries were. He planned to give them to the girls later while they cultivated, letting them munch on the pastries to sustain their energy and boost their absorption rates.
As for the two Type-4 Arcane Necklaces; the Transcendent Strike and the Spatial Guardian, hw planned to swap them with the girls’ current necklaces around 4’o clock.
They always slept deeply around that time.
Then there was the Tier-4 Martial Technique: Thunder GodKill Saber Art.
Dexter’s eyes sparkled as the knowledge of the saber art settled into his mind.

He had desperately needed a martial art. The fact that he had managed to kill those two Superhuman assassins on the highway was purely because of his bloodline and his type 3 weapon skill: Spatial Cleave.
Without the relic weapon and the bloodline he would have definitely died.
Now, he had a true, high-grade martial art for attacking and improving his attacks.

As for the two years of compressed cultivation. Dexter rolled his eyes. His cooking speed had advanced which was why he cooked with less and less time. Otherwise, he would have gained at least 5 to 7 years of cultivation.
Dexter closed his eyes. "System, accept the Two Years of Cultivation."
Instantly, a roaring tsunami of pure, refined mana erupted from the core of his system, slamming into his physical body.
"Bang! Bang! Bang!"
Deep inside Dexter’s inner universe, the entire universe had changed drastically.
There were now seven star nodes around the massive, twelve-segmented helix-shaped DNA structure floating in the darkness of the universe.
But that wasn’t all, there was now a massive crackling blue cloud and a roaring golden flames in the inner universe.
Those were actually the two talents he extracted from the corpses of the two superhuman experts.
The Thunder and the golden flames were above and below the massive helix shape structure. Connected to it tightly.
The massive, twelve-segmented helix-shaped DNA structure spun slowly in the darkness.
The first three segments were already blazing with brilliant light.
As the two years’ worth of cultivation energy surged into the void, the darkness around the helix shattered. The energy crashed into the fourth segment.
"BOOM!"
The fourth segment lit up instantly, glowing tendrils extending downward to connect with the fifth.

The fifth segment began to glow, filling rapidly with vibrant energy until it reached its peak. It then extended tendrils to the sixth, lighting it up, and continued cascading all the way down to the seventh segment.
The flood of energy finally exhausted itself, leaving the seventh segment fully illuminated.
Dexter opened his eyes and a shockwave of energy rippled through his bedroom. He had broken through and he was now at the Seventh Stage of the Superhuman Realm!
Along with his cultivation leap, his body-tempering scriptures had evolved.
The Eternal Buddha Endurance Scripture had upgraded to a Tier-7 technique, officially renamed the Indestructible Buddha Endurance Body.
The stages of the technique remained the same, but their effects had been magnified terrifyingly.
