chapters.title: Chapter 136 | What Am I Supposed To Do, Let You Go?
paragraphs: The Hero Association headquarters never slept.
Even at this hour, the corridors hummed with activity.
Heroes in armor strode through the hallways with confidence.
Support staff shuffled papers behind desks.
Jasmine Constance sat at her assigned workstation in the Silver-Rank Administrative Wing, her fingers moving mechanically across the keyboard.
A stack of dungeon clearance reports sat beside her elbow, each one requiring review and verification before being submitted to the central archive.
She was halfway through the seventh report when a familiar voice called out from behind her.
"Hey, Jasmine, did you see the morning broadcast?"
It was Darren, her colleague. A guy who had been trying to get with her since she started working here.
Jasmine didn’t look up. "I’ve been busy."
"You should check it out." Darren leaned against the edge of her desk, arms crossed. "That Ashford mess. You know, the noble family?"
Jasmine’s fingers paused on the keyboard. Just for a second. Then she resumed typing.
"What about them?"

"Turns out the bastard son he’s actually not as useless as everyone thought. The Ashford family thought he was useless and disowned him after burdening him with marrying three cripples." Darren whistled low.
Jasmine’s hands stopped moving completely.
"Three?"

"Three. And not just any three. The three crippled daughters from the Calloway, Vance, and Frost families." Darren shook his head slowly. "The ones from that SSS-rank dungeon disaster a few years back. The Crimson Valkyrie, the Shadow Saintess, and the Eternal Ice Princess."
He let out a low, pitying breath.

"The bastard son of the Ashford family, married to three crippled women. Dumped in some run-down bungalow in the outer district but he actually turned out not to be usless. He actually showed up in a C-rank dungeon outbreak and managed to deal with the disaster along with Aurora, Kinetic Man and a few heroes. A few heroes were even praising him that he saved them. "
Darren clicked his tongue. "I wonder what the Ashford family would do now that they’ve found out he’s no longer usless and actually at the superhuman realm."
Jasmine stared at the glowing screen in front of her. The text blurred.
She could feel her heartbeat in her throat.
’Dexter.’
The name screamed inside her skull but not a single sound left her lips.
She remembered him.
Of course she remembered him.
She was the one who had been there when the world told him he was nothing.
Five years ago.
Ashford Family Stable.
Jasmine had found him sitting on the edge of the roof, looking sad.
She had seen the way the other servants treated him and after she was done with her Servants duties, she run across the entire Place to find him.
When she reached the rooftop, she didn’t speak immediately. She simply walked over, sat down beside him, and wrapped her arms around his waist.
"Not even the servants...," he had whispered. His voice was empty and hollow.

"Not just being a slave, I possess an f rank talent and lowr mana affinity. I can’t even absorb mana properly. I’ll never become a hero. I’ll never be anything. There’s no hope I can ever escape this place."
Jasmine had held him tighter.
"Your rank doesn’t define you, Dexter. You can leave anytime you wish. No one can stop you."
"You don’t understand—"

"I understand perfectly." She pulled back just enough to look into his eyes. Her own were fierce. Burning. "I’ve watched you train for years. I’ve watched you push yourself harder than anyone else. Your affinity is low. So what? Talent is low, who cares?. But determination? Will?" She pressed her palm flat against his chest. "That can’t be taught. And you have more of it than anyone I’ve ever met."
For a brief moment, something flickered in his eyes. A tiny ember of hope in the middle of a dying fire.
That was the day they became inseparable.
And now, standing in the present, standing in that same hallway with Darren’s words echoing in her ears, Jasmine felt that same ember burning inside her own chest.
"Jasmine?"
Darren’s voice snapped her back.
She blinked. Her hands were trembling slightly. She pressed them flat against the desk to still them.
"You okay?" Darren frowned, leaning closer. "You look pale."
"I’m fine." Her voice came out quieter than she intended. She cleared her throat and repeated herself, louder this time. "I’m fine. Just tired."
Darren studied her for a moment. He clearly didn’t believe her. But he knew better than to push a woman you’re trying to court.

"Anyway," he continued, straightening up, "the whole thing is a mess. The three families thought they were marrying the legitimate heir. Turns out the bastard was the firstborn. So they got scammed. Now they’re stuck with a disowned nobody living in the slums with their crippled daughters.
He laughed dryly.
"Can you imagine? Three former S-rank talents, reduced to... that?"
Jasmine’s jaw tightened.
"He’s not a nobody," she said quietly.
Darren blinked. "What?"
"Nothing." Jasmine turned back to her screen. "I need to finish these reports."
Darren shrugged and wandered back to his own desk.
Jasmine stared at the holographic text floating before her eyes. None of the words registered. Her mind had already drifted far away.
’Dexter... what happened to you?’
The rooftop. One year ago.
The last day she had seen him.
But everything else was different.
Dexter stood at the edge of the stable rooftop, his back to her.
"The marriage contract came through," he said. His voice was flat, emotionless.
"The family gave me two options. Accept the arrangement and leave the estate. Or refuse and.l remain here as a servant for the rest of my life."
Jasmine’s heart had trembled.
"Then refuse!" She said grimly.
"Dexter, refuse and come with me. We can leave this city. We can go somewhere far away. My family isn’t powerful, but we can—"

"Your family isn’t powerful." He turned to face her. His eyes were dead. "That’s exactly the point, Jasmine. If I run, the Ashfords will hunt us down. And your family cannot protect you from them. No one can."
"Then let them come!" Her voice cracked. As her eyes shook. "I don’t care about the Ashfords! I don’t care about any of them! I just want—"
"But I care."
His voice was so quiet she almost missed it.
He reached up and gently wiped a tear from her cheek.
"I care about what happens to you, Jasmine. And if I run, they will use you to get to me. They will hurt you. And I..." His voice faltered. "I can’t let that happen."
"Then what am I supposed to do?" she whispered. "Just... let you go?"

chapters.title: Chapter 137 | You’re In My Bed
paragraphs: Dexter was startled awake by a crisp, chiming notification from his system.
He blinked, his eyes adjusting to the darkness. The digital clock on the nightstand read 5:00 AM. It was the dead of night.

As his senses sharpened, he realized he was not in his own room. He was in the girls’ bedroom. He hadn’t managed to leave the night before; the exhaustion from the battle, combined with Selene’s iron grip, had pulled him straight into a deep sleep.

He lay still, scanning the room with his enhanced hearing. To his left, Mira was asleep on her own bed, completely silent, not making a single sound. To his right, Lyra was also sleeping, but instead of snoring, she was making a soft, rhythmic purring sound, like a cute tiger cub.
Then, Dexter’s eyes widened.
Mira’s fingers were twitching. Not just one finger, but all five of her fingers on her right hand were making subtle, grasping motions, as if she were trying to hold onto something.
"Finally!"
Dexter whispered happily.
A massive smile broke across Dexter’s face. All their efforts, the Grade-1, Grade-2, and Grade-3 meals, the tea, the massages and the arduous cultivation—were not in vain.
Myrawas actually healing. Slowly but steadily, her nerves were regenerating. He could tell that given enough time and his continued cooking, she would heal rapidly.
His joy, however, was immediately accompanied by a sharp, tingling numbness in his left arm. He looked down.

Selene was still fast asleep, but she was clinging to his arm like a lifeline. She had wrapped both of her arms around it, pulling it tightly against her chest, hugging it like a giant teddy bear. He could feel two incredibly soft, massive mounds of flesh squeezing tightly against his forearm, making him feel incredibly embarrassed. The blood flow to his arm had been completely cut off, leaving the limb frozen and numb.

Yet, looking at her sleeping so peacefully, her silver hair—which looked significantly healthier and prettier than when he first met her—spilling across the pillow, he found himself thinking the numbness was entirely worth it. Her eyelashes fluttered softly, and she murmured something inaudible in her sleep, pulling his arm even closer.
As if sensing his gaze, Selene’s eyes suddenly snapped open.

Through her echolocation, her sightless gaze immediately locked onto Dexter. At first, her brows furrowed in confusion, as if she thought she was dreaming. Then, she blinked, realizing it was reality.
"You are here," she muttered softly.
Dexter nodded. "Yes, I’m here."
Her brows furrowed even deeper. "You are here on my bed."
"Yes, I’m on your bed.
She remained silent for a few seconds as though waiting for it to sink into Dexter. But Dexter was also doing the same.
She couldn’t handle the silence anymore and tilted her head as she said.
"Why?"
Dexter chuckled and glanced down at his left arm, which she was still desperately clinging to.
Selene followed his gaze downward. She saw her own hands and even one of her leg tightly wrapped around his bicep, pressing it against her chest and belly.
"Eh—"

Her eyes widened in shock. She instantly let go, her pale face flushing a deep crimson. She tried to hide her embarrassment by lowering her head, but her skin was simply too pale to conceal the blush.
She looked like a child who had been caught doing something wrong, yet even with her head down, Dexter could feel her echolocation completely focused on him.
Dexter chuckled at her incredible cuteness but didn’t say anything to further embarrass her. He stood up, shaking his numb arm vigorously to get the blood flowing again.
As he turned to leave, he heard Selene’s tiny, whisper-like voice. "Sorry. And... thank you."
Dexter smiled warmly. "You’re welcome."
He left the bedroom and headed straight to his own room. Sitting on his bed, he finally opened the system notification that had woken him up.
[Investment Return Detected: Suppressed Eternal Winter Ice Curse & Sustained Emotional Care]
[Multiplier: 100x]
[Rewards Granted:]
1. E-Rank Talent Advancement Card: Ice Manipulation.
2. Raw Materials: 10 kg of Premium Diamond Rice and additional spiritual ingredients.
3. Grade-3 Divine Peak Recovery Pill ×1
Dexter inspected the Grade-3 Divine Pill carefully. The system’s description was very specific:

[The pill can temporarily heal all injuries and return the user to their absolute peak form for exactly 24 hours. However, once the 24-hour duration expires, the user’s original injuries will not only return but will significantly worsen, making the pill a desperate, win-lose situation.]

Dexter frowned. Selene was blind. Although she could "see" through echolocation now, it wasn’t true sight. A pill that could temporarily heal all injuries and restore her to her peak would be incredibly tempting for a crippled hero.
But the backlash was too severe.
"I don’t think it’s safe to give this to them," Dexter muttered to himself. "If they get desperate, they might use it, and end up hurting themselves more."

Yet, he also realized that giving them the pill was like giving them hope. It was physical proof that their conditions could be reversed, that a cure existed. He wasn’t 100% sure how long it would take to fully heal them, but with the system, he was at least 50% sure he could do it eventually.
He decided to hold onto the pill for now, keeping it as a safety net rather than giving it to the girls prematurely.
As he put the pill away, a sudden thought hit him. He slapped his forehead.
"Damn it. I didn’t make dinner."
He had been so exhausted and distracted by Selene’s outbreak that he had completely forgotten to cook the evening meal. He stood up and walked to the kitchen to see what the girls had eaten.
Upon checking the kitchen, he found the pots and pans exactly where he had left them. The girls hadn’t cooked.
Instead, he checked the microwave and found it completely empty. The Celestial Moon Pastries he had stored there were gone.
Lyra and Mira had eaten the pastries for dinner. While Selene hadn’t eaten anything.

Dexter leaned against the counter, deep in thought. Lyra had been so angry the day before that she had rejected the pastry he offered her directly. For her to reject food meant she was truly mad at him.
Usually, food was his ultimate peace-offering. If food couldn’t calm Lyra down, he had no idea what would. He needed a new plan to appease her.

As for Mira, he temporarily placed her in the back of his mind. Her emotions were so unpredictable, swinging between angry, indifferent, and secretly pleased, that trying to decipher her was like dealing with someone bipolar.
He would tackle Lyra first. Her expressions were usually more readable, and right now, her face was frigid.
He sighed, staring at the empty microwave. "How do I fix this?" he muttered, scratching his chin as the sun began to peek through the kitchen window.

sentences.text: Dexter was startled awake by a crisp, chiming notification from his system.
He blinked, his eyes adjusting to the darkness.
The digital clock on the nightstand read 5:00 AM.
It was the dead of night.
As his senses sharpened, he realized he was not in his own room.
He was in the girls’ bedroom.
He hadn’t managed to leave the night before; the exhaustion from the battle, combined with Selene’s iron grip, had pulled him straight into a deep sleep.
He lay still, scanning the room with his enhanced hearing.
To his left, Mira was asleep on her own bed, completely silent, not making a single sound.
To his right, Lyra was also sleeping, but instead of snoring, she was making a soft, rhythmic purring sound, like a cute tiger cub.
Then, Dexter’s eyes widened.
Mira’s fingers were twitching.
Not just one finger, but all five of her fingers on her right hand were making subtle, grasping motions, as if she were trying to hold onto something.
"Finally!"
Dexter whispered happily.
A massive smile broke across Dexter’s face.
All their efforts, the Grade-1, Grade-2, and Grade-3 meals, the tea, the massages and the arduous cultivation—were not in vain.
Myrawas actually healing.
Slowly but steadily, her nerves were regenerating.
He could tell that given enough time and his continued cooking, she would heal rapidly.
His joy, however, was immediately accompanied by a sharp, tingling numbness in his left arm.
He looked down.
Selene was still fast asleep, but she was clinging to his arm like a lifeline.
She had wrapped both of her arms around it, pulling it tightly against her chest, hugging it like a giant teddy bear.
He could feel two incredibly soft, massive mounds of flesh squeezing tightly against his forearm, making him feel incredibly embarrassed.
The blood flow to his arm had been completely cut off, leaving the limb frozen and numb.

Yet, looking at her sleeping so peacefully, her silver hair—which looked significantly healthier and prettier than when he first met her—spilling across the pillow, he found himself thinking the numbness was entirely worth it.
Her eyelashes fluttered softly, and she murmured something inaudible in her sleep, pulling his arm even closer.
As if sensing his gaze, Selene’s eyes suddenly snapped open.
Through her echolocation, her sightless gaze immediately locked onto Dexter.
At first, her brows furrowed in confusion, as if she thought she was dreaming.
Then, she blinked, realizing it was reality.
"You are here," she muttered softly.
Dexter nodded.
"Yes, I’m here."
Her brows furrowed even deeper.
"You are here on my bed."
"Yes, I’m on your bed.
She remained silent for a few seconds as though waiting for it to sink into Dexter.
But Dexter was also doing the same.
She couldn’t handle the silence anymore and tilted her head as she said.
"Why?"
Dexter chuckled and glanced down at his left arm, which she was still desperately clinging to.
Selene followed his gaze downward.
She saw her own hands and even one of her leg tightly wrapped around his bicep, pressing it against her chest and belly.
"Eh—"
Her eyes widened in shock.
She instantly let go, her pale face flushing a deep crimson.
She tried to hide her embarrassment by lowering her head, but her skin was simply too pale to conceal the blush.
She looked like a child who had been caught doing something wrong, yet even with her head down, Dexter could feel her echolocation completely focused on him.
Dexter chuckled at her incredible cuteness but didn’t say anything to further embarrass her.
He stood up, shaking his numb arm vigorously to get the blood flowing again.
As he turned to leave, he heard Selene’s tiny, whisper-like voice.
"Sorry.
And... thank you."
Dexter smiled warmly.
"You’re welcome."
He left the bedroom and headed straight to his own room.

E-Rank Talent Advancement Card: Ice Manipulation.

chapters.title: Chapter 138 | Mad Lyra
paragraphs: Dexter didn’t go back to sleep.
He sat cross-legged on his bed and closed his eyes, as he cultivated.
Suddenly he noticed something different with his body.
"I’ve broken through?"
Dexter chuckled. He hadn’t even been trying, Yet his body had continued absorbing mana automatically.
This was the benefit of an EX-Rank affinity. His body automatically drew in energy into his body.
Whether he was awake or asleep, meditating or eating or fighting, the world offered its power to him willingly, and his body accepted it without hesitation.
He hadn’t even noticed the breakthrough happening. One moment he was Seventh Stage Superhuman. The next he had woken up and was in the Eighth Stage.
Dexter closed his eyes and turned his attention inward, entering the vast, dark universe of his inner world.
The cosmic DNA helix floated in the void, its first seven segments blazing with stable, radiant light.
The eighth segment had ignited during the night, its gray shell crumbling away to reveal a fresh, pulsing glow that connected seamlessly to the chain.
But that wasn’t all.
Dexter’s gaze shifted to the seven brilliant Star Nodes floating near the top of the helix.
They burned steadily, each one a miniature sun radiating independent mana.
But there were actually newer ones.
Overnight, he had awakened three more!
’It seems what they said is true, fighting an killing monsters really unlocks one’s potential.’
And he hadn’t even absorbed the nexus cores of the beasts yet.
Now he possess ten mana reservoirs, each one capable of storing and supplying mana separately from the others.
This meant that his total mana capacity was equivalent to ten individuals of the same cultivation realm combined.
A single Eighth Stage Superhuman would normally possess one mana pool. Dexter possessed ten.

With this kind of capacity, if he ever acquired an ultimate technique that could drain an ordinary cultivator dry in seconds or maybe when he reach a high stage in the Godslayer Thunder Saber art, he could use it recklessly.
But the true advantage of the Star Nodes was beyond that.
The Grand Cosmos Scripture didn’t use meridians.

It bypassed them entirely. Each Star Node functioned as an independent power source, capable of feeding mana directly to a specific technique or body part without needing to circulate through the traditional meridian network.
This meant Dexter could use multiple techniques simultaneously.
Conventionally, a cultivator channeled mana through their meridians to power a technique.
Using two techniques at once required splitting the mana flow, which reduced the effectiveness of both and demanded immense concentration.
Highly proficient fighters could manage two, maybe three, techniques simultaneously.
But Dexter wasn’t using meridians.
With ten Star Nodes, he could assign one node to power a flame technique with his left hand.
Another node to power a thunder technique with his right.
A third to sustain a movement technique.
A fourth to maintain a defensive barrier.
A fifth to fuel an auxiliary talent.
A sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth—all running independently, all simultaneously, without any loss of efficiency or concentration.
Ten techniques at once.
And if he awakened twenty Star Nodes, he could use twenty. If he awakened a hundred, he could use a hundred.
The Limitless Primordial Universe Star Scripture had no ceiling. Every new Star Node didn’t just increase his mana pool—it multiplied his combat versatility exponentially.
Dexter opened his eyes, a quiet, satisfied smile settling on his face.
"Fascinating," he murmured.
That wasn’t all, he noticed his injuries has all healed and when he checked them, he saw 42 rows of crimson marks on his chest.
’I killed 42 monsters yesterday, is this... the Asura Slaughter technique?’
Dexter frowned. The mark looked wierd and bloody but strangely bewitching.
He could also see his muscles and physique had improved drastically.
He had reached the 10 kills of the Asura technique. The next stage is 100kill which would take his body to the Superhuman realm.
Just his body skin and flesh alone had advanced but there wasn’t much improvement. Simply because alredy possess a body strengthening technique but it wouldn’t be bad mixing the two together.
Then his physique would be even more terrifying!
It was time to cook.
Dexter moved through the morning routine like he done time over again.
He washed his hands, tied his apron, and began preparing breakfast.
He used his heaven and earth herbs as ingredients along with the diamond rice and even went all out and produced his Sun Alcohol with it, cooking them a perfect meal.
By 6:50 AM, the meal was complete. A Grade-4 Arcane meal was ready for them.
He turned back but didn’t see Lyra waiting in the kitchen’s entrance.
Usually, she would hover near the kitchen doorway while he cooked, her eyes tracking every movement.
Today, she hadn’t come near the kitchen.
’This girl might hold grudges even more than I thought.’
He set the dining table and listened for movement in the hallway.
The girls were already awake. He could hear them shuffling through their morning routine, bathroom doors opening and closing, the sound of running water, the soft rustle of clothes being changed.
One by one, they emerged.
Mira came first, using her spectral arms to wheel herself to the dining table. She was expressionless as usual, didn’t look at Dexter and simply positioned herself at her usual spot and waited.
Selene came next, her bare feet padding softly against the floor. She stopped eating slippers in the house when she noticed she could feel vibration easily without them.
She found her chair by memory and echolocation, sat down gracefully, and placed her hands in her lap.
She didn’t look at Dexter either but for a completely different reason
Lyra appeared last. She walked to the table without a word, sat down, and picked up her spoon.
Her dark eyes were fixed on her bowl. Her AI glasses sat on her nose, their tiny lights blinking.
"Good morning,"she said.
It was devoid of the soft, melodic warmth that usually accompanied her telepathic greetings.
She didn’t project the words into his mind, instead, she typed on her phone and it spoke them aloud.
Dexter smirked at her antics to appear cold and aloof.
Dexter served the meal in silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 139 | Trying For Forgiveness
paragraphs: The four of them ate in suffocating quiet.
Just the clinking of spoons against the plate could be heard in the dining room.
Dexter cleared the table when they finished and started tk washed the dishes, listening to the girls disperse throughout the house.
Mira’s wheelchair rolled to the living room window. Selene’s went to the backyard while Lyra’s footsteps retreated to the bedroom.
’I can’t possibly explain to them that I need to kill monsters to increase my cultivation and upgrade my system.’
Dexter sighed as he stood at the kitchen sink, washing the last plate.
’I should probably speak to Lyra first.’
But she hadn’t given him the space to approach her. Every time he came near, she found a reason to leave.
’We’re staying in the same house. She will eventually let it go.’
Dexter shrugged, dried his hands, and went to his room.
He sat on his bed and began cultivating.
The mana flowed into him effortlessly as the ten Star Nodes greedily sucked energy from the surrounding.
But his mind wasn’t truly on cultivation. A few hours into cultivation—
"Ding-a-ling-a-ling!"
His alarm rang.
Dexter opened his eyes and checked the time.

It was the alarm he had set for Mira’s daily physical therapy session, the massage routine designed to stretch her muscles, prevent atrophy, and maintain what little function remained in her paralyzed limbs.
Especially for now that she was healing.
’I should move to the next style. Now.’
He stood up, stretched his legs, and headed to the living room.
Mira was at the window, her eyes closed, her spectral arms retracted.
She was cultivating deeply, her Star Nodes pulling in mana with speed.
Dexter walked over and stood behind her wheelchair.
"It’s time for your massage," he said.
"Hm."
Mira didn’t open her eyes, still indifferent as ever and didn’t respond.
Dexter didn’t wait, to ask for permission he had learned that asking Mira for permission only gave her an opportunity to refuse.
Dexter wheeled Mira to the bedroom. She didn’t like the other girls watching as her pride couldn’t bear being vulnerable in front of the other girls.

That was why she preferred to be taken care of by Dexter, rather than the two girls. She might not be able to do anything right now, but she still possess her pride and wasn’t willing to let it fall before the other girls.
Moreover, Dexter was a stranger to her back then so it didn’t count.
Lyra was already in the bedroom, sitting cross-legged on her bed with the ancient beast egg cradled in her lap.
She had taken a particular liking to the egg, always volunteering to cultivate with it despite not being the strongest cultivator among them.
When she saw Dexter wheel Mira through the doorway, she immediately understood what was about to happen. Without a word, she picked up the egg, stood, and left the room.
Dexter closed the door behind her.
He carried Mira from the wheelchair and placed her softly on the bed.
He removed her outer clothing, leaving her in just a sports bra and cotton briefs.
They had done this routine enough times now that Mira’s embarrassment had reduced considerably, though the faint pink tinge on her ears never quite disappeared.
Dexter, however, was a different story. No matter how many times he performed this ritual, his heart always raced.
He inhaled deeply and retrieved the nearly empty bottle of massage oil from the nightstand.
Pouring a small pool of oil into his palm, he warmed it between his hands and began.
The 36-Style Massage Technique activated instinctively, channeling precise threads of mana through his fingertips as he worked.
He started with her fingers, then her hands, her wrists, her forearms.
He moved up to her shoulders, kneading the atrophied muscles with careful, methodical pressure. Her neck followed, then her upper back, his thumbs working the tight bands of tissue along her spine.
He turned his attention to her legs. Starting at her toes, he stretched each one gently, then worked upward her calves, knees and thighs.
He stopped just below the junction of her thighs and waist, then gently turned her over.
The front of her body received the same careful treatment, her abdomen, her collarbones, her arms.
The oil seeped into her pores, carrying its restorative properties deep into her tissue.
When the massage was complete, Dexter lifted her carefully and carried her to the bathroom.
He used warm water and a soft cloth to clean the massage oil from her skin, patting her dry with a fresh towel the took he back to the room.
Then he dressed her in clean clothes.
Mira immediately closed her eyes and resumed cultivating.
She didn’t say a word throughout the entire process—not during the massage, not during the bath, nor after.
Dexter glanced her and smirked. "I’d thought I’d never see the day the Crimson Valkyrie would be silent."
Mira opened her eye and glanced at him. "Righteous idiot." Then she closed her eyes and ignored him.
Dexter almost choked on his own spit. ’Why was this girl such a savage?’
"Hmph!" He snorted and took her to the sitting room, close to the window.
Lyra was on the couch, the beast egg back on her lap.
Dexter glanced at her and an idea came to him.
He went to the kitchen and began preparing tea. He went all out, brewed a Grade-4 Arcane tea using the premium leaves and also mixed it with his premium alcohol.
He then retrieved the Celestial Moon Pastries from his storage ring.
He arranged them on small plates and paired each with a cup of the Grade-4 tea.
Mira first.
He carried a cup of tea and three pastries to Mira.
"I don’t want," she said flatly, without opening her eyes.
Dexter smiled. "Then toss it away if you don’t want."
Mira frowned and glanced at him. "Are you trying to bully me?"
Dexter grinned brilliantly. "Then stand up for yourself."
Mira’s eyes brow rose at the clever retort. "Hmph! Glib tongue."
She ignored him.
Dexter chuckled and placed the tea before her. She didn’t summon her specter arm to toss it which was quite the achievement.
Next, Lyra.
Dexter carried a cup of tea and four pastries instead of two.
He set the tea and pastries on the small stool directly in front of her.
Lyra opened one eye. She glanced at Dexter, then she closed her eye again, ignoring both him and the food.
Dexter chuckled softly but didn’t press. He placed the items where she could reach them and moved on.
Finally, Selene.
She was in the backyard, sitting on the old hanging swing chair that creaked softly.
Her hands rested on her knees, palms upward, and faint wisps of cold mana drifted around her like morning mist.
Dexter walked over and placed two pastries and a cup of tea on the empty space beside her swing.
Selene’s head turned toward him without opening her eyes. Through her echolocation, she could perceive his outline which was a blazing wild fire in the dark world.
"This is your cultivation pastry," Dexter said quietly. "It will help improve your cultivation speed. Try it."
Selene was silent for a moment. Then she muttered softly, "Thank you."
Dexter smiled. At least one of the three girls had thanked him today.
He turned to leave, but paused when Selene’s mouth opened slightly—as if she wanted to say something more. She hesitated, her lips parting and then closing.
The moment stretched.
Dexter raised an eyebrow but didn’t push. She would say it when she was ready. He simply nodded and walked back inside.

They had done this routine enough times now that Mira’s embarrassment had reduced considerably, though the faint pink tinge on her ears never quite disappeared.
Dexter, however, was a different story.
No matter how many times he performed this ritual, his heart always raced.
He inhaled deeply and retrieved the nearly empty bottle of massage oil from the nightstand.
Pouring a small pool of oil into his palm, he warmed it between his hands and began.
The 36-Style Massage Technique activated instinctively, channeling precise threads of mana through his fingertips as he worked.
He started with her fingers, then her hands, her wrists, her forearms.
He moved up to her shoulders, kneading the atrophied muscles with careful, methodical pressure.
Her neck followed, then her upper back, his thumbs working the tight bands of tissue along her spine.
He turned his attention to her legs.
Starting at her toes, he stretched each one gently, then worked upward her calves, knees and thighs.
He stopped just below the junction of her thighs and waist, then gently turned her over.
The front of her body received the same careful treatment, her abdomen, her collarbones, her arms.
The oil seeped into her pores, carrying its restorative properties deep into her tissue.
When the massage was complete, Dexter lifted her carefully and carried her to the bathroom.
He used warm water and a soft cloth to clean the massage oil from her skin, patting her dry with a fresh towel the took he back to the room.
Then he dressed her in clean clothes.
Mira immediately closed her eyes and resumed cultivating.
She didn’t say a word throughout the entire process—not during the massage, not during the bath, nor after.
Dexter glanced her and smirked.
"I’d thought I’d never see the day the Crimson Valkyrie would be silent."
Mira opened her eye and glanced at him.
"Righteous idiot." Then she closed her eyes and ignored him.
Dexter almost choked on his own spit. ’Why was this girl such a savage?’
"Hmph!" He snorted and took her to the sitting room, close to the window.
Lyra was on the couch, the beast egg back on her lap.
Dexter glanced at her and an idea came to him.
He went to the kitchen and began preparing tea.
He went all out, brewed a Grade-4 Arcane tea using the premium leaves and also mixed it with his premium alcohol.
He then retrieved the Celestial Moon Pastries from his storage ring.
He arranged them on small plates and paired each with a cup of the Grade-4 tea.
Mira first.
He carried a cup of tea and three pastries to Mira.
"I don’t want," she said flatly, without opening her eyes.
Dexter smiled.
"Then toss it away if you don’t want."
Mira frowned and glanced at him.
"Are you trying to bully me?"
Dexter grinned brilliantly.
"Then stand up for yourself."
Mira’s eyes brow rose at the clever retort.
"Hmph!
Glib tongue."
She ignored him.
Dexter chuckled and placed the tea before her.
She didn’t summon her specter arm to toss it which was quite the achievement.
Next, Lyra.
Dexter carried a cup of tea and four pastries instead of two.
He set the tea and pastries on the small stool directly in front of her.
Lyra opened one eye.
She glanced at Dexter, then she closed her eye again, ignoring both him and the food.
Dexter chuckled softly but didn’t press.
He placed the items where she could reach them and moved on.
Finally, Selene.
She was in the backyard, sitting on the old hanging swing chair that creaked softly.
Her hands rested on her knees, palms upward, and faint wisps of cold mana drifted around her like morning mist.
Dexter walked over and placed two pastries and a cup of tea on the empty space beside her swing.
Selene’s head turned toward him without opening her eyes.
Through her echolocation, she could perceive his outline which was a blazing wild fire in the dark world.
"This is your cultivation pastry," Dexter said quietly.
"It will help improve your cultivation speed.
Try it."
Selene was silent for a moment.
Then she muttered softly, "Thank you."
Dexter smiled.
At least one of the three girls had thanked him today.
He turned to leave, but paused when Selene’s mouth opened slightly—as if she wanted to say something more.
She hesitated, her lips parting and then closing.
The moment stretched.
Dexter raised an eyebrow but didn’t push.
She would say it when she was ready.
He simply nodded and walked back inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 140 | Lyra + Food + Food = Forgiveness!
paragraphs: Dexter loaded the clean laundry into the heater and activated the drying cycle.
"Beep!"
The machine hummed to life as the clothes started to tumble.
As he turned to check the cycle, he saw Lyra walking past him.
She was carrying an empty plate, the one he had give her with pastries in it.
But currently, it was empty and she headed toward the kitchen sink.
She placed it in the sink without looking at him, then turned and walked back past him again.
Suddenly, a soft voice whispered in his mind like a mosquito’s whine.
’The pastries were good.’
Dexter’s eyebrows raised in surprise and he turned to look at her face.
The anger and coldness which was on her face all morning had already melted away.
The pastries and the Grade-3 Arcane tea seemed to haves worked.
Dexter smiled.
’They say the way to a man’s heart is through his stomach,’he thought. ’But whoever said that clearly never met Lyra.’
"So you’re finally talking to me," Dexter said in a light tone as he teased.
Lyra’s body stiffened. She blinked, then immediately turned to rush back to the living room,
"Wait," Dexter called out.
She stopped but didn’t turn around.

Dexter scratched the back of his head awkwardly. "I know you’re still angry. And I’m sorry for worrying you. I know you didn’t want me to leave for the monster outbreak yesterday." He paused, choosing his words carefully. "But I had to go. Not just for the Association—I had personal reasons too. If I don’t grow stronger, I won’t be able to protect us. And the resources I need to grow stronger... I can only get them by fighting."
Lyra stood motionless with her back turned to him. Several long seconds passed.
Then, her soft, melodic voice echoed inside his mind.
’I know.’
Dexter blinked, frowning slightly. "So why are you still angry?"
Lyra remained silent for a while as her fist clenched tightly. Her tone thick with accusation as she spoke.
’You promised to come back safely. But you came back covered in blood instead. You broke your promise.’
Dexter was momentarily stunned.
’That was why she was angry?’
She wasn’t mad that he had chosen the Hero Association over staying home.
She was mad because he had ’promised’ to come back safely, and he hadn’t.
He had broken his word. And to Lyra, who had already been abandoned by everyone she had ever depended on, a broken promise was just as bad as a betrayal.
’And Selene almost died. If you hadn’t come back when you did...’
Dexter remained silent. She was right of course.
He had promised to come back safely, and he hadn’t. And in his excitement and urgency, he had forgotten to inject Selene’s suppressant serum before leaving.
Both failures were his. Both were avoidable. And both had been witnessed by three women who had already lost everything once and couldn’t bear to lose again.
Lyra shook her head, her expression closing off again. ’Forget it. It doesn’t matter.’
She turned to leave.
"It matters a lot."
Dexter’s voice was quiet but firm. Lyra stopped.
"It matters a lot, Lyra," he took a step closer.
"I can’t change what happened. But I can tell you that I’m sorry and I promise to keep my promise to you. Next time, I will come back safely."
Lyra stood frozen for a long moment.
Then, slowly, her shoulders dropped. The rigid tension in her spine softened. She turned her head slightly, just enough to glance at him from the corner of her eye.
’Promise?’ her mental voice asked. It was small, stripped of all its usual composure, sounding almost childlike in its vulnerability.
Dexter nodded as he thumped his chest. "Promise."
She turned even more as she faced Dexter and stared into his eyes.
There was silence for a few seconds and then Lyra lips curled up to a small smile.
Her dark soul-consuming eyes started to light up as she returned to the usual expression. She blinked and stared at Dexter.
Dexter immediately knew she had forgiven him and when he saw her expectant gaze.
Dexter couldn’t help it. He laughed.
He flipped his right hand, and golden light flashed as four Celestial Moon Pastries materialized in his palm.
He had planned to give her two, but seeing the look in her eyes, he added two more.
Lyra’s eyes widened as her pupils dilated.
Her mouth fell open slightly, and for a moment, she looked like a child who had just been handed the keys to a candy store.
In a flash, she reached out and took the pastries from his hand with both hands, cradling them against her chest like precious treasures.
Then, without another word, she turned and practically ’skipped’ away down the hallway,
’Thank you!’ her siren voice echoed in his mind.
Dexter chuckled as he watched her disappear around the corner. He shook his head, still smiling.
He had known Lyra wouldn’t stay mad at him for long. She was a foodie through and through.
’Jasmine was like that too,’ a thought surfaced unbidden in his mind.
The name hit him like a soft punch to the chest.
Jasmine Constance. His ex-girlfriend.
Another foodie with an almost bottomless appetite and a smile that could light up a room.
The parallels between Jasmine and Lyra were uncanny—both quiet, both emotionally guarded, both absolutely ravenous when it came to exceptional food.
A warm, bittersweet feeling bloomed in Dexter’s chest. The memories of Jasmine—both the good and the painful—rose to the surface of his mind like bubbles in still water.
He let them linger for a moment, acknowledging them without drowning in them.
Then, deliberately, he pushed them to the back of his mind.
He wasn’t going to think about Jasmine. Not now. Not when he had three wives who needed him. Dwelling on the past would only complicate the present, and the present was already complicated enough.
He turned back to the drying machine and checked the cycle.

chapters.title: Chapter 141 | Holding A Grudge
paragraphs: That left Mira.
Lyra was handled. Selene had never truly been angry to begin with, just embarrassed about the midnight clinging incident. But Mira was a different creature entirely.
Dexter leaned against the kitchen counter, rubbing his jaw in thought. Mira was... complicated.
One moment she was laughing in the rain, the next she was glaring at him. He couldn’t tell when she was genuinely angry versus when she was simply maintaining her pride.
He knew one thing for certain: she liked rain.
He glanced out the kitchen window. The sky was clear. Pale blue, not a cloud in sight. No indication of rain anytime soon.
So that plan was out.
He needed another approach. But what?
He stood there for a long time, staring out the window, his mind turning over possibilities.

He thought about the wheelchair incident. He had bought her a $120,000 neural-linked wheelchair, and she had been furious. Not because the gift was unwelcome, but because she liked the routine. She liked ’him’ taking care of her and she had rejected it because the machine wasn’t him.
Dexter massaged his brows as a headache started to form.
The drying machine beeped, signaling the end of its cycle. Dexter pushed off the counter and began folding the warm laundry.
[Ding!]
[Investment Return Detected: Improved Lyra’s Emotional State & Reduced Shadow Corruption]
[Multiplier: 100x]
[Rewards Granted:]
1. Grade-3 Divine Peak Recovery Pill ×1
2. 10 kg Premium Diamond Spirit Rice
Dexter didn’t even check the rewards fully. His attention was caught by two words in the notification: Reduced Shadow Corruption.
He frowned, pulling up Lyra’s status panel. His eyes widened in shock.

Her shadow corruption, which he had diligently reduced to a mere 1% through weeks of spiritual meals, had somehow skyrocketed to 10%. According to the system, his recent actions had reduced it back down to 5%, but the damage had already been done.
’How did it increase so fast?’
Then, it hit him. She had been angry at him. She had spent almost twenty-four hours furious, radiating dark, gloomy, and resentful emotions.
Because Lyra was finally starting to experience genuine emotions again after years of numbness, her negative feelings directly fueled her Shadow Manipulation talent.
And when those negative emotions spiraled, the shadow mana turned inward, corrupting her physical cells.

Dexter broke into a cold sweat. If just one day of anger had increased the corruption by 10%, it would only take ten days of sustained misery for the corruption to reach 100%. At 100%, her body would collapse and become a permanent portal to the Shadow Realm, unleashing horrific monsters into the physical world and killing her instantly.

He had never considered that emotional distress could be so lethal to her. All this time, she had been living in a state of emotional numbness, which was why the corruption had remained stagnant. Now that she was healing and feeling again, her anger was a ticking time bomb.

Dexter rubbed his forehead, realizing he would have to check the girls’ status panels every single day to prevent any unexpected surprises. If he had missed this, Lyra could have died without him even realizing why.

He looked at the Grade-3 Divine Peak Recovery Pill. Just like the one he received for Selene, it could temporarily heal all injuries and return her to her peak Ultra Realm form for six hours, but at the cost of permanently worsening her injuries afterward.

He firmly decided not to give the girls these pills. It was better to take the long, slow road to recovery than to let them risk everything for six hours of fleeting normalcy. He secured the pill deep within his storage ring, making a mental note to never reveal their existence to the girls unless absolutely necessary.

Lunch was a quiet affair, though noticeably lighter than the morning. Lyra sat at the table, happily eating her meal with one hand while cradling the ancient beast egg in her other arm. She finished six massive portions in under ten minutes.
Dexter shook his head in amazement.
’Where does all that food go?’ he thought, baffled. ’Is she secretly feeding the entire Shadow Realm?’
As she stood up to leave, his eyes inadvertently dropped to her chest. He blinked. Her chest had grown even larger since she started eating his arcane meals.
He quickly averted his gaze before she could catch him staring.
’Thank you,’ Lyra’s sweet voice chimed in his mind, her mood completely restored. She skipped out of the kitchen, leaving Mira and Selene to eat in silence before they too returned to cultivating.

As for the Hero Association’s message, Dexter decided to delay his response until tomorrow. The girls were still highly sensitive about anything related to dungeon outbreaks, and he didn’t want to trigger their trauma by announcing he had to report to the Association today. He would handle it in the morning.
Evening came, and after dinner, Dexter suddenly grabbed Mira’s wheelchair and began wheeling her toward the bedroom.
Mira squinted her eyes. "What do you want?"
Dexter prepared the bed and pulled out the massage oil. "I’ve decided to increase the duration of your massage therapy to twice a day now. The results should accelerate with this routine."
Mira’s face remained indifferent, but her crimson eyes narrowed. "Are you just looking for an excuse to touch my body?"
Dexter rolled his eyes. "Yes, Mira. I desperately wish to touch your supple skin. Please, let me have my way with you."
Mira glanced at him from the corner of her eye. "Hmph!"
She harrumphed coldly and closed her eyes, submitting to the massage without further protest.
Dexter took her to the bed and began the 36-Style Massage Technique. Halfway through, as he worked on the muscles below her waist, he decided to test the waters.
"So, Lyra has forgiven me," he said casually.
Mira said nothing.
Dexter blinked, waiting for a sharp retort, but none came. "When are you going to let it go?"
Still nothing.
"If you don’t say anything, I will stop the massage," he threatened lightly.
Mira’s head shifted slightly. Despite her silence, he knew she loved the massage and the relief it brought her.
"Do what you want," Mira replied coldly.
Dexter sighed and resumed the massage. He couldn’t actually use her physical recovery as leverage to force her forgiveness. That would be cruel.

When he was done, he carried her to the bathroom, cleaned the oil off her body, and dressed her in her pajamas. Specifically, he dressed her in the flower-print pajamas he had bought for her—the ones she absolutely despised.
Instead of returning her to her wheelchair, however, he locked the wheels and crossed his arms in front of her.
Mira glanced at him suspiciously. "What do you want to do now?"
Dexter blinked innocently. "Why do you think I want to do anything?"
Mira sneered. "You are very devious. Of course you want to do something. What is it?"
Dexter smirked. "Alright, since you know I’m devious... you are not leaving this bathroom until you forgive me."
Mira frowned, her crimson eyes blazing. Then, without a word, she simply closed her eyes and started cultivating.
Dexter stood there, utterly stunned. She would rather cultivate in the bathroom than say the words ’I forgive you’. She truly held a grudge of iron.
He stood there patiently for almost fifteen minutes. Finally, Mira opened her eyes, her brows furrowed in irritation.
"This is bullying," she snapped. "If people find out you are bullying your crippled wife in the bathroom, do you know what they will say?"
Dexter grinned. "Luckily, there’s no one here to find out."
Mira’s lips curled into a dangerous smile. "I can simply scream ’pervert,’ and the whole neighborhood will come rushing in, right?"
Dexter blinked, momentarily stunned, before his grin widened. "I placed a Grade-6 formation matrix around the house. Unless I wish it, no one below the Transcendent Realm can come in."
Mira was startled. ’A formation?’ This guy actually possessed the connections to purchase a barrier formation capable of repelling Transcendent experts?
She smirked, refusing to be outplayed. "What about Selene and Lyra? They’re in the house. They’d think you’re doing something to me."
"Hm," Dexter hummed thoughtfully. "Let them think that. They’d probably just assume it’s a normal activity between husband and wife."
Mira glared at him, her face flushing slightly. "Pervert! Who is doing husband-and-wife activities with you!?"
She looked away, her jaw tight. Dexter laughed and waited.
He could see the battle happening behind her eyes—her stubborn pride fighting against the absurd, somewhat amusing reality of being held hostage in the bathroom over a grudge.
Finally, she let out a sharp exhale. "Fine! I’ve forgiven you. Happy?"
Dexter smiled brilliantly and clapped his hands together. "See? That was so simple!"
He laughed out loud as he unlocked her wheelchair, spinning her around and wheeling her out of the bathroom toward the bedroom.
Behind him, Mira muttered under her breath, "Devious bastard."

"What do you want to do now?"
Dexter blinked innocently.
"Why do you think I want to do anything?"
Mira sneered.
"You are very devious.
Of course you want to do something.
What is it?"
Dexter smirked.
"Alright, since you know I’m devious... you are not leaving this bathroom until you forgive me."
Mira frowned, her crimson eyes blazing.
Then, without a word, she simply closed her eyes and started cultivating.
Dexter stood there, utterly stunned.
She would rather cultivate in the bathroom than say the words ’I forgive you’.
She truly held a grudge of iron.
He stood there patiently for almost fifteen minutes.
Finally, Mira opened her eyes, her brows furrowed in irritation.
"This is bullying," she snapped.
"If people find out you are bullying your crippled wife in the bathroom, do you know what they will say?"
Dexter grinned.
"Luckily, there’s no one here to find out."
Mira’s lips curled into a dangerous smile.
"I can simply scream ’pervert,’ and the whole neighborhood will come rushing in, right?"
Dexter blinked, momentarily stunned, before his grin widened.
"I placed a Grade-6 formation matrix around the house.
Unless I wish it, no one below the Transcendent Realm can come in."
Mira was startled. ’A formation?’ This guy actually possessed the connections to purchase a barrier formation capable of repelling Transcendent experts?
She smirked, refusing to be outplayed.
"What about Selene and Lyra?
They’re in the house.
They’d think you’re doing something to me."
"Hm," Dexter hummed thoughtfully.
"Let them think that.
They’d probably just assume it’s a normal activity between husband and wife."
Mira glared at him, her face flushing slightly.
"Pervert!
Who is doing husband-and-wife activities with you!?"
She looked away, her jaw tight.
Dexter laughed and waited.
He could see the battle happening behind her eyes—her stubborn pride fighting against the absurd, somewhat amusing reality of being held hostage in the bathroom over a grudge.
Finally, she let out a sharp exhale.
"Fine!
I’ve forgiven you.
Happy?"
Dexter smiled brilliantly and clapped his hands together.
"See?
That was so simple!"
He laughed out loud as he unlocked her wheelchair, spinning her around and wheeling her out of the bathroom toward the bedroom.
Behind him, Mira muttered under her breath, "Devious bastard."

chapters.title: Chapter 142 | Eccentric Old Lady Lucy
paragraphs: The next morning, Dexter sorted through his routine.
He woke early, cooked breakfast for the girls, took care of Mira’s morning needs, and served the meal at the dining table.
If it were another person, they would have gotten tired a long while ago. Even a good person would have definitely complained after a while.

But Dexter was happy to do these chores everyday. Who knows if he’s starting to develop something for the girls, or maybe it’s purely transactional and he looked forward to the investment returns from the system.
Halfway through breakfast, he suddenly asked, "How would you all feel about renovating the house?"
He leaned back in his chair. "I’ve saved up quite a bit of money. I think it’s about time we fixed this place up properly."
Lyra and Selene both looked up from their meals.
Mira, meanwhile, remained completely focused on her breakfast.
She calmly used her Spectral Arms to scoop food from her plate, eating without reacting as though Dexter hadn’t said anything.
Selene glanced around the house before speaking softly. "...I don’t think there’s anything wrong with it."
Lyra nodded in agreement. ’...Mm.’
Dexter pursed his lips. He understood their reluctance. The idea of strangers stomping and entering the house, disturbing their peace, they probably hated it.
Just like when those people came in to arrange the new beds, they hated it. Now if others came once more, especially since they would take more time during the repair, they might hate ie even more.
But the house needed work.
The wallpaper in several rooms had peeled away, exposing bare plaster.
The bathroom wall had cracked during Mira’s outbreak, and the mirror had shattered.
The front porch gate was rusted and the swing chair in the backyard was also rusty and its wooden slats splintering.
The kitchen roof had developed a slow leak that dripped into a bucket he had strategically placed during the last rainstorm.
And the exterior walls which had been originally painted a clean cream color had faded to a muddy, dull brown that made the bungalow look abandoned.
The Hero Association had repaired the structural damage from the monster outbreak, and hadn’t bothered with rest.
Dexter nodded slowly. "Okay. I won’t call anyone for renovations. I guess I’ll have to do it myself."
Selene slowly nodded. Lyra blinked her eyes glanced curiously at Dexter and then nodded before returning her attention to her food.
Still, Mira still hadn’t said anything.
Dexter shrugged, a faint smile tugging on his lips n at his lips as he recalled the events of the previous night.
After breakfast, the girls retreated to their bedroom to cultivate, arranging themselves in a loose circle around the ancient beast egg, which sat at the center like a shrine.
They cultivated in unison. The Grand Cosmos Scripture activated simultaneously in three bodies, each one drawing mana through their awakened Star Nodes rather than their shattered meridians.
Mana surged toward the bungalow from every direction, invisible currents of energy converging on the small house like rivers feeding into a lake.
The Mana Hurricane phenomenon began again.
The ancient beast egg absorbed its share of the mana, its surface glowing faintly with a warm, golden pulse that had grown steadily brighter over the past few days.
The three girls absorbed their own mana simultaneously, their Star Nodes drinking greedily from the hurricane they had created.
Dexter stood in the kitchen, staring at the notification on his Type-3 Arcane phone. It was another message from the Hero Association—a reminder this time.
> ’[Reminder: Promotion Processing]’

> Hero Dexter Ashford, this is a second notification regarding your approved promotion. You are required to report to your nearest Hero Association branch within twenty-four hours to complete your promotion procedures.
> Failure to report may result in suspension of your hero license and associated benefits.
> Please confirm your intended arrival time.
’Suspension? Aren’t this guys ruthless?’
Dexter frowned and then pocketed the phone.
"Will go later."
For now, he needed to stay home, partly to keep an eye on the girls after yesterday’s near-disaster with Selene, and partly because he wasn’t ready to leave them again so soon after reconciling.
He finished washing the breakfast dishes, dried them, and placed them in the cabinet.

He wiped down the counter, swept the kitchen floor, and checked the leak in the kitchen ceiling and it was actually still dripping slowly into the bucket. He made a mental note to fix it as part of his renovation plan.
Then he gathered the trash, food scraps, packaging, the empty syringe from the empty serum he’d used on Selene—and carried the dustbin outside to the curb.
The morning air was cool and fresh. The street was quiet, most of the neighbors already at work.
A few birds chirped from the power lines.
The sunlight was pale but pleasant, casting long shadows from the houses across the street.
Dexter placed the dirt in the trash can ans as Dexter was about to turn back toward his gate, his eyes caught movement across the road.
Old Lady Lucy.
The old lady who lives in the house directly opposite his bungalow.
Her gate was open, and she was tending to her front yard, mowing the small patch of grass with a manual push mower.
Dexter had greeted her once before and she had responded with a curt nod and immediately returned to her gardening without a word.
She was eccentric—sometimes acknowledging him, other times pretending he didn’t exist. He had learned not to take it personally.
This morning, he decided not to greet her. Better to avoid the awkwardness of being ignored.
He turned toward his gate.
Then, from the corner of his eye, he saw movement. The old woman had stopped gardening.
She was looking directly at him.
Then, to his surprise...
She raised a hand and waved.
Dexter blinked.
The old woman nodded gently before waving again.
Surprised, Dexter raised his own hand and waved back.
A faint smile spread across the old woman’s wrinkled face. She slowly lifted a finger and curled it twice, gesturing for him to come over.
Dexter paused.
His gaze lingered on the white-haired old woman standing quietly among the colorful flowers.
Should I go?

chapters.title: Chapter 143 | Business Shaping Up
paragraphs: ’Should I go?’
Dexter hesitated for several seconds before shaking his head.
’Well... it won’t hurt to find out.’
Dexter crossed the street toward the old woman’s gate.
She was a small, white-haired woman with her pale blue eyes. Up close, she looked to be in her seventies, but her posture was straight and she behaved younger than her age.
"You must be Dexter," the old woman said, smiling warmly. "I’m Lucy."
"Good morning, you must be Old Lady Lucy" Dexter replied politely.
"Ah, Seems like Tessa has told you about me," Lucy said, her eyes crinkling at the corners.
"How are you finding the neighborhood? Hope there’s no problem like the previous time?"
Dexter shook his head. "Apart from the monster outbreak, everything’s been fine."
Lucy nodded thoughtfully. "All right. These things happen." She paused, wiping her hands on her apron. "Oh, Tessa informed me that you’re an Arcane Chef. Is that true?"
Dexter raised an eyebrow, glancing at the old woman. He slowly nodded. "Yes. I am."
Lucy’s smile widened. "Tessa also said you two are planning to go into business together. Selling food at her father’s bakery."
She chuckled softly. "It’s a really nice idea, actually. A really nice idea."
Dexter frowned slightly.

Tessa had only mentioned the business idea once. He had assumed she was joking. But it seemed she was serious. And now that the old woman across the street knew about it, the idea had clearly gained momentum.
Moreover, Dexter had to admit he needed a platform. He couldn’t just set up a stall on a random street corner and start selling Arcane meals.
The bakery was an already established business with loyal customer base, and a reputation in the neighborhood. It was the perfect testing ground.
"When are you starting?" Lucy asked, her pale blue eyes curious.
Dexter rubbed the back of his neck. "I plan on doing the business, but not today. Definitely this week, but not today."
Lucy nodded. "Tessa hasn’t stopped praising your cooking," she said, laughing softly. "Now you’ve made me curious. I wonder just how delicious your food really is."
Dexter chuckled. "When we finally open, I’ll prepare a portion for you. My treat. You’ll be the first customer.
Lucy’s eyes softened, a gentle warmth replacing her sharp eyes. "Thank you, Dexter. It’s been a long time since someone spoiled this old woman."
Dexter smiled. "You’re welcome."
After exchanging another goodbye, he turned and walked back toward his house.
As he pushed it open, a familiar voice drifted down from above.
"Hey, Dexter."
He looked up. Tessa was sitting on the wall again, her red hair tied back with a strip of cloth as her green eyes brightened with mischief.
Dexter rolled his eyes. "You’re in trouble, Tessa."
Tessa blinked widened, her freckled face expressing false innocence. "What did I do this time?"
Dexter furrowed his brows. "First of all, today’s Wednesday. Why aren’t you in school this morning? And don’t tell me you’re on a break."
Tessa’s eyes rolled around rapidly and then her eyes lit up ws she spoke.
"Um, we were supposed to go for an excursion today, but my dad doesn’t have money to pay for such an expensive excursion. So I decided to stay at home." She smiled brightly.
Dexter stared at her for a long moment, then nodded. "That’s a believable excuse."
Tessa puffed out her cheeks indignantly. "It’s not an excuse. It’s the truth!"
Dexter rolled his eyes. He knew she wasn’t going to tell him the real reason, and he definitely knew she wasn’t going to school. He decided to drop the matter.
"Second," he said, turning to face her fully with his arms crossed. "You only told me about the idea of going into business together. You never told me you’d already implemented a full-blown plan."

Tessa’s smile widened into a grin. "Oh, I forgot to tell you." She swung her legs casually. "I wanted to tell you, but I didn’t know how to approach you after coming into your home the last time. I thought you might be angry that I entered without your permission."
Dexter remained silent for a moment, his expression unreadable.

Tessa, reading the disapproval on his face, scratched her head awkwardly. "Look, it’s actually a simple business plan," she continued quickly. "I feel we should test the waters by making twenty portions first. Twenty portions of whatever food you want to make. Then we see how the twenty portions go. If they sell well, we can decide whether to increase or reduce the daily portions for selling at the bakery."
Dexter uncrossed his arms. He considered the plan and felt it was feasible.
Twenty portions was a manageable number he could cook that in an hour to two hours with his Great Grandmaster Foodsmith skills.
And if each portion sold for even five thousand dollars. the same price the Akane Restaurant charged for a Grade-One meal—twenty portions would generate one hundred thousand dollars in a single day.
The numbers were insane!
And that was just ghe conservative estimate.
If his Grade-Two or Grade-Three meals commanded higher prices—and they should, given their vastly superior quality and taste the revenue could be even greater.
"Fine," Dexter said. "But we start small. Twenty portions. Grade-One meals only."
Tessa’s eyes lit up. "Really? You’re in?"
"I’m in."
Tessa practically bounced on the wall. "Yes! Okay, so when do we start? Tomorrow? Today? Right now?"
Dexter held up a hand. "Not today. I have somethings to do and certainly not tomorrow. Let’s start the day after. That gives me time to prepare ingredients and figure out the logistics."
Tessa nodded rapidly, her red ponytail bouncing. "Day after tomorrow. Got it. I’ll tell Dad to clear a space in the bakery for a food counter."
Dexter nodded. "Good."
Tessa nodded her head and then spoke. " I assume you don’t have containers to place the food in."
Dexter shook his head. "No, I plan on purchasing those at the market."
"We have a few," Tessa said, swinging her legs. "My dad bought extra this week. Maybe you can use some to pack the food inside."
Dexter pursed his lips, looking at her. After a moment, he shrugged. "Alright then. I assume you’ll be either at the bakery or at home?"
Tessa nodded her head like a chicken pecking grain. "Yep!"

Dexter glanced at her, a fleeting thought crossing his mind—why did she never have any friends over? She was always alone, on the wall, in the bakery, or playing chess with old Grandma Lucy. But it wasn’t any of his business.
He waved at her. "I’ll see you later."
He turned and walked back into his house.
After washing his hands, he changed into clean clothes, a dark shirt and joggers, and slipped on proper shoes.
He walked to the living room where Lyra was sprawled on the couch, the beast egg cradled in her lap.
"I’m heading out to get some things for the renovation," he announced.

"Selene, I’m heading out to purchase some things at the market."
She looked up from the swing, her echolocation mapping his outline. "...Okay."
Dexter nodded and headed back inside. He walked to the living room. Where Lyra was seated on the couch and Mira was at the window.
"I’m heading out."
Dexter said announces to then.
’Take care, Dexter,’Lyra’s soft, melodic voice echoed in his mind.
Dexter smiled at her. "I will."
Then he turned to face Mira.
Mira opened her eyes. She looked at him with a flat expression.
"Okay," she said. Then, without changing her expression, she added: "Tell the fourth wife we said ’hi’."
Dexter almost choked on his own spit. "Fourth wife? What fourth wife?"
Mira simply sneered, closed her eyes, and resumed cultivating.
Dexter felt Lyra’s gaze on him from the couch.
He turned and saw her looking up at him through her AI glasses, her dark eyes narrow with suspicion.
He coughed awkwardly. "Don’t mind her. She just likes stirring up trouble."
Lyra blinked and looked at him suspiciously before slowly nodding her head.
Dexter glared at Mira who sat there with that infuriating ghost of a smile on her lips as he opened the door and left.
Dexter took the Tier-6 car and drove out of the neighborhood. But he wasn’t actually heading to the supermarket.
He was going to the Hero Association.
Since he was heading to get somethings, he might as well finsh all his task today.l instead of postponing it till tomorrow.
The drive took about fifteen minutes.
The familiar fortress-like structure of the Hero Association Branch soon loomed into view. It was just as majestic and intimidating as the first time Rachel had brought him here.
He pulled up to the main gate and lowered his window.
"Identificarion Please?"
The guard leaned forward, scanning the golden identification card Dexter held out.
The guard’s posture changed instantly. He snapped to attention, his fist slamming against his chest in a sharp salute.
"Welcome, Mr. Dexter! Have a great day, sir!"
Dexter nodded politely, rolled up the window, and drove through the gate.
He parked in the visitor lot, killed the engine, and walked toward the administration center.

The main hall was as enormous as he remembered, hundreds of heroes moving through the place. He approached the reception counter, where a young woman with glasses and a professional smile sat behind a sleek terminal.
"I’m here for my promotion," Dexter said. "Dexter Ashford."
The receptionist offered him a courteous smile. "One moment, please."
She lowered her gaze and began typing rapidly on her terminal.
A few seconds passed. Then her expression changed slightly as her smile became more genuine and less forced.
She looked back up at Dexter.

"Mr. Dexter, we’ve been expecting you." She straightened in her chair. "You’ve been scheduled for the twentieth floor. Please take the elevator at the end of the corridor." She gestured toward a hallway on the left.
"Someone will be waiting to receive you."
"Thank you," Dexter said, keeping his expression neutral.
He walked down the indicated corridor and at the end of the corridor, a sleek elevator waited with its doors already open.
He stepped inside. The doors closed with a soft hiss and he pushed the button marked ’20’.
A few seconds later.
"Ding!"
The elevator chimed.
’Floor 20.’
The doors slid open.
The elevator doors opened on the twentieth floor, and Dexter stepped out into a wide, elegantly furnished corridor.

A middle-aged man was standing directly in front of the elevator, waiting. He was dressed in a sharp grey suit, his hair neatly combed, his posture straight and professional. He smiled warmly as Dexter stepped forward.
"Mr. Dexter?"
Dexter nodded.
The man immediately extended his hand. "It’s a pleasure to finally meet you. My name is Simon. I’m one of the administrative supervisors here."
Dexter shook his hand. "The pleasure is mine."
Simon’s smile widened. "Supervisor Stan has spoken very highly of you."
Dexter’s brows furrowed slightly as he searched his memory. Stan... then it clicked.
Supervisor Stan the senior official who had accompanied Rachel during the dungeon outbreak investigation and had quietly arranged for Dexter to receive a substantial payout.
"Ah, Supervisor Stan," Dexter said, nodding. "I remember him."
Simon gestured down the corridor. "Please follow me.
He led Dexter to a massive corner office nearby.
The room was impressive floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the entire Hero Association compound, a polished mahogany desk, leather chairs, and bookshelves.
Simon gestured for Dexter to sit. Dexter settled into a comfortable leather chair opposite the desk while Simon took his own seat on the other side.
Simon folded his hands on the desk and leaned forward slightly.

"First of all," he began, his tone formal but warm, "on behalf of the Hero Association, I’d like to sincerely thank you for your contribution during the monster outbreak at Stonebridge Market District."
Dexter gave a small nod. "It was my duty."

Simon continued. "When the dimensional gate first appeared, it was classified as an E-Rank Gate. However, after further investigation, we have officially upgraded the incident to a C-Rank Monster Outbreak."
He paused, letting the weight of that classification settle.

"Initially, we considered classifying it as a B-Rank outbreak. However, the total number of Ultra-Class monsters that emerged was fewer than ten. According to Hero Association regulations, that places the incident within the C-Rank category."
He slid a document across the desk. Dexter glanced at it—a detailed after-action report with his name, contribution summary, and combat assessment.
"Taking your performance into account," Simon said, "the Association has unanimously approved your promotion. You will be promoted from F-Rank directly to D-Rank Hero."
He paused again, a faint smile touching his lips.
"In addition... you will retain your Gold Privilege status."
Dexter’s eyebrows rose. "Since it’s a C rank outbreak which I participated in, should I not receive a C rank License?"

Simon nodded, clearly anticipating the question. "Ordinarily, yes. You would have received a C-Rank license, given that you participated in clearing a C-Rank outbreak. However, there’s a complication."
He leaned back in his chair.

"Your Gold Privilege is extremely valuable. It’s a status reserved for rookies whose evaluated potential places them in the top percentile of their registration cohort. If we promoted you directly to C-Rank, your privilege tier would automatically reset under Association regulations. You would lose your Gold status and revert to Iron Privilege until you rebuilt your record through additional C-Rank dungeon clears."
Simon spread his hands.

"We felt that would unduly penalize you and undervalue your actual combat ability. The board engaged in considerable discussion before reaching a consensus. It was decided that maintaining your Gold Privilege as a D-Rank Hero would serve you and the Association far better than a standard C-Rank license with Iron Privilege."
He tapped the document.

"A Gold D-Rank Hero receives significantly more benefits than an ordinary C-Rank Hero. Higher mission priority, better dungeon invitations, access to premium equipment stores, increased stipend, and priority for emergency response opportunities."
Dexter considered this for a moment. It doesn’t sound half bad. As long as the pay and benefits were better, he didn’t particularly care what letter was printed on his card.
He nodded. "That’s acceptable."
Simon smiled. "Good." He then asked, "May I have your current license card, please?"
Dexter reached into his pocket and produced his golden F-Rank Hero identification card. He handed it across the desk.
Simon examined the card briefly, then snapped his fingers. A side door opened, and a young, very pretty woman stepped into the office.
, She carried a tablet and smiled pleasantly.
"What can I do for you, Mr. Simon?"
