chapters.title: Chapter 145 | Rachel!
paragraphs: A side door opened, and a young and incredibly beautiful woman stepped in, carrying a tablet and smiled.
"What can I do for you, Mr. Simon?"
Simon glanced at her indifferently and handed her the card. "Please upgrade this card to D-Rank. Maintain Gold Privilege status."
"Certainly." The secretary took the card, smiled at Simon and then swayed her hips as she disappeared back through the side door.
Simon turned back to Dexter. "Now, regarding the monster corpses from the outbreak..."
Dexter’s ears perked up. This was the part he cared about most.

"Sadly," Simon continued, his expression apologetic, "most of the resources recovered from the monster corpses have already been allocated. The funds earned from processing the carcasses have been directed toward repairing and renovating the Stonebridge Market District, which suffered extensive structural damage during the outbreak."
Dexter’s expression remained neutral, though he rolled his eyes.
’He should be talking about the mall Aurora and the Six-arm goblin king had destroyed.’
"Also, some had been distributed towards falling heroes families and also civilians families too."
"However," Simon added, raising a finger, "you are not leaving empty-handed."
Dexter’s eyes lit up.

"The Association will transfer your combat bonus directly to your registered bank account. This includes your standard outbreak participation pay, your per-kill bounty for each verified monster you eliminated, and a special hazard bonus for engaging Ultra-Class opponents above your registered rank."
Simon consulted a document on his desk.

"Additionally, your monthly salary has been adjusted to reflect your new D-Rank status. Although you’ve already received this month’s salary at your previous rate, the difference will be calculated and added to your next payment. Your benefits package has also been upgraded—you now have access to the Association’s premium medical coverage, discounted equipment purchases, and priority dungeon scheduling."
Dexter nodded, mentally calculating.
Between the combat bonus, the kill bounties, the hazard pay, and the salary adjustment, he was looking at a substantial influx of dollars.
"One more thing," Simon said, leaning forward with a more personal expression.
"Yesterday, several heroes who participated in the outbreak came forward. They pointed out some things to my attention."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.

"They said you saved them," Simon said simply. "They said you are the reason they are still alive. Some of them wished to get your contact information—your phone number, your address. I informed them that I cannot distribute a hero’s personal information without their explicit permission."
He paused.
"But they were quite... adamant... about thanking you. One of them was the hero named Plasmatic. He was particularly insistent."
Simon smiled.
"So I would like your permission. May I share your contact information with the heroes who requested it? I will screen the list and only provide it to verified, licensed heroes with clean records."
Dexter thought about it for a moment.
Having contacts within the hero community could be useful—both for future dungeon raids and for potential emergencies.
Plasmatic, in particular, was someone worth staying in touch with. His long-range firepower complemented Dexter’s close-combat style perfectly.
"Yes," Dexter said. "You can give them only my number. But only those i fought with in the battlefield .
Simon nodded, making a note. "I’ll have the list sent to your phone by end of day. You’ll be able to review it and approve each individual."
Then Simon paused. He stroked his beard thoughtfully and leaned back in his chair.
"There was... one more person who asked for your contact information."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Who?"
Simon met his gaze as he looked at him strangely. There was an hint of surprise in his face as he spoke.
"Aurora."
Dexter frowned.
Aurora. The S-rank hero. The woman with the Sky Manipulation talent who had single-handedly killed the Six-Armed Goblin King and destroyed the dungeon core.
"Aurora?" Dexter repeated slowly.
Simon nodded with a smile, as if he couldn’t quite believe it himself.
Dexter’s frown deepened. "Why does she want my contact information?"
Simon shrugged, spreading his hands. "Beats me. I have no idea. She simply gave no reason and asked."
Dexter continued frowning. Aurora was an S-rank hero, one of the most powerful and influential young heroes in the entire city.
Having a connection with someone at that level could be good but it could also lead to complications.
And frankly, he hadn’t forgotten the way she had looked at him.
The cold, dismissive gaze didn’t exactly inspire a desire to exchange phone numbers.
Dexter shook his head slowly. "There’s no need for that."
Simon blinked. "I’m sorry?"
"I don’t want you to give out my contact information to Aurora," Dexter said flatly.
Simon stared at him with a stunned look.
"I’m certain I’m not hearing that right."
Simon said carefully, leaning forward. "I said... ’Aurora’ wants your contact information. Aurora. The current generation S-rank hero."
Dexter nodded calmly. "I know. I heard you. But I don’t want you to give out my contact information to her."
Simon sat back in his chair, genuinely stunned.
Aurora has always kept to herself. The fact that she had proactively, asked ’Dexter’s’ contact information meant she had deemed him important or worth her time.
And now Dexter was rejecting her.
It was really shocking.
Simon opened his mouth to say something but the look in Dexter’s eyes stopped him.
Simon closed his mouth. He nodded slowly, making a final note on his document.
"Very well," he said, his voice carefully neutral. "I will inform Hero Aurora that her request was declined."
Dexter nodded. "Thank you."
At that moment, the side door opened, and the secretary walked in.
She carried a small velvet tray with a sleek golden card resting on top, along with a folder of documents. She presented them to Simon with a professional smile.
"Your card and documents, sir."
Simon took the tray and turned to Dexter. He picked up the golden card and held it out across the desk.
"Here is your new license. D-Rank, Gold Privilege."
Dexter took the card. It was heavier than his previous one.

Simon also handed him the folder. "These are your upgraded documents, your new rights, responsibilities, codes of conduct, and operational guidelines. Please read through them carefully. As a D-Rank Hero, you represent the Hero Association in a more visible capacity than before. Your actions will be scrutinized more closely, and your responsibilities will increase accordingly."
Dexter nodded, tucking the card into his pocket and the folder under his arm. "All right."
Simon stood, extending his hand across the desk. Dexter rose and shook it.
"Take care, Mr. Dexter," Simon said. "And congratulations again."
Dexter nodded. "Take care as well."
Dexter left the office and walked down the corridor, toward the elevator.
The doors opened and he stepped inside and pressed the ground floor.
As the elevator descended, Dexter pulled out his new D-Rank card one more time, turning it over in his fingers. It looked more premium than last one.
"Ding!"
He slipped the card back into his pocket as the elevator chimed, announcing his arrival at the ground floor.
The doors slid open.
Dexter stepped out... he froze.
Outside, an incredibly beautiful woman was standing directly in front of the elevator, smiling at him.
She wore a fitted white blazer over a dark blouse and her posture was confident, and her smile was astonishingly striking to say the least.
The woman was Rachel...

chapters.title: Chapter 146 | Just Friends, Nothing Else...
paragraphs: Dexter blinked, momentarily caught off guard. "Rachel?"
Her smile widened briefly—then shifted into an exaggerated pout.
"Dexter," she said, her voice carrying a teasing edge. "You came to the Hero Association and didn’t inform me?" She placed a hand on her chest. "I’m slightly hurt by that."
Dexter scratched the back of his head awkwardly. "I wasn’t coming here for anything related to your department. I only came to receive my promotion. That’s why I didn’t visit."

Rachel’s pout softened into a genuine smile. "Yes, I heard about your feat. They said you fought alongside Aurora, Kinetic Man, and Bullet Spear Man during the outbreak." Her green eyes widened with interest. "It must have been quite the scene, right?"
Dexter nodded modestly. "It was quite all right. I only assisted a bit."
Rachel laughed softly, shaking her head. "Don’t be modest. I heard you saved more than ten heroes’ lives during the monster outbreak. You should be quite proud of yourself."
She fell into step beside him as they walked toward the main exit. The corridor was busy with heroes and staff moving between departments.
"Almost everyone is starting to learn about the hero who saves other heroes," she continued, her voice carrying a note of genuine admiration. "That’s quite the title, you know."
Dexter was quite stunned.
’The hero who saves other heroes?’
He hadn’t thought of it that way.
But the title was different than "the bastard son of the Ashford family" or "the man who married three cripples."
Dexter smiled faintly but said nothing.
They reached the main entrance. The massive glass doors slid open, letting in the afternoon sunlight and the distant sounds of the city.
A brief silence settled between them as they walked.
Rachel broke the silence first.
"So," she said, tilting her head slightly. "Where are you heading? Are you going home right now?"
Dexter nodded. "Yeah, I just need to pick up a couple of things at the mall before heading home."
Rachel’s green eyes brightened. "Why don’t I take you for lunch? I’m on my break anyway." She smiled warmly. "I know a restaurant nearby."
Dexter was stunned.
’Why do women feel the need to take me for lunch?’
He was supposed to be the one asking women for lunch. But now, for the second time, a woman was asking ’him’ out for a meal. First Violette, now Rachel.
Dexter shook his head. "No, I have quite a lot of things to do at home."
Rachel nodded, her smile dimming slightly. "Oh, your wives. How are they?" She forced a smile. "How are they? I hope the house renovation was up to their standards?"
Dexter nodded. "It’s holding quite all right."
He paused. He had been about to mention the cabinet incident—how the wall-mounted cabinet had nearly crushed Selene’s skull. But something stopped him.

If he told Rachel about the cabinet, she would immediately offer to inspect the house. She would use it as a reason to visit—citing safety concerns, Association protocols, or follow-up evaluations. And once she was inside the bungalow, Mira, Lyra, and Selene would not let it go.
The first time Rachel had visited, when she hugged him on the porch and mentioned their kiss at the hotel bar, the girls had nearly destroyed the living room.
A second visit would be worse. Especially now that the girls were cultivating again, their powers were growing, and their tolerance for perceived threats to their household had not improved.
And Rachel worked for the Hero Association.
So Dexter said nothing about the cabinet.
"The house is holding quite all right," he repeated. "The renovation was okay."
Rachel nodded. "All right."
She was quiet for a moment, then glanced at him sideways. "I’m assuming if I offer to drive you home, you would also decline."
Her tone was bitter, carrying an edge of accusation.
Dexter replied awkwardly. "I’m sorry about that, but I’m afraid I have to decline."
Then Rachel spoke again in a much quieter tone.
"So... am I really that difficult to be around?"
Dexter blinked. He turned to look at her. Her eyes were focused straight ahead, her jaw tight, her posture stiff.
The playful, confident woman who had greeted him at the elevator was gone, replaced by someone more vulnerable—someone who was genuinely asking.
"What?" Dexter said.

"Every time I offer to help, you politely refuse. Lunch, a ride, even a simple conversation." She sighed softly, the sound carrying a weight that surprised him. "It makes me wonder if I’m doing something wrong."
Dexter shook his head immediately. "You’re not."
"Then what is it?"

He scratched the back of his head awkwardly. The honest answer was complicated, and he wasn’t sure how to deliver it without sounding either arrogant or insulting. But something about Rachel’s expression—the genuine confusion and hurt in her eyes—made him choose honesty over deflection.
"Because I already have three wives waiting for me at home."
Rachel stared at him, her brow creasing. "What?"
Dexter continued, his voice measured but firm. "I don’t want to create misunderstandings."
"Misunderstandings?"
He nodded. Rachel was silent.

Dexter looked up at the sky. The afternoon sun hung high above the Association compound, casting long shadows across the polished courtyard. He watched a distant hero streak across the sky, leaving a faint trail of light.
"They’ve already been through enough," he said quietly. "The last thing I want is to make them feel insecure."
Rachel frowned. The silence between them stretched for several paces.
Then she spoke, her voice carrying a note of frustration.

"I just want to be friends," she said. "Simply friends with no strings attached. You’re a good person. You took in three strangers without complaining. Making you one of the rarest men out there with a good heart."
She sighed and continued. " I just want to be friends with a good person like you." She turned to face him, her green eyes earnest.
"How is that going to create a misunderstanding?"
Dexter frowned as he studied her face carefully, searching for any trace of hidden intent.
"Just friends?" he asked. "Nothing else?"
Rachel nodded her head confidently. "Yes. Just friends. Nothing else."

chapters.title: Chapter 147 | Friends & Purchases
paragraphs: "Friends?"
Dexter eyed her suspiciously. He had a feeling that Rachel’s interest wasn’t purely platonic and why was her cheeks a bit flushed?
But then again, he couldn’t control how others felt. He could only control his own actions.
"Okay," he said finally. "Just friends then."
Rachel’s face lit up with a brilliant smile. "All right, friend."
Then she blinked her eyes innocently. "Since we’re just friends, can I get your contact information?" She held up her phone.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
"My number?"
Rachel nodded naturally.
"Friends exchange phone numbers, don’t they? Besides, if anything changes within the Hero Association, I can let you know immediately. And... I can also ask how you’re doing every now and then."
Dexter looked at her.
Rachel puffed out her cheeks.
"It’s just your phone number."
He stared at her for another second before finally giving a helpless shrug.
"...Fine."
He recited his phone number. Rachel typed it into her device double-checking each digit before saving.
"Got it," she said, sliding her phone back into her blazer pocket. She looked up at him with a warm smile. "I’ll text you later, friend."
Dexter nodded. "Goodbye, Rachel."
"Goodbye, Dexter."
He turned and walked away to his car.
As Dexter exited the Hero Association’s main gate, the guards saluted him once more. He nodded rode out.
He didn’t head home immediately.

Instead, he pulled up his phone’s GPS and searched for the nearest commercial district. He needed to purchase renovation supplies like paint, tools, fixtures, and building materials. He also needed a few things too.
The GPS displayed a large shopping mall about ten minutes from the Association. Dexter set the route in his vehicle screen as he pressed the pedal.
As he drove, his phone buzzed.
He glanced at the screen.
’[New Message from: Rachel]’
> ’Hey, friend. Drive safe. 😊’
Dexter stared at the message for a long moment. Then he shook his head, pocketed the phone, and focused on the road.
He had lots of things to do, the last thing he needed was another complication.
But as he drove toward the mall, a small, involuntary smile tugged at the corner of his lips.
’Friends.’
He’d believe it when he saw it.
Dexter drove to one of the city’s largest commercial mall.
He parked the ordinary looking SUV in the parking lot.
Then as he entered he saw a few trolleys. He calculated then grabbed two of them.
Then he blinked his eyes, recalculated and then went to grab two more, making four and then began his shopping.
He started with the hardware section.

The house needed extensive work. Mira had cracked the bathroom wall tiles during her spectral arm mishap, so replacement tiles were first on the list. He selected premium ceramic tiles in a soft, neutral tone that would complement the bathroom’s existing color scheme.

From there, the list grew rapidly. He loaded the first trolley with multiple buckets of premium interior wall paint, warm cream for the living room, light gray for the bedrooms, and pure white for the ceilings. He also selected exterior weather-resistant paint in a clean, modern color for the outside walls.

To complete the painting work, he picked up paint rollers, brushes of various sizes, extension poles, paint trays, painter’s tape, protective plastic sheets, sandpaper, scrapers, a folding ladder, gloves, and safety goggles.

Since the wallpaper in several rooms had begun peeling with age, he selected several nice rolls of wallpaper with simple, modern patterns, clean, tasteful designs. He also grabbed wallpaper adhesive and trimming tools.

He moved to the electrical and plumbing section next. Replacement light bulbs, new electrical switches, new curtains, curtain rods, screws, nails, wall anchors, wood filler, silicone sealant, a heavy-duty drill set, screwdrivers, hammers, measuring tape, levels, wrenches, and replacement plumbing fittings all went into the second trolley.
For the backyard, he picked up several pieces of treated lumber to repair the old swing chair that Selene loved.
The chains were corroded, the wooden slats were splintering, and the frame itself was beginning to bow.
He also bought replacement chains, bolts, and weather-resistant wood stain.
Remembering the leaking kitchen roof, he purchased roofing sealant, replacement roofing sheets, insulation material, and waterproof coating.
Dexter sighed as he walked back to admire the various tools here. he washed he could take them all back home and test them and also figure out their uses!
Sadly he couldn’t afford to spend so much money.

The garden section was closed so he thought for a bit and picked up a few flower pots, bags of garden soil, and several flowering plants, marigolds, lavender, and a small hydrangea bush to make the front yard feel more welcoming. The bungalow’s exterior was dull and unwelcoming. A few plants wouldn’t transform it into a mansion, but they would at least make it look nice.
The third trolley was for necessities.
The massage oil he had been using on Mira was almost finished. He picked up two new bottles of premium grade massage oil, soothing, and can easily transmit mana from finger tips to the muscles.
Then his eyes caught something on a nearby shelf.
’Massage Glove 3000 Pro.’
Dexter picked up the box and read the description.
The glove was a device designed for deep tissue massage, with multiple intensity settings and vibration modes.

It claimed to be 300% more efficient than ordinary hands at penetrating deep into muscle tissue, stimulating blood flow, and accelerating nerve recovery. It was expensive—$8,000—but the potential benefit for Mira’s physical therapy was significant.
He added it to the trolley.
He also picked up extra electric toothbrushes, a new set for the girls and a replacement for himself.
He grabbed shaving cream and a high-quality shaving kit for his growing beard and mustache, which had begun to itch annoyingly.
’That should be all right?’
Dexter pondered and shrugged as he walked towards the checkout. But then, he passed the food section and he immediately thought of Lyra.
’I should probably get a few things for her.’

chapters.title: Chapter 148 | I’m Back!
paragraphs: ’I should probably get a few snacks for her.’
Dexter packed an assortment of snacks—chips, cookies, dried fruit, crackers, several tubs of premium ice cream in various flavors, and also, soda cans.
Lyra’s appetite was bottomless, and having quick snacks available would keep her satisfied between meals without requiring him to cook every time she got hungry.

The girls were all cultivating a Tier-7 technique now, which meant their bodies could process and expel impurities and excess calories through their cultivation. The energy of the Grand Cosmos Scripture would naturally cleanse their systems, so the junk food wouldn’t negatively affect their health or their figures. Dexter wasn’t worried about that.
He also picked up cooking ingredients for the bakery business, ordinary ingredients only. He was not going to use his precious Heavenly Treasures or Diamond Spirit Rice for commercial meals.
It would simply be an astronomical waste.
The meals he sold to customers would be made with standard, high-quality market ingredients, enhanced by his Great Grandmaster Foodsmith skills.
Even with ordinary ingredients, his cooking would produce Grade-One, Grade-Two meals or even Grade-three meals.
He purchased large quantities of vegetables, rice, cooking oil, spices, seasonings, and several large cooking pots for commercial-scale preparation.
By the time he was done, he had filled four trolleys to the brim.
He pushed all four to the checkout counter, where a bored clerk began scanning items.
The total appeared on the display.
Dexter paid with his phone, received the receipt, and then flipped his right hand.
Golden light flashed, and all four trolleys’ worth of items vanished into his storage ring in a flash.
"W-what?"
The cashier froze. Her scanner hovered mid-air over the last item. The couple behind Dexter in line was stunned.
A storage ring. was an artifact only high level heroes possess!
Which meant that the man in the plain dark shirt and joggers was also a high level hero!
Dexter ignored the stunned stares, pocketed his receipt, and walked out to the parking lot.
He pulled up his phone and searched for exotic beast meat suppliers. Then he selected one close by. It was a massive, warehouse-style establishment about fifteen minutes from the mall.
[Primordial Harvest: Exotic Beast Meat & Dungeon Resources]
Dexter drove there and arrived within twenty minutes. The building was enormous, it looked like a proper company instead of a butchers place.
He walked inside.
The inside was cold but clean and the place was painted stainless white too, looking eerily like an horror movie company.
Massive refrigerated display cases lined the walls, each one containing cuts of meat that ranged from ordinary-looking beef to flesh that glowed.
A receptionist who was a young man in a clean white coat greeted him from behind a polished counter.
"Welcome to Primordial Harvest. How can I assist you?"
"I want to buy Mutated Class beast meat," Dexter nodded and replied.
The receptionist nodded professionally. "Certainly, sir. We sell Mutated Class beast meat by the kilogram. Our current inventory ranges from Level 1 to Level 12, with prices scaling accordingly."
He pulled up a holographic catalog, displaying rows of available cuts with images, classifications, and prices.
Mutated Class Beast Meat (Standard Grade):
- Level 1 — $1,000/kg
- Level 2 — $2,000/kg
- Level 3 — $3,000/kg
Premium Mutated Class Beast Meat (Exceptional Nutrition/Rare Bloodline):
- Level 1 — $2,000/kg
- Level 2 — $4,000/kg

Dexter studied the prices as he calculated in his mind. Mutated Class beast meat was the most affordable tier—the meat of monsters from the lowest classification of dimensional gates. Even at these prices, it was still incredibly expensive compared to ordinary meat. A single kilogram of Level 1 meat cost as much as a month’s groceries for a normal family.
No wonder killing monsters and selling their corpses was the most lucrative business in the hero world. Well, apart from the Only Heroes website. (^o^)

Their bodies alone were worth fortunes. A single Level 3 goblin corpse—of which Dexter had killed dozens during the outbreak—would have been worth thousands in meat alone, not counting the nexus core.
"What about Fiend Class?" Dexter asked.
The receptionist smiled, clearly expecting the question. He scrolled to a different section of the catalog.
Fiend Class Beast Meat (Standard Grade):
- Level 1 — $3,000/kg
- Level 2 — $6,000/kg
- Level 3 — $9,000/kg
Fiend Class meat was three times more expensive than Mutated Class. The meat was denser, richer in mana, and possessed significantly greater nutritional and restorative properties.
Dexter made his selections quickly.

"Twenty kilograms of Level 1 Mutated Class Berserk Muscular Cow Meat," he said. The Berserk Muscular Cow was a common Mutated Class beast essentially a mutated bison with enhanced muscle density. Its meat was lean, protein-rich, and carried a mild mana signature that was easy to work with.

"Twenty kilograms of Level 1 Fiend Class Twin-Headed Turkey Meat," he added. The Twin-Headed Turkey was a Fiend Class creature whose meat was renowned for its restorative properties—particularly its ability to nourish damaged meridians and accelerate nerve regeneration.

This was for the girls. He had been feeding them ordinary market meat. If he incorporated Fiend Class meat into their daily meals, the grade of his cooking would increase significantly, and the nutritional benefits would accelerate their healing.
The receptionist processed the order.
20 kg × $1,000/kg = $20,000 (Mutated Class)
20 kg × $3,000/kg = $60,000 (Fiend Class)
Dexter felt a paid in his heart as he paid the money.
A year ago, that sum would have been more money than he had earned in his entire life combined. Now, it was an investment that would return a 100 fold.
He stored the meat in his spatial ring alongside the renovation supplies and walked out of Primordial Harvest.
’If I stayed in the market any longer, I might start buying things neither the girls nor I actually need,’
The drive back was uneventful.
He arrived at Fenmore Street twenty minutes later and parked the Vehicle in front of his bungalow. As he stepped out of the vehicle, his eyes caught movement across the street.
Tessa’s father, Henry, was also just returning home, carrying several large bags of flour on each shoulder with ease.
He had probably just returned from a supply run for the bakery.
The two men’s eyes met and Dexter nodded politely.
Henry returned the nod with a small smile. Then he turned and carried his flour bags inside the bakery.

Dexter wanted to actually walk over and discuss the food business, finalize the details, and coordinate the timeline for their trial run. But seeing the bags of flour and the fatigue on Henry’s face, he decided against interrupting him.
’Maybe later.’
Dexter opened the small gate and walked to up to the door.
The bungalow was quiet but he could hear Mira’s breathing from the living room, Lyra’s soft purring from the bedroom, and Selene’s breath from the backyard.
"I’m back!"

Their bodies alone were worth fortunes.
A single Level 3 goblin corpse—of which Dexter had killed dozens during the outbreak—would have been worth thousands in meat alone, not counting the nexus core.
"What about Fiend Class?" Dexter asked.
The receptionist smiled, clearly expecting the question.
He scrolled to a different section of the catalog.
Fiend Class Beast Meat (Standard Grade):
- Level 1 — $3,000/kg
- Level 2 — $6,000/kg
- Level 3 — $9,000/kg
Fiend Class meat was three times more expensive than Mutated Class.
The meat was denser, richer in mana, and possessed significantly greater nutritional and restorative properties.
Dexter made his selections quickly.
"Twenty kilograms of Level 1 Mutated Class Berserk Muscular Cow Meat," he said.
The Berserk Muscular Cow was a common Mutated Class beast essentially a mutated bison with enhanced muscle density.
Its meat was lean, protein-rich, and carried a mild mana signature that was easy to work with.
"Twenty kilograms of Level 1 Fiend Class Twin-Headed Turkey Meat," he added.
The Twin-Headed Turkey was a Fiend Class creature whose meat was renowned for its restorative properties—particularly its ability to nourish damaged meridians and accelerate nerve regeneration.
This was for the girls.
He had been feeding them ordinary market meat.
If he incorporated Fiend Class meat into their daily meals, the grade of his cooking would increase significantly, and the nutritional benefits would accelerate their healing.
The receptionist processed the order.
20 kg × $1,000/kg = $20,000 (Mutated Class)
20 kg × $3,000/kg = $60,000 (Fiend Class)
Dexter felt a paid in his heart as he paid the money.
A year ago, that sum would have been more money than he had earned in his entire life combined.
Now, it was an investment that would return a 100 fold.
He stored the meat in his spatial ring alongside the renovation supplies and walked out of Primordial Harvest.
’If I stayed in the market any longer, I might start buying things neither the girls nor I actually need,’
The drive back was uneventful.
He arrived at Fenmore Street twenty minutes later and parked the Vehicle in front of his bungalow.
As he stepped out of the vehicle, his eyes caught movement across the street.
Tessa’s father, Henry, was also just returning home, carrying several large bags of flour on each shoulder with ease.
He had probably just returned from a supply run for the bakery.
The two men’s eyes met and Dexter nodded politely.
Henry returned the nod with a small smile.
Then he turned and carried his flour bags inside the bakery.
Dexter wanted to actually walk over and discuss the food business, finalize the details, and coordinate the timeline for their trial run.
But seeing the bags of flour and the fatigue on Henry’s face, he decided against interrupting him.
’Maybe later.’
Dexter opened the small gate and walked to up to the door.
The bungalow was quiet but he could hear Mira’s breathing from the living room, Lyra’s soft purring from the bedroom, and Selene’s breath from the backyard.
"I’m back!"

chapters.title: Chapter 149 | Fixing The House
paragraphs: Mira was sitting in her wheelchair by the living room window, exactly where he had left her. Her head was tilted slightly toward the glass, her crimson eyes watching nothing in particular.
At the sound of his voice, she briefly glanced in his direction before closing her eyes again and returning to her own world without a single word.
Dexter shook his head slightly. ’Same as always.’
He walked further inside and found Lyra standing in the doorway of her room. Her AI smart glasses blinked slightly. The moment she saw him, her dark eyes brightened.
’You’re back.’
She said in his mind but she was looking at him with wide eyed and with an expectant gaze as her body leaned er body forward just a fraction, as though she were waiting for something.
Dexter understood what she meant but he simply smiled and said nothing.
He had indeed bought snacks of various varieties for her but he wasn’t going to give it to her just yet.
’Let her wait a little. It’ll make it sweeter.’
He turned away from Lyra’s hopeful stare and walked through the hallway toward the backyard to check up on Selene. He open the rear door, he found Selene.
Her silver-white hair hung loose over her shoulders as she sat on the swing cultivation with her palms on her laps and upwards.
She turned her head toward the sound and nodded slightly.
"Welcome back."
Dexter nodded. "Thanks."
before nodding once and heading back inside.

He walked to the storage room near the back of the house and began unloading everything he had purchased. One by one, he pulled each item from his spatial storage and arranged them neatly against the wall, cataloguing everything in his mind.
Then he got to work.
He started with the tiles.

The kitchen floor had several cracked and loose tiles that had been bothering him since the first day they moved in. He pried them up carefully, scraped away the old adhesive, and laid down fresh grout before pressing the new tiles into place one by one.

From the kitchen, he moved to the bathroom. The wall above the shower fixture had a section where the old tiles had completely fallen away, leaving an ugly patch of exposed concrete. He measured the gap, cut the replacement tiles to size, and fitted them snugly into the wall. He grouted the seams, wiped away the excess, and stepped back to inspect his work.
It was clean and looked professional.

Dexter wasn’t a trained contractor, but he was no stranger to manual labor. Growing up in the Ashford estate as little more than a servant, he had been forced to perform nearly every odd job imaginable. Serving food, washing floors, scrubbing dishes, mending fences, repairing roofs and yes, construction work.
Whenever something in the estate needed fixing, the Head Servants pocket the money to call professionals and give the job to the servants to fix instead.

Over the years, he had learned to work with his hands out of pure necessity and that experience had made him versatile. Tiling, painting, carpentry, basic plumbing — he could do all of it. Not perfectly, but well enough.

After finishing the bathroom, he moved on to the wallpaper. He carefully stripped the damaged sections, applied fresh adhesive, and pressed the new wallpaper flat against the walls, smoothing out every air bubble with a clean cloth. Then he moved to the bedroom and repeated the process.
Once the wallpaper was done, he opened the cans of paint. A soft, warm white for the kitchen to make the small space feel brighter. A light grey for the bathroom.
Slowly, the rooms began to transform, becoming neater and cleaner.
Just like that, two hours passed.
"Riiiiing!"
Dexter checked his phone.
[Alarm; Make lunch for ’Wives?’]
Dexter set down the paint roller and wiped his hands on a rag. It was time to make lunch.

He washed up in the backyard tap, changed into a clean shirt, and walked into the kitchen. Lyra was already there. She had followed him from the moment he entered the kitchen and now sat on a small stool near the counter, watching him with sharp, unblinking eyes.
Dexter glanced at her. "You’re going to watch me the entire time?"
She nodded without a shred of shame.
He sighed and pulled out the ingredients.
Today’s lunch was going to be special.
Fiend-Class meat was rich in mana and possessed a naturally savory, deeply complex flavor that ordinary beef or pork could never match.

Dexter seasoned the meat carefully, using a blend of herbs and spices then seared it in the Type-II Cooking Pot until the surface caramelized beautifully, then reduced the heat and let it simmer in its own juices alongside fresh vegetables and a portion of Diamond Rice.
The kitchen filled with an incredible aroma and the smell was so intense that even Mira, sitting in the living room with her eyes closed, unconsciously turned her head toward the kitchen.
Dexter plated the meals. Four bowls of steaming rice, each topped with thick slices of the seared Fiend-Class meat and a ladle of the rich cooking broth.
He paused, studying the food carefully.
[Grade 4 Meal]
He had expected the Fiend-Class meat to push the meal’s grade higher. Perhaps even to Grade Five. If it had reached Grade Five, then there might have been tribulation lightning.
But nothing happened.
Dexter blinked in mild disappointment, then simply shrugged.
’Grade Four is still excellent. I’ll try again another time.’
He carried the bowls to the dining table and called the girls.
They gathered quickly. Lyra was already in her seat before Dexter had finished setting the last bowl down.
Mira wheeled herself to the table with the help of her Spectral Arms, Selene walked in last.
Then they all ate in silence.
Lyra of course was intensely focused on her food.
Selene ate slowly but somehow consumed the meal quickly as her pale face has a tint of red in them.
And, Mira was also eating speedily despite the fact that she was using her spectral arm.
Dexter watched them from across the table, a quiet pride swelling in his chest. As a cook, there was no greater compliment than seeing someone lose themselves entirely in a meal he had prepared.
"I have something to tell you," Dexter said.
Mira eyed him while Selene tilted her head upwards and Lyra continued focusing on her food.

"I’ve arranged a business partnership with Tessa and her father," Dexter said. "They own the bakery on the corner. I’ll be preparing a few portions of my meals each day, and they’ll sell them at the bakery on a trial basis."
He paused.
"If it sells, great. If it doesn’t, then that’s it for my plan."
The room was quiet for a moment.
Then Lyra’s brows furrowed as she pouted.
’You want to cook for other people?’
Dexter smiled.
"Not particularly. I’m exchanging my services for money. Selling Enchanted Meals is a lucrative business, Lyra. And since I can cook, I decided to try it."
Lyra’s blinked her eyes as her deepened and she focused in her food but she was slower this time.
Mira, on the other hand spoke in her usual flat tone.
"Do what you want."
Selene nodded slowly. "That’s a nice idea, Dexter. I’m sure you’ll do well."
Dexter smiled. "Thank you, Selene."
The girls gradually dispersed after their meal.
But Lyra remained in the kitchen doorway, her arms crossed, her pout still firmly in place.
Dexter looked at her then, with a flick of his wrist, a bag of snack materialized in his hands.
Lyra’s eyes widened and the pout vanished instantly as her hands shot forward with speed.
Then she looked up at him, and for the briefest moment, a faint smile tugged at the corner of her lips.
’Thank you Dexter. Good luck on your business.’
Then she turned and hurried toward the living room couch, already tearing open the bag of chips before she even sat down.
Dexter watched her go, shaking his head with a quiet chuckle.
’That girl and her food.’

chapters.title: Chapter 150 | Deep Tissue Massage
paragraphs: After finishing the dishes, Dexter dried his hands and walked into the living room, directly towards Mira. He stopped behind her wheelchair and unlocked the brakes.
Mira’s eyes snapped open. She turned her head and glared at him with slight irritation.
"I’m beginning to think you look forward to this every day."
Dexter snorted lightly. "I’ve touched better."
Mira glare intensified as she her eyes narrowed into a dangerous slit. "What are you trying to say."
Dexter blinked his eyes and sneered. "You know what I mean, brat."
Mira clenched her teeth. "I’m older than you..."
Dexter shrugged. "Yet you act like a naughty kid."
Her eyes were practically blazing with flames as she huffed and stared at Dexter.
Dexter had long since grown immune to her death glares. He gripped the handles of her wheelchair and steered her away from the window and into her bedroom.
He parked the wheelchair beside the bed, then carefully lifted her in his arms and gently lowered onto the center of the mattress, then reached into his spatial storage.
He brought out the new massage oil today and also the a specialized massaging glove.
The glove was incredibly thin and flexible. When he wore it, they fit snugly over his hands.
The glove had multiple vibration settings, At its lowest setting, it produced a gentle hum barely stronger than a phone’s notification.
At its highest, it could deliver deep, penetrating vibrations that reached all the way to the bone.
Combined with his Tier-2 36 Styles Massage Technique, the glove would immediately amplify the effectiveness of the massage.
Dexter reached for the hem of Mira’s shirt, lifted her torso just enough to pull the shirt over her head, then removed her skirt, leaving her in a plain sports bra and sport briefs.

Her skin was pale and smooth, almost looking as though it hadn’t been in the sun at all. Afterwards, he positioned her face-down on the bed with her arms resting at her sides and her face turned to one side against the pillow.
He poured a measure of warm massage oil into his palm and then he began, starting with her shoulders.
Since he was using it for the first time, he set the gloves to its lowest vibration, pressing his oiled fingers into the dense muscle where her neck met her shoulders.
Activating the 36 Styles Technique, mana surged through his finger tips as he followed the pattern of the technique.
At first, the vibration was so subtle that Mira wasnt able to feel it.
Seeing that she wasn’t complaining, Dexter gradually increased the intensity.
The humming grew a bit louder as the vibrations penetrated deeper into her tissue.
At that moment, Mira felt something and her eyes immediately flew open as she muttered.
"What are you doing?" she muttered.
Dexter didn’t look at her and continued with his work.
"I bought a massaging glove. It increases the effectiveness of the massage by roughly 300 percent."
He paused, then added without thinking, "You’ll feel more comfortable and relaxed than before."
The tips of Mira’s ears turned a faint shade of pink.
But Dexter noticed it and he blinked.
’Her blood circulation is certainly improving.’
His hands moved from her shoulders down to her upper back. As he worked the muscles along her spine, her shoulder blades and her lower back.
Mana seeped into every section, stimulating weakened nerves while gently encouraging circulation throughout her body.
He moved to her neck and cradled her head gently in one hand and worked the muscles at the base of her skull with the other.

These were the most sensitive areas, the ones closest to the site of her spinal injury. He increased the vibration slightly and channeled a thin thread of mana through his fingertips, letting it seep into the damaged nerve endings.
Dexter continued down her spine.
From the middle of her back, he carefully worked lower before returning to the muscles surrounding her waist, making sure not to apply unnecessary force directly onto the spine itself.
Without realizing it, Mira’s breathing had become quieter than before.
He worked vertebra by vertebra, pressing and rolling and vibrating the muscles on either side of her spinal column.
The 36 Styles Technique guided his mana into the damaged pathways, gently coaxing the severed nerve endings to remember what it felt like to carry a signal.

He reached the dimples at the base of her spine, where her lower back met her hips. He pressed deep, using the heel of his palm combined with the glove’s vibration to work the thick muscle tissue there.
Once he finished with her back, Dexter moved to her arms.
He stretched each finger individually before working through her palms, wrists, forearms, elbows, and upper arms, ensuring every muscle received equal attention.
Only after finishing both arms did he continue to her legs.

Beginning with her feet, he gently massaged each toe before moving across the soles of her feet. The vibration from the glove combined with the flowing mana to relax muscles that had remained inactive for years.
Slowly, he worked upward through her calves before reaching her thighs, then her upper thigh as the gloves vibrated, hitting deep within her tissue.
Mira unconsciously let out a soft breath.
Dexter frowned slightly.
"Too much vibration?"
Taking that as confirmation, he continued until both legs had been thoroughly treated.
Finally, he wiped away the excess massage oil with a warm towel before carefully helping Mira turn onto her back.
The moment she faced him, Dexter blinked.
Her cheeks were completely red.
Even the tips of her ears and her neck had turned a noticeable shade of crimson.
She stared directly at him.
Dexter tilted his head in confusion.
"What’s wrong?" he asked, his brow furrowing with concern. "Are you running a fever? Your face is completely red."
Mira’s glare intensified.
"You’re asking ’me’ if something is wrong?" she hissed through clenched teeth.
Dexter blinked. "Yes? Because your face is—"
"Nothing. Just continue."
